title: A 62-year-old heavy smoker develops hypercortisolism over a few months with marked hypokalaemia and a high ACTH. What is the most likely source?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 62-year-old heavy smoker develops hypercortisolism over a few months with marked hypokalaemia and a high ACTH. What is the most likely source?
options: Ectopic ACTH from a small cell lung carcinoma
body.explanation: High ACTH means an ACTH-dependent cause. Besides a pituitary adenoma, ACTH can come from an ectopic tumour, such as small cell lung carcinoma or a neuroendocrine tumour. Adrenal tumours and exogenous steroids give a low ACTH.
option_notes: Smoker, fast onset, marked hypokalaemia, high ACTH: ectopic ACTH.
An adrenal adenoma gives a low ACTH.
Exogenous steroids give a low ACTH.
Adrenal carcinoma gives a low ACTH.

title: Hypercortisolism is defined as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hypercortisolism is defined as:
options: All clinical and biological signs of a chronic glucocorticoid excess
A brief, transient rise in cortisol during an acute stress such as surgery
A chronic excess of mineralocorticoids with hypertension and low potassium
body.explanation: Definition: all the clinical and biological manifestations caused by a chronic excess of glucocorticoids; adrenal hypercortisolism is called Cushing's syndrome.

title: Haemolysis tests listed in the jaundice workup include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Haemolysis tests listed in the jaundice workup include:
body.explanation: Haemolysis tests: LDH, haptoglobin, Coombs tests, haemoglobin electrophoresis.

title: Cough during meals and nasal regurgitation suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cough during meals and nasal regurgitation suggest:
body.explanation: Neurological, muscular or ENT causes.
option_notes: A stricture gives retrosternal sticking of solids.
Cough and nasal regurgitation mean a pharyngeal problem.

title: Which stimuli can trigger vomiting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which stimuli can trigger vomiting?
options: Chemoreceptor trigger zone stimulation by drugs or toxins
body.explanation: Four triggers: gastrointestinal irritation, vestibular disturbances, higher cortical centre stimulation and CTZ stimulation by drugs or toxins.

title: Causes of primary adrenal insufficiency include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of primary adrenal insufficiency include:
body.explanation: Primary AI: Addison's disease (anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies), adrenal tuberculosis, and other causes: haemorrhage, metastasis, infection.

title: Laboratory tests and what they look for in constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Laboratory tests and what they look for in constipation:
body.explanation: CBC for anemia/infection, thyroid tests for hypothyroidism, electrolytes for hypercalcemia/hypokalemia, glucose for diabetes.
option_notes: Wrong: thyroid tests look for hypothyroidism; electrolytes detect hypercalcemia.
Wrong: blood glucose screens for diabetes.

title: Physiological causes of hyperprolactinaemia include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Physiological causes of hyperprolactinaemia include:
body.explanation: The physiologic column of the table lists pregnancy, nursing, nipple stimulation, exercise, stress, sleep and seizures.

title: Associated symptoms to ask about in jaundice include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Associated symptoms to ask about in jaundice include:
body.explanation: Associated: fever, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, GI bleeding, diarrhoea, neurological symptoms, weight loss, joint pain.

title: The dermatological exam in jaundice also looks for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The dermatological exam in jaundice also looks for:
body.explanation: Listed: pruritus lesions, purpura, ecchymoses, tattoos, among others.

title: Secondary (organic) constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Secondary (organic) constipation:
options: Is diagnosed mainly by anorectal manometry
Is mainly due to colonic inertia or spastic colon
body.explanation: Secondary/organic constipation results from an identifiable structural, biochemical or medical condition.
option_notes: Correct: structural, biochemical or medical condition.
Wrong: manometry is a functional test for primary constipation.
Wrong: colonic inertia is a primary cause.

title: Total bilirubin in a jaundiced patient may be:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Total bilirubin in a jaundiced patient may be:
body.explanation: Increased total bilirubin: conjugated or unconjugated or both.

title: When is surgery indicated in GI bleeding?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When is surgery indicated in GI bleeding?
body.explanation: Endoscopic haemostasis comes first; surgery is for refractory bleeding or perforation.
option_notes: Surgery when endoscopy fails or there is perforation.
Most ulcer bleeds are treated endoscopically.
Haemorrhoids do not need surgery for a first bleed.

title: Endocrine and metabolic causes of secondary constipation listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Endocrine and metabolic causes of secondary constipation listed in the lecture include:
body.explanation: Endocrine/metabolic: hypothyroidism, diabetes mellitus, hypercalcemia, hypokalemia, chronic kidney disease.
option_notes: Wrong: it is hypothyroidism that is listed.
Wrong: it is hypercalcemia that is listed.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Prolonged diarrhoea. 2 to 4 weeks; post-infectious or parasitic.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Prolonged: 2 to 4 weeks.
Another box. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.
Another box. Definition box: over 300 g/day, over 3 stools a day, over 90% water.

title: On the coronary artery disease figure:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the coronary artery disease figure:
options: Four stages are shown, from healthy artery to near complete blockage
Initial fatty deposits are shown before plaque that obstructs blood flow
The most advanced stage shown is near complete blockage
The most advanced stage shown is complete occlusion by a thrombus
The healthy artery already shows fatty deposits in its wall
body.explanation: Stages pictured in order: healthy artery, initial fatty deposits, plaque obstructs blood flow, near complete blockage.
option_notes: Fatty deposits come second, obstructing plaque third.
No complete occlusion or thrombus is shown.
The healthy artery has no deposits.

title: The laboratory assessment of diabetic nephropathy includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The laboratory assessment of diabetic nephropathy includes:
options: Albumin-to-creatinine ratio on an early morning spot urine
body.explanation: Assessment: 24-h urine, ACR on early morning spot urine (a urine test), serum creatinine and GFR (eGFR is a blood test).

title: Lymphadenopathy found in a vomiting patient suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Lymphadenopathy found in a vomiting patient suggests:
body.explanation: Lymphadenopathy suggests infection or malignancy.
option_notes: Wrong: suggested by headache and papilledema.
Wrong: suggested by absent bowel sounds.

title: Why can type 1 diabetes appear abruptly in a previously well young person?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why can type 1 diabetes appear abruptly in a previously well young person?
options: Symptoms appear only after about 90% of beta cells are destroyed
Insulin resistance develops in a few days
The pancreas is removed by autoantibodies at once
Glucose stops being filtered by the kidney
body.explanation: The autoimmune destruction is silent for a long time; diabetes becomes apparent after about 90% of the beta cells have been destroyed.
option_notes: Symptoms appear once about 90% of beta cells are destroyed.
Beta-cell destruction is slow and silent.

title: Which sputum occurs in pulmonary oedema?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which sputum occurs in pulmonary oedema?
body.explanation: Coughing up blood or bloody froth is a symptom of pulmonary oedema.
option_notes: Fluid and red cells leaking into the alveoli give pink froth.
Chocolate pus suggests an amoebic abscess.

title: Hepatocellular injury with ALT > AST leads, on the chart, to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hepatocellular injury with ALT > AST leads, on the chart, to:
body.explanation: ALT > AST next steps: viral serology, ANA & ASMA, AMA, transferrins, alpha-1 antitrypsin.

title: A 20-year-old has mild jaundice when fasting or ill. Bilirubin is unconjugated, liver tests are normal and there is no haemolysis. What is the most likely caus…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 20-year-old has mild jaundice when fasting or ill. Bilirubin is unconjugated, liver tests are normal and there is no haemolysis. What is the most likely cause?
body.explanation: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia without haemolysis points to a conjugation defect such as Gilbert syndrome (Crigler-Najjar is the rare, severe form).
option_notes: Unconjugated, intermittent, normal liver tests, no haemolysis.

title: The medical history of a jaundiced patient covers:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The medical history of a jaundiced patient covers:
body.explanation: History: age, sex, occupation, chronic liver disease, surgery, autoimmune disease, viral risk factors, travel, lifestyle, medications, family history.
option_notes: Not a history item on slide 17.

title: About the oesophagus on physical examination:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the oesophagus on physical examination:
options: It is palpated in the left supraclavicular fossa
It is not accessible to examination
It is assessed by epigastric percussion
It is felt by deep palpation under the left ribs
body.explanation: The slide states the oesophagus is not accessible to examination (one may only look for a cervical mass).
option_notes: That site is for lymph nodes.
Not accessible; that is spleen palpation.

title: About vomiting (emesis):
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About vomiting (emesis):
options: It is a passive return of gastric contents
It is the forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth
It is always preceded by nausea
It involves violent cyclic contractions of the abdominal muscles, diaphragm and respiratory muscles
body.explanation: Vomiting is the forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth, usually preceded by nausea; an active mechanism of violent cyclic contractions of the abdominal, diaphragmatic and respiratory muscles.
option_notes: Wrong: it is an active mechanism.

title: Where is tracheal breathing heard?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where is tracheal breathing heard?
body.explanation: Tracheal breathing: very loud, over the neck. Bronchial breathing: loud, high-pitched, over the sternum.
option_notes: Tracheal breathing is heard over the neck.

title: What does MIBG scintigraphy evaluate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does MIBG scintigraphy evaluate?
body.explanation: MIBG scintigraphy is a functional test of the adrenal medulla and paragangliomas.
option_notes: MIBG is taken up by catecholamine-producing tissue (adrenal medulla, paragangliomas).
Thyroid nodules are explored with thyroid scintigraphy.
Bone metastases are explored with bone scintigraphy.
Kidney function is not explored by MIBG.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Typical symptoms. Pyrosis (retrosternal burning rising to the throat) and regurgitation.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: The optic-chiasmatic syndrome is caused by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The optic-chiasmatic syndrome is caused by:
options: Downward extension into the sphenoid sinus
Lateral extension into the cavernous sinus
body.explanation: Suprasellar extension of the pituitary adenoma compresses the optic chiasm, giving the optic-chiasmatic syndrome.
option_notes: Wrong: the chiasm lies above the gland.
Wrong: this gives cranial nerve palsies (diplopia, ptosis).
Wrong: not a mass effect mechanism.

title: About the setting of the digestive examination:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the setting of the digestive examination:
options: Patient lying flat on a bed
Doctor standing on the patient's left side
body.explanation: The slide asks for an intimate, calm environment, the patient lying flat on a bed and the doctor on the patient's right side.
option_notes: The doctor stands on the right side.
Patient lies flat on a bed.

title: What does jugular venous distension evaluate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does jugular venous distension evaluate?
body.explanation: It evaluates right heart function and central venous pressure; it is not a sign of dehydration.
option_notes: The JVP reflects right heart filling pressure.
It is not a test of hydration.

title: What is odynophagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is odynophagia?
body.explanation: Odynophagia: painful swallowing. Aphagia: complete inability. Globus: lump sensation without true difficulty.

title: Which substance relaxes vascular smooth muscle?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which substance relaxes vascular smooth muscle?
body.explanation: Endothelial nitric oxide relaxes smooth muscle; endothelin-1, angiotensin II and thromboxane A2 constrict it.

title: At diagnosis, what does the examination include?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: At diagnosis, what does the examination include?
body.explanation: Capillary glucose, glycosuria, dehydration, BMI, infectious signs and a search for complications.
option_notes: Capillary glucose is part of the examination.
Weight, height and BMI are recorded.
Dehydration and infection are looked for.
Thyroid scintigraphy is not part of it.

title: Late postprandial vomiting may suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Late postprandial vomiting may suggest:
options: A psychogenic cause such as stress
body.explanation: Late postprandial vomiting may suggest a duodenal or pyloric obstruction.
option_notes: Wrong: that is vomiting during meals.
Wrong: not linked to timing on the slide.

title: A woman has hot, sweaty skin, heat intolerance and weight loss despite eating more. Which mechanism explains the weight loss?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A woman has hot, sweaty skin, heat intolerance and weight loss despite eating more. Which mechanism explains the weight loss?
options: Increased metabolism with lipolysis and protein catabolism
Loss of fluid in the urine
body.explanation: Thyroid hormones increase metabolism: lipolysis and protein catabolism explain weight loss despite polyphagia.
option_notes: Urine loss is not the mechanism.

title: On the risk-factor wheels, factors shown for macrovascular but NOT for microvascular complications include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the risk-factor wheels, factors shown for macrovascular but NOT for microvascular complications include:
body.explanation: The microvascular wheel shows only glucose, BP and genetics; the macrovascular wheel adds lipids, smoking, insulin resistance, obesity and inflammation.

title: LH/FSH deficiency produces:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: LH/FSH deficiency produces:
options: In women, oligo/amenorrhoea with anovulatory cycles
In men, erectile dysfunction, low libido and testicular atrophy
body.explanation: Table: women - oligo/amenorrhoea, anovulation, loss of axillary/pubic hair, osteoporosis; men - ED, low libido, testicular atrophy, loss of sexual hair, osteoporosis.
option_notes: Sexual hair is lost, not increased.

title: What confirms the cause of a pleurisy?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What confirms the cause of a pleurisy?
body.explanation: Pleural biopsy or thoracoscopy confirm the aetiology.
option_notes: The X-ray shows the effusion, not its cause.
Fremitus is a sign, not a cause.
Biopsy gives tissue for the cause.

title: A cholestatic pattern (raised ALP and GGT) on the chart may be due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A cholestatic pattern (raised ALP and GGT) on the chart may be due to:
body.explanation: Cholestasis possible diagnoses: choledocholithiasis, PSC, obstructing tumours, any liver disease, pregnancy.

title: What is the normal adult respiratory rate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the normal adult respiratory rate?
body.explanation: Adults 12 to 20; infants and neonates 30 to 60. Polypnoea over 20; bradypnoea under 12.
option_notes: Adults breathe 12 to 20 times a minute.

title: Causes of upper GI bleeding include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of upper GI bleeding include:
body.explanation: Upper GI causes: peptic ulcer, oesophageal/gastric varices, Mallory-Weiss tear, erosive gastritis or duodenitis, gastric or oesophageal cancer, stress ulcers, drug-induced lesions.
option_notes: Wrong: haemorrhoids are an anal (lower) cause.

title: Which are signs of hypercortisolism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are signs of hypercortisolism?
body.explanation: Moon face, purple striae, truncal obesity, hypertension.
option_notes: Cortisol excess causes hypertension, not hypotension.

title: Why does a person with uncontrolled diabetes lose weight while eating more?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why does a person with uncontrolled diabetes lose weight while eating more?
options: Without insulin the cells behave as if fasting, so fat is broken down and hunger rises
Food is not absorbed by the gut
body.explanation: A defect of insulin leads to lipolysis: the cells are in a 'fasting state', so weight drops and polyphagia appears as compensation.
option_notes: Lipolysis from the 'fasting' cells, with compensatory hunger.

title: Which is a cause of dysentery?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cause of dysentery?
body.explanation: Causes: colorectal cancer and polyps, IBD, infectious proctitis, radiation and ischaemic colitis.
option_notes: Hepatitis A does not cause bloody stools.
Ulcerative colitis inflames the rectum and colon.

title: Complications of Cushing syndrome include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Complications of Cushing syndrome include:
body.explanation: Complications: diabetes, dyslipidaemia (high TC, high TG), hyperuricaemia; hypertension with LVH and retinopathy; bacterial, viral and mycotic infections; thromboembolism.

title: Which causes a nocturnal cough?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which causes a nocturnal cough?
body.explanation: Nocturnal: GERD, asthma. Morning bronchial cleansing: bronchiectasis, chronic bronchitis.
option_notes: Chronic bronchitis gives a morning cough.
Pneumothorax gives sudden cough and pain.
Lying down favours reflux and asthma attacks at night.

title: What is Zenker's diverticulum?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is Zenker's diverticulum?
body.explanation: A structural ENT cause, a pulsion diverticulum, shown by barium swallow.
option_notes: The pharyngeal wall bulges out under pressure.

title: The take-home messages state that:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The take-home messages state that:
options: Jaundice is always due to liver disease
It can be a symptom of haematological or genetic disease
Physiology of bilirubin is key to aetiological reasoning
Separating cholestatic from non-cholestatic is the first step
body.explanation: Jaundice is usually liver/biliary but can be haematological or genetic; bilirubin physiology guides reasoning; cholestatic vs non-cholestatic is step one.

title: What does angina pectoris mean in Latin?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does angina pectoris mean in Latin?
body.explanation: From Latin for strangling of the chest: chest pain from myocardial ischaemia.
option_notes: Angina means strangling; pectoris means of the chest.
This is not the literal meaning.
This is not the literal meaning.
Death of heart muscle is infarction.

title: In a prolactinoma, mass effect occurs with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a prolactinoma, mass effect occurs with:
body.explanation: The slide says mass effects occur with macroadenomas only.
option_notes: Microadenomas are too small to compress nearby structures.
Microadenomas do not cause mass effect.

title: What does a clear-liquid vomica suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does a clear-liquid vomica suggest?
body.explanation: Clear liquid: hydatid cyst. Pus: abscess. Pus with bile: liver abscess with bronchial fistula. Chocolate pus: amoebic abscess.
option_notes: A liver abscess gives pus with bile.
A ruptured hydatid cyst releases clear fluid.

title: In the 'Main symptoms of diabetes' figure, the urinary signs shown are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the 'Main symptoms of diabetes' figure, the urinary signs shown are:
body.explanation: The urinary box lists polyuria and glycosuria.

title: On the jaundice strategy chart, corpuscular haemolysis (a red cell defect) is usually:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the jaundice strategy chart, corpuscular haemolysis (a red cell defect) is usually:
body.explanation: The chart splits haemolysis into corpuscular, usually extravascular, and extracorpuscular, usually intravascular.
option_notes: Duct dilatation belongs to cholestatic jaundice.

title: In the classification of hypoglycaemia:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the classification of hypoglycaemia:
options: Level 3 is defined by a glucose below 40 mg/dL
Level 1 by definition requires injectable glucagon
body.explanation: Level 1 <= 70 mg/dL (treat with fast-acting carbohydrate, adjust therapy); level 2 < 54 mg/dL; level 3 has no specific glucose threshold.
option_notes: Level 3 has no specific glucose threshold.
Level 1 is treated with fast-acting carbohydrate and dose adjustment.

title: In the type 1 diabetes figure, blood glucose rises because:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the type 1 diabetes figure, blood glucose rises because:
options: No insulin is made, so glucose cannot enter cells
The pancreas secretes excess but inactive insulin
Glucose absorption from the intestine is increased
The kidney reabsorbs more glucose than normal
body.explanation: Figure: the body destroys the beta cells, no insulin is produced, glucose cannot move into the cells and blood glucose rises.
option_notes: Correct: insulin acts as the key letting glucose in.
Wrong: shown in the type 2 figure, not type 1.

title: A 45-year-old's blurred vision and tingling feet lead to two fasting glucose values of 1.40 g/L. What do the symptoms tell you?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 45-year-old's blurred vision and tingling feet lead to two fasting glucose values of 1.40 g/L. What do the symptoms tell you?
options: They are symptoms that can reveal diabetes
body.explanation: Blurred vision and paresthesia are among the symptoms that can reveal diabetes; two fasting values ≥ 1.26 g/L confirm it.
option_notes: Two high fasting values confirm diabetes.
The type is decided on other features.

title: A 26-year-old woman has infrequent stools with abdominal discomfort, bloating and cramps that worsen with exam stress. Tests are normal. What fits best?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 26-year-old woman has infrequent stools with abdominal discomfort, bloating and cramps that worsen with exam stress. Tests are normal. What fits best?
body.explanation: IBS-C: abdominal discomfort, infrequent stools, bloating and cramping with no organic disease; stress can worsen it.
option_notes: Discomfort, bloating, stress and normal tests fit IBS-C.
No red flags and normal tests.
Anismus causes difficult evacuation, not pain-led symptoms.

title: At Hb 10 g/dL, when does cyanosis appear?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: At Hb 10 g/dL, when does cyanosis appear?
body.explanation: The lower the Hb, the lower the saturation needed; cyanosis in a severely anaemic patient means critical illness.
option_notes: With less Hb, saturation must fall lower before cyanosis shows.
Normal saturation does not cause cyanosis.
Too high for an anaemic patient.

title: Microvascular complications of diabetes are manifested mainly by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Microvascular complications of diabetes are manifested mainly by:
options: Thickening of the capillary basement membrane
Plaque formation in the coronary arteries
body.explanation: Microvascular disease of capillaries and precapillary arterioles is manifested mainly by thickening of the capillary basement membrane.

title: Charcot arthropathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Charcot arthropathy:
options: Occurs with severe neuropathy and long-standing diabetes
Is initiated by an injury causing a bone fracture
Leads to gross deformity with a cubic foot
Is caused by arterial occlusion with dry gangrene
body.explanation: Charcot: severe neuropathy, long-standing diabetes, initiating injury with fracture, gross deformity, cubic foot, acute Charcot foot.
option_notes: Not the mechanism on the slide.

title: According to the lecture summary:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture summary:
options: 20-60% of adults have thyroid nodules, usually under 1 cm
Thyroid ultrasound is expensive and rarely informative
The family history and radiation exposure are irrelevant for a thyroid lump
body.explanation: Summary: 20-60% of adults have nodules (usually <1 cm); ultrasound is accessible, cheap and informative; Hashimoto is very common. Lump work-up includes family history and radiation exposure.
option_notes: Correct: Hashimoto thyroiditis is very common.
Wrong: accessible, cheap and gives important information.
Wrong: both must be carefully evaluated.

title: What is the first-line exam for upper GI bleeding?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the first-line exam for upper GI bleeding?
body.explanation: EGD after stabilisation finds the source in over 90 percent and can treat it.
option_notes: The first-line test, after stabilisation; it can also treat.
Colonoscopy is for lower GI bleeding.
Capsule endoscopy is for small-bowel bleeding when other tests are negative.
CT is not first-line for upper bleeding.

title: Which bacteria does stool culture identify?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which bacteria does stool culture identify?
body.explanation: Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter and E. coli.
option_notes: Streptococcus is not an enteric pathogen.
S. aureus gives toxin food poisoning, not dysentery.
Shigella and Salmonella are typical invasive enteric bacteria.
Mycobacteria are not found on routine stool culture.

title: Regarding functional tests in constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding functional tests in constipation:
options: They are requested based on the clinical context
They are indicated when primary constipation is suspected
They are the first tests to rule out organic disease
body.explanation: Functional tests are requested by clinical context if primary constipation is suspected: colonic transit studies, defecography, anorectal manometry.
option_notes: Wrong: colonoscopy is an initial test to rule out organic disease.
Wrong: organic disease is ruled out by initial tests (endoscopy, imaging, labs).

title: Which are added sounds? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are added sounds? (choose all)
body.explanation: Added: wheeze, rhonchi, crackles, rub, stridor. Vesicular and tracheal breathing are normal sounds.

title: What is a normal ejection fraction?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is a normal ejection fraction?
body.explanation: Normal about 64 to 70 percent; 40 to 50 is borderline; 40 percent or less is systolic failure.

title: Endoscopic findings listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Endoscopic findings listed in the lecture include:
options: Signs of chronic GERD or Barrett's oesophagus
body.explanation: Findings: ulcers, erosions, masses, signs of chronic GERD or Barrett's oesophagus. Gallstones are seen on ultrasound.

title: What liver is soft, smooth and painful?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What liver is soft, smooth and painful?
body.explanation: Cardiac: diffuse enlargement, soft to firm, regular border, smooth, painful.
option_notes: The cirrhotic liver is hard and painless.
Storage diseases give a firm, painless liver.
Metastases give a hard, nodular liver.
Congestion stretches the capsule: soft, smooth and painful.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Oropharyngeal dysphagia. Difficulty starting the swallow, cough, nasal regurgitation; neurological, muscular or ENT causes.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Oropharyngeal: hard to start the swallow, cough, nasal regurgitation.
Another box. Oesophageal phase: involuntary peristalsis.
Another box. Motor: liquids as much as solids (paradoxical).

title: Psychogenic causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Psychogenic causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Psychogenic: anxiety or stress-related vomiting; eating disorders (bulimia). Migraine and vestibular disorders are neurological.

title: Which are red flags in dysphagia? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are red flags in dysphagia? (choose all)
body.explanation: Age over 50, rapid progression, weight loss over 5 kg, anaemia, caustic or radiation history.
option_notes: Age over 50 raises the cancer risk.
Anaemia can reveal a bleeding tumour.
Globus is not a red flag.

title: Why do pregnant women often get heartburn?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why do pregnant women often get heartburn?
options: Raised intra-abdominal pressure, and progesterone lowers LES tone
body.explanation: Obesity and pregnancy increase intra-abdominal pressure, and progesterone is among the drugs and hormones that lower LES tone.
option_notes: Both mechanisms are on the slides.
Acid excess is not the mechanism given.
The pylorus is not the barrier.

title: In which patients can ketoacidosis develop quickly instead of over a few days?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In which patients can ketoacidosis develop quickly instead of over a few days?
options: A patient whose insulin pump malfunctions
A middle-aged adult on stable insulin injections
body.explanation: DKA signs usually develop gradually over a few days, except in children, pregnant women and the elderly, or when an insulin pump malfunctions.
option_notes: Pump failure stops insulin delivery abruptly.
In most adults, signs develop gradually over a few days.

title: An 80-year-old woman with untreated hypothyroidism is found stuporous, with a temperature of 34 °C and slow, shallow breathing. Which laboratory findings are e…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An 80-year-old woman with untreated hypothyroidism is found stuporous, with a temperature of 34 °C and slow, shallow breathing. Which laboratory findings are expected?
body.explanation: Myxoedema coma, the end stage of untreated hypothyroidism in the elderly, combines weakness, stupor, hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia and hypoventilation, and can end in shock and death.
option_notes: Myxoedema coma: hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoventilation.
Glucose and sodium fall, not rise.
These are not features of myxoedema coma.
High FT4 with low TSH is hyperthyroidism.

title: Gastroenteritis as a cause of acute vomiting can be:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Gastroenteritis as a cause of acute vomiting can be:
body.explanation: Gastroenteritis: viral, bacterial or parasitic; food poisoning.

title: Which are features of hyperprolactinaemia in a woman?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are features of hyperprolactinaemia in a woman?
body.explanation: Galactorrhoea, menstrual disorders, infertility and low libido. Heat intolerance and tremor are hyperthyroidism.
option_notes: Milk secretion is a classic sign in women.
Heat intolerance and tremor are signs of hyperthyroidism.

title: Which is a sign of severe hypoxia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a sign of severe hypoxia?
body.explanation: Severe hypoxia: tachycardia, tachypnoea, bradycardia, extreme restlessness and cyanosis.

title: Organs projecting onto the right hypochondriac region include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Organs projecting onto the right hypochondriac region include:
body.explanation: Right hypochondriac: liver, gallbladder, right kidney, small intestine.
option_notes: Spleen is in the left hypochondriac region.

title: After excretion into the gut, per the diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: After excretion into the gut, per the diagram:
options: Part of urobilinogen returns via the portal vein
Bilirubin is conjugated in the gut wall
body.explanation: In the gut bilirubin becomes urobilinogen, partly reabsorbed via the portal vein (some reaching the kidney), the rest eliminated as stercobilinogen.

title: Adrenal scintigraphy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Adrenal scintigraphy:
options: Uses a radioactive marker taken up by the adrenals
Shows hyperplasia as bilateral or unilateral homogeneous fixation
Can reveal a tumour or metastasis
Is the examination of choice for adrenal exploration
body.explanation: Scintigraphy injects a radioactive marker with adrenal uptake: normal fixation, hyperplasia (increased volume, bilateral or unilateral homogeneous fixation), tumour or metastasis.
option_notes: Wrong: CT/MRI is the examination of choice.

title: About the laboratory test list for jaundice:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the laboratory test list for jaundice:
options: It is given in no particular order
It includes iron tests and protein electrophoresis
It requires viral serology always first
body.explanation: Warning: this is a list, no order intended; includes CBC, smear, PT, LFT, protein electrophoresis, iron, haemolysis, autoimmune, viral and infection tests.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Motor dysphagia. Impaired peristalsis or LES relaxation: liquids as much as solids (paradoxical), intermittent.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Motor: liquids as much as solids (paradoxical).
Another box. Oropharyngeal: hard to start the swallow, cough, nasal regurgitation.
Another box. Endoscopy: the first-line test.

title: Which cause hepatomegaly? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cause hepatomegaly? (choose all)
body.explanation: Heart failure, steatosis, cirrhosis, tumours, hepatitis and more.
option_notes: Congestion from heart failure enlarges the liver.
Appendicitis does not enlarge the liver.
Migraine does not involve the liver.

title: How long after bleeding starts does melena appear?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How long after bleeding starts does melena appear?
body.explanation: Melena appears 6 to 8 hours after bleeding starts.
option_notes: Blood needs time to be digested.

title: Metabolic and endocrine causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Metabolic and endocrine causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Metabolic and endocrine: DKA, adrenal crisis, hyperthyroidism, hypercalcaemia.

title: Risk factors for constipation to look for in the history include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Risk factors for constipation to look for in the history include:
body.explanation: Risk factors listed: older patients, low-fiber diet, sedentary lifestyle, pregnancy.

title: Which is a neurological cause of dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a neurological cause of dysphagia?
body.explanation: Stroke, Parkinson's, ALS, multiple sclerosis, myasthenia gravis, myopathies.
option_notes: Myasthenia gravis weakens the swallowing muscles.
A peptic ulcer is not a cause.
A hiatal hernia is digestive, not neurological.

title: What is bronchiectasis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is bronchiectasis?
body.explanation: A permanent, irreversible increase in bronchial calibre (3rd to 8th order), with morning bronchorrhoea.

title: Which fat distribution is typical of hypercortisolism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which fat distribution is typical of hypercortisolism?
body.explanation: Truncal obesity with a moon face and particular fat deposits, while the limbs lose muscle.
option_notes: Fat gathers on the trunk, face and neck.
The limbs get thinner from muscle wasting.
Fat is central, not only gluteal.
Patients gain weight centrally, they do not get thin.

title: Why does primary, but not secondary, adrenal insufficiency cause hyperpigmentation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why does primary, but not secondary, adrenal insufficiency cause hyperpigmentation?
options: ACTH is high in primary AI
Aldosterone is high in primary AI
Cortisol is high in secondary AI
Melanocytes are destroyed in primary AI
body.explanation: In primary AI the adrenals fail, cortisol is low and ACTH rises, causing hyperpigmentation. In secondary (pituitary) AI ACTH is low, so the skin is pale.
option_notes: Low cortisol lifts feedback, so ACTH rises and darkens the skin.
Aldosterone is low in primary AI.
Cortisol is low in secondary AI.

title: On noriodocholesterol scintigraphy, an aldosterone-producing adenoma gives:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On noriodocholesterol scintigraphy, an aldosterone-producing adenoma gives:
body.explanation: Morphological exploration: noriodocholesterol scintigraphy - adenoma: unilateral hyperfixation.
option_notes: Wrong: bilateral homogeneous fixation suggests hyperplasia.
Wrong: whole-body search is MIBG for phaeochromocytoma.

title: On the steroidogenesis diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the steroidogenesis diagram:
options: All three cortical zones start from cholesterol
Side-chain cleavage turns cholesterol into pregnenolone
Aldosterone is synthesised in the zona reticularis
body.explanation: Each zone starts from cholesterol -> pregnenolone (CYP11A1); in the fasciculata, 11-deoxycortisol -> cortisol via CYP11B1; aldosterone is made in the glomerulosa.
option_notes: Correct: cholesterol is the start in each zone.
Correct: last step of cortisol synthesis.
Wrong: aldosterone is made in the zona glomerulosa.

title: Which mechanism causes choleriform diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which mechanism causes choleriform diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Secretory (choleriform): profuse watery diarrhoea persisting during fasting, e.g. cholera, ETEC.
option_notes: A toxin makes the gut actively secrete water (cholera).
Osmotic diarrhoea stops with fasting and is not choleriform.

title: An ECG is done in a vomiting patient mainly to look for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An ECG is done in a vomiting patient mainly to look for:
body.explanation: ECG: if electrolyte imbalance is suspected, particularly hypokalaemia, which can affect heart rhythm.
option_notes: Wrong: gastric emptying is not assessed by ECG.
Wrong: that is the hCG test.
Wrong: meningitis is a clinical and cerebral diagnosis.

title: On the 'Major complications of diabetes' figure:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the 'Major complications of diabetes' figure:
options: High blood glucose and blood pressure can damage eye vessels, causing retinopathy, cataracts and glaucoma
High blood pressure damages small kidney vessels and excess glucose overworks the kidneys
Brain complications are classed as microvascular
Hypoglycaemia is given as the main cause of coronary heart disease
body.explanation: Microvascular: eye, kidney, neuropathy. Macrovascular: brain, heart (high BP and insulin resistance raise coronary risk), extremities.
option_notes: Brain (stroke, TIA) is on the macrovascular side.
Heart panel cites high BP and insulin resistance.

title: A 35-year-old woman has tiredness worse in the evening, weight loss, nausea, BP 90/60 and dark knuckles and gums. Na is 128 mmol/L and K 5.9 mmol/L. What is th…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 35-year-old woman has tiredness worse in the evening, weight loss, nausea, BP 90/60 and dark knuckles and gums. Na is 128 mmol/L and K 5.9 mmol/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
body.explanation: Asthenia peaking in the evening, weight loss, digestive signs, hypotension, hyperpigmentation over pressure areas and gums, hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia: primary adrenal insufficiency. Secondary AI has no hyperpigmentation and no hyperkalaemia.
option_notes: Evening tiredness, pigmentation, low BP, low Na and high K: primary AI.
Secondary AI has no pigmentation and no hyperkalaemia.
Cushing's gives weight gain and hypertension.
An aldosterone adenoma gives hypertension and low potassium.

title: How many people had AFib in 2019?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How many people had AFib in 2019?
body.explanation: 33.5 million in 2010, almost 59 million in 2019, projected to rise over 60 percent by 2050.

title: Which cause abolished breath sounds on one side? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cause abolished breath sounds on one side? (choose all)
body.explanation: One-sided: pleurisy, pneumothorax, hydropneumothorax, main bronchus obstruction. Bilateral: upper airway obstruction or advanced emphysema.

title: Which muscles waste in Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which muscles waste in Cushing's syndrome?
body.explanation: Proximal limb muscle atrophy contrasts with truncal obesity.
option_notes: Facial fat increases (moon face); facial muscles are not the typical site.
The diaphragm is not the typical site.
Proximal limb muscles waste, in contrast with truncal obesity.
The heart is not the muscle that wastes.

title: What is a vomica?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is a vomica?
body.explanation: A vomica is the sudden evacuation through the mouth, during coughing, of an abundant purulent collection.
option_notes: A vomica is a sudden, abundant expectoration of pus.

title: KDIGO 2012 GFR categories (mL/min/1.73 m2):
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: KDIGO 2012 GFR categories (mL/min/1.73 m2):

title: What defines dysentery?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What defines dysentery?
body.explanation: A syndrome of diffuse abdominal pain, frequent stools with mucus, blood and/or pus, and false urges.
option_notes: Dysentery is mucus and blood in the stools with urgency and false urges.
Watery diarrhoea without blood is not dysentery.
Vomiting and fever alone do not define dysentery.

title: In the post-traumatic hypopituitarism case (flattened pituitary after a middle cranial fossa fracture), anterior pituitary tests would show:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the post-traumatic hypopituitarism case (flattened pituitary after a middle cranial fossa fracture), anterior pituitary tests would show:
options: Low fT4 with a TSH that is not raised
Markedly raised TSH with low fT4
body.explanation: Severe hypopituitarism gives central adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism and GH deficiency (panhypopituitarism chart). The slide asks the question without giving answers.
option_notes: Central hypothyroidism: TSH is low or normal.
High TSH is primary hypothyroidism. Prolactin is ambiguous (low, or high from stalk effect).

title: Hyperthyroidism appears in the lecture as a cause of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hyperthyroidism appears in the lecture as a cause of:
body.explanation: Hyperthyroidism is listed among both acute and chronic metabolic and endocrine causes.
option_notes: Correct: acute metabolic and endocrine causes.
Correct: chronic metabolic and endocrine causes.
Wrong: it is a metabolic and endocrine cause.
Wrong: it is listed among the etiologies.

title: What coronary stenosis typically causes stable angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What coronary stenosis typically causes stable angina?
body.explanation: Atherosclerotic plaque narrowing a coronary artery by more than 70 percent cannot meet demand on exertion.
option_notes: Over 70% stenosis cannot meet demand on exertion.

title: Which test detects non-acid reflux?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test detects non-acid reflux?
body.explanation: Impedancemetry detects non-acid reflux; manometry assesses LES pressure.
option_notes: Impedance detects reflux whatever its acidity.
Manometry measures LES pressure and motility.
Endoscopy shows lesions, not reflux episodes.

title: The hypogastric region contains:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hypogastric region contains:
body.explanation: Hypogastric region: urinary bladder, sigmoid colon, female reproductive organs.
option_notes: Caecum is in the right iliac region.

title: Which chest pain improves sitting forward?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which chest pain improves sitting forward?
body.explanation: Pericarditis: sharp retrosternal pain, worse on coughing, swallowing and inspiration, relieved by sitting and leaning forward.
option_notes: Pneumothorax is not relieved this way.
Pneumonia is not relieved this way.
Dissection is not relieved by position.

title: Which features suggest type 2 diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which features suggest type 2 diabetes?
options: Age over 40 with a family history
Progressive onset, sometimes found at a complication
Ketoacidosis as the usual first sign
body.explanation: No inaugural ketoacidosis in type 2: ketoacidosis only with an added factor such as infection.
option_notes: Age over 40 with a family history fits type 2.
Type 2 starts slowly and may be found at a complication.

title: How does hypertension cause AFib?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How does hypertension cause AFib?
body.explanation: Long-standing high blood pressure enlarges and scars the atria.
option_notes: Pressure overload stretches and scars the atria.

title: What surgical options treat angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What surgical options treat angina?
body.explanation: Coronary angioplasty and coronary bypass surgery.
option_notes: Transplant is not the standard treatment.

title: Autoimmune Addison's disease is marked by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Autoimmune Addison's disease is marked by:
body.explanation: Primary AI aetiologies: Addison's disease - anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies; adrenal tuberculosis - calcifications on imaging.
option_notes: Wrong: calcifications point to adrenal tuberculosis.
Wrong: autoimmune adrenals are small (cortical retraction).

title: In men, the usual manifestations of hyperprolactinaemia are those of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In men, the usual manifestations of hyperprolactinaemia are those of:
body.explanation: The slide states that in men the usual manifestations are those of hypogonadism.
option_notes: Wrong: that is Cushing, not prolactin excess.
Wrong: not a feature of prolactin excess.

title: About bile-stained (green or yellow) vomiting:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About bile-stained (green or yellow) vomiting:
options: The content table links it to bile reflux
The summary slide also links it to duodenal obstruction
Bilious vomiting is a reassuring sign
body.explanation: Bile-stained vomit suggests bile reflux (summary slide: bile reflux or duodenal obstruction). Bilious or feculent vomiting is an alarm symptom suggesting intestinal obstruction.
option_notes: Wrong: it is an alarm symptom.

title: In the zona reticularis, per the steroidogenesis diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the zona reticularis, per the steroidogenesis diagram:
options: DHEA can be converted to androstenedione
body.explanation: The reticularis path: 17(OH)-pregnenolone -> DHEA (17,20-lyase) -> DHEAS (SULT2A1); DHEA -> androstenedione via 3beta-HSD, which has very low activity in this zone.
option_notes: Correct: 'very low activity in this zone'.

title: A 30-year-old has burning behind the sternum after meals and bitter fluid in the mouth when lying down, with no other symptoms. What is the next step?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 30-year-old has burning behind the sternum after meals and bitter fluid in the mouth when lying down, with no other symptoms. What is the next step?
options: The diagnosis is clinical: no test is needed first
body.explanation: Typical forms (heartburn + regurgitation) without alarm signs are diagnosed clinically.
option_notes: Typical symptoms without red flags are enough.
Endoscopy is for alarm signs, atypical forms, age over 50 or treatment failure.
pH-metry is for atypical cases or NERD.
A barium swallow looks for complications.

title: Which cause atrial fibrillation? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cause atrial fibrillation? (choose all)
body.explanation: Hypertension, coronary disease, valvular (especially mitral) disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathy.
option_notes: Mitral disease enlarges the left atrium.
Asthma is not a classic cause.

title: Surgery in GI bleeding is indicated for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Surgery in GI bleeding is indicated for:
body.explanation: Surgery is indicated in case of refractory bleeding or perforation.

title: Post-prandial, urgent diarrhoea that improves with fasting, in hyperthyroidism, is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Post-prandial, urgent diarrhoea that improves with fasting, in hyperthyroidism, is:
body.explanation: Due to accelerated transit.
option_notes: Fast transit after meals is motor diarrhoea.

title: About Graves' disease:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About Graves' disease:
options: It is an autoimmune disease on a genetically predisposed background
It may be associated with other autoimmune diseases
Scintigraphy typically shows a single hot nodule with an extinguished contralateral lobe
body.explanation: Graves': most common cause, predominantly female, autoimmune on a genetic background, sometimes with other autoimmune diseases; scintigraphy shows diffuse homogeneous hyperfixation.
option_notes: Correct: sometimes associated with other autoimmune diseases.
Wrong: diffuse homogeneous hyperfixation; hot nodule = toxic adenoma.

title: Which feature points to haemoptysis rather than haematemesis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which feature points to haemoptysis rather than haematemesis?
body.explanation: Haemoptysis is frothy blood preceded by coughing; haematemesis is red or black blood, sometimes with food debris or clots, often preceded by nausea and retching (slide 06).
option_notes: Black blood with food points to haematemesis.
Nausea and retching come before haematemesis.
Frothy blood after coughing is haemoptysis.
Clots with food debris point to haematemesis.

title: Factors involved in type 2 diabetes include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Factors involved in type 2 diabetes include:
options: Insulin resistance with progressive insulin deficiency
body.explanation: Type 2: genetic (family history), environmental (nutritional imbalance, low activity, android obesity) and metabolic factors (insulin resistance, progressive insulin deficiency).

title: Why do patients with Cushing's syndrome bruise without obvious injury?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why do patients with Cushing's syndrome bruise without obvious injury?
options: Capillary fragility with thin, fragile skin
body.explanation: Skin atrophy (fine, fragile skin) and capillary fragility cause ecchymoses without obvious injury.
option_notes: Thin skin and fragile capillaries cause easy bruising.
Platelets are not low in Cushing's.
Liver failure is not the cause.

title: A fasting glucose of 1.15 g/L and a 2-hour OGTT value of 1.55 g/L are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A fasting glucose of 1.15 g/L and a 2-hour OGTT value of 1.55 g/L are:
options: Abnormal but below the diabetes thresholds
body.explanation: Normal is fasting under 1.10 g/L and under 1.40 g/L 2 hours after OGTT. Diabetes needs fasting ≥ 1.26 g/L or 2-hour ≥ 2 g/L. These values sit in between (prediabetes range).
option_notes: Above normal but below the diabetes thresholds.
Normal is fasting under 1.10 and 2-hour under 1.40 g/L.

title: Diabetic amyotrophy is associated with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Diabetic amyotrophy is associated with:
options: Weakness, wasting and severe pain of pelvic girdle and thigh muscles
Distal symmetric loss of vibration sense only
Involvement of a single mixed nerve trunk
body.explanation: Amyotrophy: muscle weakness, wasting and severe pain of muscles in the pelvic girdle and thigh.

title: What causes unstable angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes unstable angina?
body.explanation: A thrombus on the plaque further narrows the artery, so pain occurs even at rest and does not go away.
option_notes: Aortic stenosis is a fixed valve cause.
A clot on a ruptured plaque narrows the artery further.
Anaemia lowers oxygen supply but is not the cause.

title: Which cause follows long-standing reflux?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cause follows long-standing reflux?
body.explanation: Peptic stricture: reflux history, slow progression, mainly solids, no early deterioration.
option_notes: Achalasia is a motor disorder unrelated to reflux.
Acid reflux scars and narrows the lower oesophagus.

title: Laboratory signs of organ damage in hypothyroidism include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Laboratory signs of organ damage in hypothyroidism include:
body.explanation: Organ-damage tests: macrocytic anaemia, dilutional hyponatraemia (fluid retention), hypercholesterolaemia, hyperprolactinaemia. Per the lecture slides; some textbooks say the anaemia is more often normocytic.
option_notes: Correct: dilutional hyponatraemia from fluid retention.

title: What is stridor?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is stridor?
body.explanation: Stridor: inspiratory, musical, very loud, monophonic, from laryngeal spasm or swelling in upper airway obstruction.
option_notes: Stridor is a loud inspiratory upper airway sound.

title: In adults, GH deficiency causes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In adults, GH deficiency causes:
options: Reduced lean body mass and increased body fat
Increased cardiovascular risk and impaired well-being
body.explanation: Table: GH deficiency - children: short stature; adults: reduced exercise capacity, lower lean mass, more body fat, impaired psychological well-being, higher CV risk.
option_notes: Short stature is the feature in children.

title: Regarding inspection of the thyroid region:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding inspection of the thyroid region:
options: The patient is asked to swallow
Inflammatory signs such as oedema and redness are sought
A normal thyroid gland is usually visible as a midline bulge on inspection from the front
A thyroglossal cyst is assessed by asking the patient to stick out the tongue
body.explanation: Inspection is done from front and side, with swallowing, looking for goitre, scars, dilated veins and inflammatory signs; a thyroglossal cyst is tested with 'stick out tongue'. The normal thyroid is not visible.
option_notes: Correct: 'Swallow' is part of thyroid inspection.
Correct: search for inflammatory signs (oedema, redness).
Wrong: the normal thyroid is not visible.

title: Features of hypothyroidism in the comparison table include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Features of hypothyroidism in the comparison table include:
options: Frequent bowel movements and soft stools
body.explanation: Hypothyroid column: weight gain, loss of appetite, cold sensitivity, thinning hair, dry skin, constipation, joint pain, depression/impaired memory, bradycardia.
option_notes: Wrong: thinning skin is hyperthyroid; hypo gives dry skin.

title: What must be reported in a pleurisy on general exam?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What must be reported in a pleurisy on general exam?
body.explanation: In pleurisy, report the presence or absence of pericarditis and ascites, and of meningeal signs.

title: What causes a Mallory-Weiss tear?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes a Mallory-Weiss tear?
body.explanation: A mucosal tear at the oesophagogastric junction after vomiting.
option_notes: Crohn's disease is not the cause.
Repeated vomiting tears the mucosa at the oesophagogastric junction.

title: Which is a cardiovascular sign of hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cardiovascular sign of hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: Persistent resting tachycardia, palpitations, loud heart sounds, systolic murmur, raised systolic BP.
option_notes: Hyperthyroidism speeds the heart; bradycardia fits hypothyroidism.
Heart sounds are loud, not soft.
Persistent resting tachycardia is a key sign.

title: Regarding stroke in diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding stroke in diabetes:
options: A stroke can induce a DKA revealing diabetes
Strokes in diabetics are mostly haemorrhagic rather than ischaemic
Strokes are less frequent in diabetics
body.explanation: Strokes are more frequent in diabetics, mainly ischaemic; a stroke can reveal diabetes or induce a DKA revealing it.

title: A patient on anticoagulants suddenly develops lumbar pain, vomiting and collapse. Which cause of primary adrenal insufficiency fits?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient on anticoagulants suddenly develops lumbar pain, vomiting and collapse. Which cause of primary adrenal insufficiency fits?
body.explanation: Bilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a cause of primary adrenal insufficiency and can present acutely.
option_notes: Anticoagulation plus sudden lumbar pain and collapse.
Tuberculosis is slow, with calcified adrenals.
A pituitary tumour gives secondary AI.

title: On the differential diagnosis diagram, primary polydipsia starts with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the differential diagnosis diagram, primary polydipsia starts with:
options: Ineffective AVP action in the kidneys
body.explanation: Diagram: (1) polydipsia, (2) suppressed AVP release, (3) polyuria.
option_notes: AVP is suppressed secondarily, not primarily deficient.

title: Which feature is common to both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism in the comparison table?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which feature is common to both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism in the comparison table?
body.explanation: Fatigue, muscle weakness, menstrual irregularity and goitre appear in both states.

title: What is the most common significant arrhythmia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the most common significant arrhythmia?
body.explanation: Atrial fibrillation is the most common clinically significant arrhythmia worldwide.
option_notes: AFib is the commonest significant arrhythmia.

title: What does a vertical sternal scar indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does a vertical sternal scar indicate?
body.explanation: A vertical scar over the sternum indicates previous open-heart surgery.
option_notes: An appendectomy scar is in the right iliac fossa.
A lung biopsy does not leave a sternal scar.
Sternotomy, splitting the sternum, is used for open-heart surgery.
A rib fracture leaves no scar.

title: In a constipated patient, what do absent bowel sounds suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a constipated patient, what do absent bowel sounds suggest?
body.explanation: Absent sounds: ileus. Hyperactive sounds: obstruction. Faecal loading is suggested by dullness on percussion (slide 15).
option_notes: Faecal loading is found as dullness on percussion, not by silence.

title: Regarding dexamethasone suppression tests in suspected Cushing:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding dexamethasone suppression tests in suspected Cushing:
options: The 1 mg overnight test is the best screening test
The low-dose test uses 2 mg/day for 48 h
The high-dose test is the first screening test
body.explanation: The 1 mg overnight DXM test is the best screening test; the LDDST (2 mg/day for 48 h) is optimal in psychiatric problems, morbid obesity or alcoholism. The HDDST is for finding the cause.
option_notes: Wrong: HDDST follows a high or normal ACTH.

title: The diagnostic algorithm for thyroid cancer includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The diagnostic algorithm for thyroid cancer includes:
options: Thyroid hormone tests plus calcitonin as a tumour marker
Fine needle aspiration biopsy, then histopathology
Thyroid scintigraphy as the mandatory first step before palpation
body.explanation: Algorithm: 1 palpation, 2 ultrasound, 3 thyroid hormones + tumour markers (calcitonin), 4 FNA biopsy, 5 histopathology.
option_notes: Wrong: scintigraphy is not in the algorithm.

title: The positive diagnosis of jaundice relies on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The positive diagnosis of jaundice relies on:
body.explanation: The slide states: Diagnosis = clinical examination.

title: How is stroke volume calculated?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is stroke volume calculated?
body.explanation: Stroke volume = end-diastolic minus end-systolic volume: 135 minus 65 = 70 mL.
option_notes: The subtraction is the other way round.
Volume at the end of filling minus volume left after ejection.

title: According to the lecture conclusion:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture conclusion:
options: Severity of diabetes depends on its acute and chronic complications
Type 2 diabetes has no inaugural ketoacidosis
Type 1 diabetes occurs typically with overweight and cardiovascular risk factors
Diagnosis relies on symptoms alone, without specific criteria
body.explanation: Conclusion: diagnosis based on specific criteria; T1 sudden, young, no overweight or CV risk; T2 older, no inaugural ketoacidosis; severity = complications.
option_notes: T1 is without overweight or CV risk factors.
Diagnosis is based on specific criteria.

title: Adrenal CT scan/MRI:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Adrenal CT scan/MRI:
options: Is the examination of choice for adrenal exploration
Shows normal adrenals with an inverted Y shape
body.explanation: CT/MRI is the examination of choice: it visualises normal adrenals (inverted Y) and pathological states (tumours, hyperplasia, atrophy).
option_notes: Wrong: atrophy is one of the pathological situations shown.

title: The aims of paraclinical tests in vomiting are to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The aims of paraclinical tests in vomiting are to:
options: Give an initial work-up of the possible etiologies
Guide further diagnostic and therapeutic decisions
Apply the same full panel to every patient
body.explanation: Aims: initial work-up of etiologies, detect complications, guide decisions. The choice of tests depends on the presentation and suspected etiology.
option_notes: Wrong: tests depend on the presentation and suspected etiology.

title: On the summary slide, digoxin appears in which group of causes of vomiting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the summary slide, digoxin appears in which group of causes of vomiting?
body.explanation: Drugs/toxins: chemotherapy, opioids, antibiotics, NSAIDs, digoxin, alcohol, toxins.
option_notes: Correct: listed with chemotherapy, opioids, antibiotics, NSAIDs.
Wrong: psychogenic vomiting, eating disorders, rumination.
Wrong: raised ICP, migraine, vertigo, meningitis.
Wrong: digestive diseases such as gastroenteritis or obstruction.

title: What is the first-line test for dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the first-line test for dysphagia?
body.explanation: EGD visualises the mucosa and allows biopsies; it is the gold standard.
option_notes: The barium swallow is a second-line test.
Endoscopy sees the mucosa and takes biopsies.
CT is for staging, not first-line.
Manometry comes after a normal endoscopy.

title: Aldosterone-producing adenoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Aldosterone-producing adenoma:
options: Is a benign tumour of the adrenal cortex
Presents with systolo-diastolic hypertension and hypokalaemia
Is a tumour of the adrenal medulla
body.explanation: It is a benign adenoma of the adrenal cortex producing excessive aldosterone; clinically, systolo-diastolic hypertension with hypokalaemia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Definition. Stools over 300 g/day, more than 3 per day, over 90% water.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Definition box: over 300 g/day, over 3 stools a day, over 90% water.

title: Biochemical diagnostic criteria for DKA in adults include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Biochemical diagnostic criteria for DKA in adults include:
options: Blood glucose >250 mg/dL or known diabetes
Blood glucose above 600 mg/dL is required for the diagnosis
body.explanation: Criteria: ketonaemia >=3 mmol/L or significant ketonuria (>2+), glucose >250 mg/dL (>14 mmol/L) or known diabetes, plus acidosis.

title: About hypothyroidism:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About hypothyroidism:
options: It causes a generalised slowing down of metabolic processes
It always has a pituitary origin, with the thyroid gland itself being normal
It can be of primary or secondary origin
It results from an excess of thyroid hormones
body.explanation: Hypothyroidism is a clinical syndrome from thyroid hormone deficiency, causing generalised slowing of metabolism; origin may be primary (peripheral) or secondary (pituitary).
option_notes: Correct: generalised slowing of metabolic processes.
Wrong: it is a hormone deficiency.

title: On abdominal auscultation of a vomiting patient:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On abdominal auscultation of a vomiting patient:
options: Hyperactive bowel sounds may indicate obstruction
Absent bowel sounds may suggest ileus
body.explanation: Hyperactive bowel sounds may indicate obstruction; absent sounds may suggest ileus.

title: What liver is hard, irregular and nodular without pain?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What liver is hard, irregular and nodular without pain?
body.explanation: Cirrhosis: firm to hard, sharp irregular border, nodular surface, painless.
option_notes: The congestive liver is soft and painful.
Cirrhosis gives a hard, irregular, nodular, painless liver.
An abscess is smooth and very painful.
Acute hepatitis gives a soft, tender liver.

title: What ECG change occurs in Prinzmetal angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What ECG change occurs in Prinzmetal angina?
body.explanation: Transmural ischaemia gives ST elevation during attacks.
option_notes: ST depression is stable or unstable angina.
Spasm closes the artery fully: transmural ischaemia, ST elevation.

title: Which system causes fluid retention in heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which system causes fluid retention in heart failure?
body.explanation: Low renal flow activates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, retaining fluid to raise preload.
option_notes: Low kidney flow activates RAAS, retaining salt and water.
The parasympathetic system does not retain fluid.
The thyroid axis does not cause this.

title: What does the Frank-Starling mechanism describe?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does the Frank-Starling mechanism describe?
body.explanation: Like a rubber band: more ventricular filling (preload) gives a larger stroke volume.
option_notes: The opposite: less filling, weaker contraction.
More stretch gives a stronger contraction.

title: In the hepatocyte (slide 12):
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the hepatocyte (slide 12):
options: Conjugated bilirubin is secreted towards the bile canaliculus
Bilirubin arriving from blood is conjugated
Haemoglobin is broken down into bilirubin
body.explanation: The hepatocyte takes up bilirubin from blood, conjugates it and secretes conjugated bilirubin into bile.

title: What is hemoptysis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is hemoptysis?
body.explanation: Blood expectorated from the subglottic airways during coughing; it excludes gum, pharyngeal, nasal and digestive bleeding.
option_notes: Blood coughed up from below the glottis.

title: The extra-digestive symptoms listed with vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The extra-digestive symptoms listed with vomiting include:
body.explanation: Extra-digestive symptoms: headache, photophobia (meningeal syndrome), altered consciousness. Diarrhoea is listed among the digestive associated symptoms.
option_notes: Wrong: listed, but as a digestive symptom.

title: The initial laboratory work-up in GI bleeding includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The initial laboratory work-up in GI bleeding includes:
body.explanation: Initial work-up: CBC, blood typing, crossmatch, ionogram, creatinine, liver enzymes.
option_notes: Wrong: not part of the emergency work-up; bleeding is visible.

title: What fluid defines a pyopneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What fluid defines a pyopneumothorax?
body.explanation: Yellow: hydropneumothorax. Pus: pyopneumothorax. Blood: haemopneumothorax. Chyle: chylopneumothorax.
option_notes: Clear fluid with air is hydropneumothorax.

title: What does digital clubbing indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does digital clubbing indicate?
body.explanation: Enlarged, rounded Hippocratic nails with swollen distal phalanges indicate a pathology causing chronic hypoxaemia.

title: A pituitary tumour spreads sideways into the cavernous sinus. What can it cause?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A pituitary tumour spreads sideways into the cavernous sinus. What can it cause?
body.explanation: Cranial nerves III, IV and VI run there: diplopia and ptosis.
option_notes: Cranial nerves III, IV and VI are compressed in the sinus.
Hearing (VIII) is not in the cavernous sinus.
Smell (I) is not in the cavernous sinus.

title: Regarding the digestive and other examination in jaundice:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the digestive and other examination in jaundice:
options: The abdomen can be skipped if imaging is planned
body.explanation: Digestive exam: buccal cavity, abdomen, proctological exam; plus lymph nodes and other organs and systems.
option_notes: Abdomen is part of the exam.

title: A 32-year-old woman has weight loss despite a big appetite, palpitations, heat intolerance, a diffuse goitre with a bruit and bilateral exophthalmos. Which res…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 32-year-old woman has weight loss despite a big appetite, palpitations, heat intolerance, a diffuse goitre with a bruit and bilateral exophthalmos. Which result is the most specific for the cause?
body.explanation: TRAb are highly specific to Graves' disease. A low TSH only confirms thyrotoxicosis, whatever the cause; anti-TPO and anti-Tg are used to look for the cause of hypothyroidism; calcitonin is a tumour marker for thyroid cancer.
option_notes: TRAb are highly specific to Graves' disease.
A low TSH confirms thyrotoxicosis but not its cause.
Calcitonin is a tumour marker (medullary thyroid cancer).

title: What is normal cardiac output?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is normal cardiac output?
body.explanation: Cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume: 70 x 70 mL = 4.9 L/min.
option_notes: Too low for a resting adult.
70 beats x 70 mL is about 5 L/min.
This is about one stroke volume.

title: Which complication of Cushing's syndrome is specific to children?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which complication of Cushing's syndrome is specific to children?
body.explanation: Bone and muscle complications include osteoporosis with fractures and vertebral compression, aseptic osteonecrosis, myopathy and, in children, growth retardation.
option_notes: Osteonecrosis can occur at any age.
Vertebral compression occurs at any age.

title: A jaundiced patient is drowsy and has a flapping tremor of the outstretched hands. What does this suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A jaundiced patient is drowsy and has a flapping tremor of the outstretched hands. What does this suggest?
options: A simple gallstone in the bile duct
body.explanation: Asterixis and the Glasgow score are part of the general examination of a jaundiced patient: a flapping tremor with drowsiness points to hepatic encephalopathy.
option_notes: Asterixis and altered consciousness point to hepatic encephalopathy.
Biliary obstruction alone does not cause encephalopathy.

title: Which triad is diagnostic of Graves' disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which triad is diagnostic of Graves' disease?
body.explanation: Per the lecture (slide 31), the diagnosis is clinical: thyrotoxicosis + goitre + exophthalmos. Some textbooks quote another triad (hyperthyroidism, ophthalmopathy, pretibial dermopathy); the lecture's triad is the one asked here.
option_notes: Pain, fever and a goitre suggest subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
Weight gain and cold intolerance fit hypothyroidism.
Nodule, hoarseness and lymph nodes are warning signs of thyroid cancer.
Thyrotoxicosis + goitre + exophthalmos is the clinical triad in the lecture.

title: Visual field defects of the optic-chiasmatic syndrome include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Visual field defects of the optic-chiasmatic syndrome include:
body.explanation: Suprasellar extension compresses the chiasm: bitemporal visual loss in the superior fields (bitemporal superior quadrantanopia, then hemianopia) and homonymous contralateral hemianopia.
option_notes: Slide 24 (nasal field of the other eye).
Wrong: not described on the slides.

title: Diabetic retinopathy as a mode of discovery:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Diabetic retinopathy as a mode of discovery:
options: Vision is usually normal until vitreous haemorrhage or retinal detachment
Clinical signs are poor, so at-risk patients need screening by fundus examination
It always causes early visual loss
It is diagnosed by measuring intraocular pressure alone, without fundus examination
body.explanation: Retinopathy has poor clinical signs; vision is usually normal until vitreous haemorrhage or retinal detachment; screening by fundus +/- angiography.
option_notes: Wrong: fundus after dilation is key.

title: In cholestasis, prothrombin time is abnormal when the ratio falls below:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In cholestasis, prothrombin time is abnormal when the ratio falls below:
body.explanation: Prolonged prothrombin time (or decreased ratio <70%).

title: What is the ejection fraction in diastolic failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the ejection fraction in diastolic failure?
body.explanation: In diastolic failure the ejection fraction stays normal (about 64 percent), but stroke volume is still low because filling is reduced.
option_notes: Contraction is preserved, so the EF stays normal.
A low EF is systolic failure.
Zero is impossible in a living patient.

title: Signs of hypothyroidism shown in the lecture figures include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Signs of hypothyroidism shown in the lecture figures include:
body.explanation: Figures show puffy face, loss of eyebrow hair, carpal tunnel syndrome, slow heartbeat, and delayed relaxation of tendon reflexes.
option_notes: Correct: delayed relaxation of tendon reflexes.

title: The electrolyte imbalances listed as causes of acute vomiting are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The electrolyte imbalances listed as causes of acute vomiting are:
body.explanation: Electrolyte imbalances: hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia.

title: What do fine velcro crackles suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What do fine velcro crackles suggest?
body.explanation: Fine crackles: fluid, infection, fibrosis (velcro). Coarse crackles: fluid or infection (rice krispies).
option_notes: Fine velcro crackles suggest fibrosis or fluid.

title: The assessment after a stroke in a diabetic includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The assessment after a stroke in a diabetic includes:
options: ECG and echocardiography or cardiac stress test
body.explanation: Assessment: ECG, echocardiography/stress test, coronary angiogram, carotid Doppler, CT scan.

title: Which are alarm symptoms in a vomiting patient?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are alarm symptoms in a vomiting patient?
options: A single episode in a healthy young adult
body.explanation: Alarm symptoms: persistent vomiting, severe or progressive pain, haematemesis, fever, neurological symptoms, dehydration, weight loss, bilious or feculent vomiting, elderly patient, immunocompromised state.

title: Which investigation is therapeutic?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which investigation is therapeutic?
body.explanation: ERCP is listed as therapeutic; ultrasound, CT, MRI, endoscopic ultrasound and biopsy are diagnostic.
option_notes: ERCP can remove stones or place a stent.

title: The right iliac region contains:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The right iliac region contains:
body.explanation: Right iliac region: appendix, caecum.

title: Which recent drug suggests C. difficile?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which recent drug suggests C. difficile?
body.explanation: Recent antibiotics point to Clostridioides difficile.
option_notes: Paracetamol does not cause C. difficile.
Antibiotics disturb the flora and favour C. difficile.
Antacids are not the classic cause.

title: What is the tripod position?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the tripod position?
body.explanation: Patients with emphysema or distress lean forward with hands on knees to use accessory muscles, especially pectoralis major.
option_notes: Leaning forward, hands on knees, to use accessory muscles.

title: What are dysenteric stools composed of?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What are dysenteric stools composed of?
body.explanation: Non-faecal stools of whitish mucus with pus and blood.
option_notes: Dysenteric stools are mucus, pus and blood.

title: Surgical acute abdomen causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Surgical acute abdomen causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Surgical: peritonitis, appendicitis, cholecystitis, intestinal obstruction. Acute pancreatitis is listed as non-surgical.

title: Inspection of the perianal area during the rectal examination looks for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Inspection of the perianal area during the rectal examination looks for:
body.explanation: Inspection: examine the perianal area for hemorrhoids, fissures or fistulas (illustrated on the following slide).
option_notes: Wrong: strictures are found on palpation.

title: Central hyperthyroidism due to TSH hypersecretion:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Central hyperthyroidism due to TSH hypersecretion:
options: Is due to a pituitary adenoma
Shows high FT4 and FT3 with normal or high TSH
Shows high FT4 with a suppressed TSH
body.explanation: Slide: TSH hypersecretion is very rare; pituitary adenoma; high FT4 + FT3 with normal or high TSH.
option_notes: Suppressed TSH is not the central pattern described.

title: Pituitary anatomy relevant to mass effect:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Pituitary anatomy relevant to mass effect:
options: The gland sits in the sella turcica
The cavernous sinuses lie on both sides
The optic chiasm lies below the gland
The posterior lobe is the adenohypophysis
body.explanation: The pituitary lies in the hypophyseal fossa of the sella turcica, with the optic chiasm above and the cavernous sinuses on both sides.
option_notes: Wrong: the anterior lobe is the adenohypophysis.

title: Which phase of swallowing is voluntary?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which phase of swallowing is voluntary?
body.explanation: Oral: voluntary; pharyngeal: reflex; oesophageal: involuntary peristalsis.
option_notes: The oral phase is the only voluntary one.
Only the first phase is voluntary.
The pharyngeal phase is a reflex.

title: Equivalent diagnostic thresholds for diabetes per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Equivalent diagnostic thresholds for diabetes per the slides:
options: Random glucose 200 mg/dL = 7.0 mmol/L with symptoms
body.explanation: Criteria: FPG >=126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L), 2-h OGTT >=200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L), A1c >=6.5% (48 mmol/mol), random >=200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) with symptoms.

title: Polyuria and polydipsia are found in:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Polyuria and polydipsia are found in:
