body.explanation: All three conditions of the differential diagnosis produce polyuria and polydipsia; the hypopituitarism table lists ADH deficiency as polyuria and polydipsia.
option_notes: Table: ADH deficiency - polyuria and polydipsia.

title: Headache with papilledema in a vomiting patient suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Headache with papilledema in a vomiting patient suggests:
body.explanation: Headache and papilledema are signs of raised intracranial pressure.
option_notes: Correct: signs of raised intracranial pressure.
Wrong: a gastric emptying disorder, no papilledema.
Wrong: suggested by hyperactive bowel sounds.
Wrong: a pregnancy cause, no papilledema.

title: According to the key messages on GI bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the key messages on GI bleeding:
options: Meckel's diverticulum is typical of the elderly
Polyps or cancer are typical causes in the elderly
Severity is assessed only after endoscopy
Endoscopy has only a diagnostic role
body.explanation: Key messages: always assess severity first; endoscopy is the cornerstone of diagnosis and therapy; ulcers and varices in adults, polyps or cancer in the elderly, Meckel's in the young.
option_notes: Wrong: Meckel's is cited in the young.
Wrong: it is the cornerstone of diagnosis and therapy.

title: Pectus excavatum may point to which syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Pectus excavatum may point to which syndrome?
body.explanation: A sunken or protruding sternum, with ligamentous hypermobility, may signal Marfan syndrome.
option_notes: Down syndrome is not the classic link.
Turner syndrome is not the classic link.
Cushing syndrome does not deform the sternum.
Marfan's connective tissue defect deforms the sternum.

title: What can haematochezia also indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What can haematochezia also indicate?
body.explanation: Usually lower tract, but massive upper bleeding with fast transit can cause it.
option_notes: Massive upper bleeding with fast transit can come out bright red.
Minor gastritis does not cause haematochezia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Pharyngeal phase. Reflex closure of the larynx and propulsion into the oesophagus.
option_notes: Another box. Oropharyngeal: hard to start the swallow, cough, nasal regurgitation.
Another box. Endoscopy: the first-line test.
This is the box at the arrow. Pharyngeal phase: reflex.
Another box. Motor: liquids as much as solids (paradoxical).

title: About the clinical aspect of the definition of constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the clinical aspect of the definition of constipation:
options: Delayed evacuation of the large bowel content
body.explanation: Clinically, constipation is a delayed evacuation of the large bowel content, with fewer than 3 stools per week.
option_notes: Correct: clinical aspect on the definition slide.
Correct: <3 stools/week is the clinical threshold.
Wrong: quantitative aspect is a reduced amount, <100 g/day.
Wrong: constipated stools are hard from dehydration.

title: Correct pairings of oral lesion and cause include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Correct pairings of oral lesion and cause include:
body.explanation: Slides 6-7: aphthous ulcer (IBD), atrophic glossitis (B12 deficiency), oral candidiasis (fungus), angular cheilitis (iron deficiency anaemia).

title: Which are modifiable risk factors? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are modifiable risk factors? (choose all)
body.explanation: Tobacco, hypertension, diabetes, cholesterol, diet, activity; age and sex are not modifiable.

title: Stool consistency typical of constipation, as described in the history slide:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Stool consistency typical of constipation, as described in the history slide:
body.explanation: Stool consistency: hard or pellet-like stools.

title: Which diarrhoea gives greasy, pale, foul stools?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which diarrhoea gives greasy, pale, foul stools?
body.explanation: Malabsorption: abundant greasy stools with weight loss, anaemia, bone pain; celiac, Crohn's, pancreatic insufficiency.
option_notes: Fat malabsorption gives greasy, pale, foul stools.
Motor diarrhoea is post-prandial and urgent.

title: Which metabolic disorder accompanies hypercortisolism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which metabolic disorder accompanies hypercortisolism?
body.explanation: Cortisol excess causes diabetes or prediabetes and hypertension.
option_notes: Cortisol raises glucose; hypoglycaemia fits adrenal insufficiency.
Hypothyroidism is not caused by cortisol excess.
Cortisol excess causes diabetes or prediabetes.

title: What is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: Graves' disease, autoimmune, predominantly in women aged 20 to 40.
option_notes: Autoimmune Graves' disease is the most common cause, mainly in women aged 20 to 40.
Toxic adenoma is less common than Graves'.
Iodine deficiency causes goitre and hypothyroidism.

title: Why does prolactin excess cause amenorrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why does prolactin excess cause amenorrhoea?
options: It suppresses GnRH, so LH and FSH fall and ovulation stops
body.explanation: The lecture's diagram: prolactin up, GnRH down, FSH and LH down, anovulation, plus milk secretion.
option_notes: Prolactin does not destroy the ovaries; the effect is reversible.
Prolactin lowers GnRH, then LH and FSH, so ovulation stops.
The effect is central (GnRH), not on the uterus.

title: On the chart, conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with normal LFTs suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the chart, conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with normal LFTs suggests:
body.explanation: Normal LFT: decreased excretion/reuptake of bilirubin, e.g. Dubin-Johnson and Rotor syndromes.

title: About the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system on the diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system on the diagram:
options: Angiotensin I becomes angiotensin II in the lungs
Aldosterone increases Na+ and water retention
body.explanation: Liver angiotensinogen -> (renin) angiotensin I -> (lungs) angiotensin II -> adrenal aldosterone -> Na+ and water retention, K+ excretion, raised ECF volume and renal arterial pressure.
option_notes: Correct: conversion shown in the lungs.
Correct: angiotensin II acts on the adrenals.

title: During abdominal palpation, a patient suddenly develops headache, sweating and a very high BP. Which mechanism do the slides describe?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During abdominal palpation, a patient suddenly develops headache, sweating and a very high BP. Which mechanism do the slides describe?
options: Paroxysmal symptoms of a phaeochromocytoma triggered by tumour compression
body.explanation: The paroxysmal symptoms of phaeochromocytoma can be triggered by tumour compression; during attacks BP can be much higher than usual.
option_notes: Tumour compression can trigger an attack.
Acute AI gives collapse, not a very high BP.
A vasovagal reaction lowers BP and pulse.
Apoplexy is a pituitary event with visual loss.

title: In the pathophysiology of diabetic ketoacidosis:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the pathophysiology of diabetic ketoacidosis:
options: Increased lipolysis supplies free fatty acids for ketogenesis
Glucosuria causes osmotic diuresis and dehydration
Counter-regulatory hormones are decreased, blocking gluconeogenesis
body.explanation: Absolute insulin deficiency + increased counter-regulatory hormones: lipolysis, FFA, ketogenesis, ketonaemia, acidosis; hyperglycaemia, glucosuria, osmotic diuresis, dehydration.

title: Which ultrasound grades need fine-needle aspiration?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which ultrasound grades need fine-needle aspiration?
body.explanation: FNAC for U3 (indeterminate), U4 (suspicious) and U5 (malignant) lesions.
option_notes: U1 needs FNAC only in a high-risk patient.
U1 and U2 are normal or benign; FNAC only if high risk.
FNAC for U3 (indeterminate), U4 (suspicious) and U5 (malignant).

title: Clinical signs of peripheral artery disease include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Clinical signs of peripheral artery disease include:
body.explanation: PAD exam: loss of pulses, pain on palpation, pallor, muscle atrophy and hair loss, cool cyanotic skin, bruit, brittle slow-growing nails.
option_notes: Hot feet suggest neuropathy; PAD gives cool skin.

title: Which statement about polyphagia in uncontrolled diabetes is correct?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which statement about polyphagia in uncontrolled diabetes is correct?
options: It compensates for the cells' 'fasting state' caused by lack of insulin
It is a sign of hypoglycaemia
body.explanation: Without insulin the cells are in a fasting state: lipolysis causes weight loss, and polyphagia appears as compensation.
option_notes: Hyperglycaemia comes from lack of insulin, not from eating.
Weight is lost despite eating more.

title: Psychiatric causes of chronic vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Psychiatric causes of chronic vomiting include:
options: Psychogenic vomiting in response to stress or trauma
body.explanation: Psychiatric: functional vomiting, eating disorders (binge-purge), psychogenic vomiting in response to stress or trauma.

title: What does angular cheilitis suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does angular cheilitis suggest?
body.explanation: Angular cheilitis is a sign of iron deficiency anaemia.
option_notes: Vitamin C excess is not a cause.
Oral cancer gives an ulcer or mass.
Hypothyroidism is not the classic cause.

title: Aldosterone synthesis in the zona glomerulosa, per the diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Aldosterone synthesis in the zona glomerulosa, per the diagram:
body.explanation: In the glomerulosa: progesterone -> DOC (21-hydroxylase) -> corticosterone -> 18(OH)-corticosterone -> aldosterone (18-oxidase, CYP11B2).
option_notes: Wrong: 17(OH)-progesterone belongs to the fasciculata (cortisol) pathway.
Wrong: 11-deoxycortisol is the cortisol precursor in the fasciculata.

title: Morning vomiting is often seen in:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Morning vomiting is often seen in:
body.explanation: Morning vomiting: often in pregnant women or individuals with alcohol dependence.
option_notes: Wrong: vomiting during meals suggests a psychogenic cause.
Wrong: that gives late postprandial vomiting.

title: LES hypotonia as a cause of GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: LES hypotonia as a cause of GERD:
options: Is the most frequent anatomical cause
Is the same thing as hiatal hernia
body.explanation: LES hypotonia may be congenital or acquired; hiatal hernia is the most frequent anatomical cause.
option_notes: Wrong: hiatal hernia is the most frequent anatomical cause.
Wrong: it can also be acquired.
Wrong: they are listed as separate causes.

title: On scintigraphy, a nodule that does not take up the tracer is called:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On scintigraphy, a nodule that does not take up the tracer is called:
body.explanation: Scintigraphy classifies nodules as hot (hyperfunctional) or cold (non-functional).
option_notes: A hot nodule takes up more tracer than the rest of the gland.
'Toxic' describes hormone excess, not a scintigraphy pattern.
Ectopic means thyroid tissue outside its normal place.

title: In suspected diabetic coronary artery disease:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In suspected diabetic coronary artery disease:
options: Examination should rule out other causes of chest pain
Cardiac and vascular auscultation is performed
Troponin assay looks for myocardial necrosis
The ankle-brachial index is the key diagnostic test
body.explanation: Clinical: rule out other chest pain causes, cardiac and vascular auscultation. Paraclinical: ECG, troponin (necrosis), coronary angiography.

title: Which endocarditis lesions are painful?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which endocarditis lesions are painful?
body.explanation: Osler nodes: raised, painful, red, from immune complexes. Janeway lesions: small, red, painless. Splinter haemorrhages: dark lines under nails, from microemboli.
option_notes: Osler nodes are painful immune nodules.
Roth spots are in the retina and painless.

title: The photographs of primary adrenal insufficiency show pigmentation of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The photographs of primary adrenal insufficiency show pigmentation of:
options: The nail beds of the toes
body.explanation: The photos show pigmented tongue and buccal mucosa and pigmented toenail beds, matching the slide: buccal mucosa, gums and nail beds.
option_notes: Correct: buccal mucosa and tongue photo.
Wrong: new scars pigment, old scars do not.

title: About upper GI endoscopy (EGD) in GI bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About upper GI endoscopy (EGD) in GI bleeding:
options: It should be done before any resuscitation
It has diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic roles
It is performed urgently after stabilisation
It is the first-line exam for lower GI bleeding
body.explanation: EGD is first-line in suspected upper GI bleeding, performed urgently after stabilisation, with diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic roles.
option_notes: Wrong: it is done after stabilisation.
Wrong: colonoscopy is key for lower GI bleeding.

title: A 45-year-old woman has fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, hoarseness, puffy face, dry coarse skin, bradycardia, delayed ankle-jerk relaxati…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 45-year-old woman has fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, hoarseness, puffy face, dry coarse skin, bradycardia, delayed ankle-jerk relaxation and a neck swelling. Regarding the diagnosis:
options: Hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto thyroiditis is the most likely diagnosis
Graves' disease is likely, given the goitre
Thyroid carcinoma is the most likely diagnosis
body.explanation: All features are hypothyroid (hypometabolism, bradycardia, delayed reflexes) with a goitre; Hashimoto is the common autoimmune cause.
option_notes: Correct: classic hypothyroid picture with goitre.
Wrong: Graves' gives weight loss, heat intolerance, tachycardia.
Wrong: de Quervain has a painful tender thyroid and fever.
Wrong: cancer presents as a nodule, not hypometabolism.

title: In which condition must lymph nodes be reported?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In which condition must lymph nodes be reported?
body.explanation: Report adenopathy in tuberculosis, haematological malignancy and sarcoidosis.

title: Endoscopic haemostasis techniques include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Endoscopic haemostasis techniques include:
body.explanation: Endoscopic haemostasis: injection (adrenaline, sclerosant), thermal coagulation, haemoclips, variceal band ligation. Surgery is for refractory bleeding or perforation.
option_notes: Wrong: surgery is reserved for refractory bleeding or perforation.

title: Graves' disease predominantly affects people aged:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Graves' disease predominantly affects people aged:
body.explanation: Epidemiology slide: Graves disease predominantly affects those aged 20-40 years; overall hyperthyroidism incidence rises with age.
option_notes: Wrong: toxic multinodular goitre is the older-patient cause.

title: According to the slides, T4 increases:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the slides, T4 increases:
body.explanation: The slide lists T4: + lipolysis, + intestinal peristaltism, + nervous excitability, + proteic catabolism (muscle loss).

title: Mineralocorticoids:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Mineralocorticoids:
options: Act mainly on water and electrolyte metabolism
Cause Na+ excretion and K+ retention
Have a minor role compared with gonadal hormones
body.explanation: Mineralocorticoids act on water and electrolyte metabolism (+++): Na+ reabsorption, K+ excretion and acid-base balance.
option_notes: Wrong: reverse - Na+ reabsorption and K+ excretion.

title: On the pituitary physiology reminder diagram, prolactin acts on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the pituitary physiology reminder diagram, prolactin acts on:
body.explanation: The diagram shows prolactin going to the mammary glands; TSH to thyroid, ACTH to adrenal cortex, FSH/LH to gonads.
option_notes: Thyroid is the target of TSH.
Adrenal cortex is the target of ACTH.
Correct: prolactin targets the mammary glands.
Gonads are the targets of FSH and LH.

title: Normal thyroid dimensions on ultrasound per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Normal thyroid dimensions on ultrasound per the slides:
options: A thickness above 2.5 cm suggests goitre
Lobe height 10-12 cm, with a thickness up to 4 cm being normal
body.explanation: Normal dimensions: height 4-6 cm, width 1.5-2.5 cm, thickness 1.5-2.5 cm; if >2.5 cm, goitre.

title: Which are thoracic deformities? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are thoracic deformities? (choose all)
body.explanation: Pectus excavatum (funnel), carinatum (keel) and arcuatum (wave).

title: What is the atrial rate in atrial flutter?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the atrial rate in atrial flutter?
body.explanation: Flutter: 250 to 350, organised re-entrant circuit. AFib: 350 to 600, chaotic.
option_notes: Flutter is an organised circuit at 250 to 350.
This is a normal sinus rate.

title: Which causes carry the worst prognosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which causes carry the worst prognosis?
body.explanation: Along with severity, comorbidities and delay.
option_notes: Variceal and malignant bleeding carry the worst prognosis.
Erosive gastritis usually stops by itself.

title: Fat-soluble vitamins whose deficiency may occur in cholestasis include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Fat-soluble vitamins whose deficiency may occur in cholestasis include:
body.explanation: The slide lists symptoms of liposoluble vitamins ADEK.

title: Capillary blood glucose is defined as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Capillary blood glucose is defined as:
options: Glucose measured in a capillary vessel
A laboratory measurement of venous HbA1c
body.explanation: Examination slide: capillary blood glucose = measurement of glucose level in a capillary vessel, done with glucose meters.
option_notes: Wrong: that is a urine test.
Wrong: HbA1c is a lab criterion.
Wrong: OGTT is a separate diagnostic test.

title: Which bone disease occurs in Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which bone disease occurs in Cushing's syndrome?
body.explanation: Hypercortisolism causes osteoporosis.
option_notes: Osteopetrosis is an excess of bone density.
Paget's disease is not caused by cortisol.
Rickets comes from vitamin D deficiency in children.

title: What is the ECG hallmark of atrial fibrillation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the ECG hallmark of atrial fibrillation?
body.explanation: AFib: absent P waves and irregularly irregular QRS spacing. Flutter: sawtooth F waves.
option_notes: No P waves and irregular QRS spacing.

title: Cholestatic jaundice with dilated bile ducts on ultrasound:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cholestatic jaundice with dilated bile ducts on ultrasound:
options: May be due to biliary lithiasis
body.explanation: Dilated bile ducts: yes = extrahepatic (obstructive), e.g. biliary lithiasis; no = intrahepatic, e.g. chronic liver disease.
option_notes: That is when ducts are not dilated.

title: According to the lecture, nausea typically originates from:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture, nausea typically originates from:
body.explanation: Nausea typically originates from the gastrointestinal tract or the central nervous system.

title: Which is a metabolic cause of hepatomegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a metabolic cause of hepatomegaly?
body.explanation: Metabolic: steatosis, Wilson's, haemochromatosis, Gaucher. Congestion: heart failure, Budd-Chiari.
option_notes: Iron overload is a metabolic cause.
Hepatitis B is an infectious cause.
A metastasis is a tumoural cause.

title: The three levels of diagnosis in GI bleeding are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The three levels of diagnosis in GI bleeding are:
options: Positive diagnosis: confirming the bleeding is digestive
Topographic diagnosis: identifying the underlying disease
Etiological diagnosis: identifying the underlying lesion or disease
Topographic diagnosis: upper versus lower GI origin
body.explanation: Positive diagnosis confirms bleeding is digestive; topographic diagnosis determines upper vs lower origin; etiological diagnosis identifies the lesion or disease.
option_notes: Wrong: that is the etiological diagnosis.

title: What is the most frequent anatomical cause of GERD?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the most frequent anatomical cause of GERD?
body.explanation: Hiatal hernia is the most frequent anatomical cause.
option_notes: Zenker's diverticulum is a pharyngeal pouch.
Achalasia is a failure of LES relaxation, the opposite problem.
Hiatal hernia displaces the LES from the crura.
Pyloric stenosis causes vomiting, not reflux through a weak LES.

title: Glomerular changes of diabetic kidney disease shown on the physiopathology figure include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Glomerular changes of diabetic kidney disease shown on the physiopathology figure include:
options: Podocyte proliferation with increased slit diaphragms
body.explanation: Figure b shows basement membrane thickening, arteriole hyalinosis, mesangial matrix deposition, podocytopathy (loss, effacement, fewer slit diaphragms), albuminuria.
option_notes: Podocyte loss and fewer slit diaphragms.

title: A patient with acromegaly has night-time tingling of the hand. Regarding this complaint:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with acromegaly has night-time tingling of the hand. Regarding this complaint:
options: It fits carpal tunnel syndrome from median nerve compression
It is caused by ulnar nerve entrapment
It comes from neural enlargement and wrist tissue swelling
body.explanation: Neural enlargement and wrist tissue swelling lead to carpal tunnel syndrome in up to half of patients, with painful median nerve compression and acroparaesthesias.
option_notes: Wrong: the median nerve is involved.
Wrong: up to half of all patients.

title: What is tenesmus?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is tenesmus?
body.explanation: A repeated, painful urge to defecate with no stool, as if evacuation were incomplete.
option_notes: Blood in the stool is rectorrhagia or haematochezia.
Tenesmus is a painful urge to defecate with nothing to pass.

title: According to the introduction slide, jaundice:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the introduction slide, jaundice:
options: Is typically defined by bilirubin above 35 umol/L
Is a symptom of a wide range of diseases
Is a single disease of the liver
body.explanation: Jaundice = excess bilirubin (typically >35 umol/L), a symptom of many diseases needing a structured aetiological strategy.
option_notes: It is a symptom, not one disease.

title: Hyperpigmentation in primary adrenal insufficiency:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hyperpigmentation in primary adrenal insufficiency:
options: Is accentuated over knuckles, toes, elbows and knees
Appears in scars formed after the onset of ACTH excess
Appears in old scars formed before the disease
body.explanation: Predominant in sun-exposed areas and pressure areas; scars formed after the onset of ACTH excess become pigmented, older ones do not; it also affects buccal mucosa and gums.
option_notes: Wrong: buccal mucosa and gums are pigmented.

title: A woman has a dull, rounded swelling above the pubis on percussion that disappears after she passes urine. What was it?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A woman has a dull, rounded swelling above the pubis on percussion that disappears after she passes urine. What was it?
body.explanation: The abdomen is tympanic except the right hypochondrium (liver) and the hypogastrium when the bladder is full.
option_notes: A full bladder makes the hypogastrium dull; emptying it removes the dullness.
Ascites gives dullness in the flanks and does not vanish after voiding.
The liver lies in the right hypochondrium.
Gas gives a tympanic, not dull, sound.

title: About slow colonic transit:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About slow colonic transit:
options: Stool moves slowly through the colon
It is synonymous with outlet dysfunction
It may be associated with hyperspasticity and increased secondary contractions
It is mainly caused by failure of the pelvic floor to relax
body.explanation: Slow transit = delayed movement of stool through the colon, often with reduced motility or hyperspasticity with increased secondary colonic contractions.
option_notes: Wrong: outlet dysfunction is the other, distinct mechanism of primary constipation.
Correct: hyperspasticity is also possible (spastic colon).
Wrong: pelvic floor failure to relax is outlet dysfunction.

title: Symptoms of diabetic nephropathy shown on the infographic include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms of diabetic nephropathy shown on the infographic include:
options: Swelling of ankles, hands, feet or eyes
body.explanation: Listed symptoms: worsening BP regulation, proteinuria, swelling, increased urge to urinate, dyspnoea, loss of appetite, nausea, itching, exhaustion.
option_notes: Loss of appetite is listed instead.

title: Acute complications of diabetes include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Acute complications of diabetes include:
body.explanation: Acute: DKA, hypoglycaemia, hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state, lactic acidosis. Chronic: degenerative complications such as retinopathy.

title: A thyrotoxic patient has lost muscle bulk. According to the slides, which action of T4 explains this?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A thyrotoxic patient has lost muscle bulk. According to the slides, which action of T4 explains this?
body.explanation: T4 increases protein catabolism, causing muscle loss (amyotrophy). Lipolysis explains the fat loss, peristalsis the soft stools and nervous excitability the tremor and irritability.
option_notes: Lipolysis explains fat loss, not muscle loss.
Nervous excitability explains tremor and irritability.

title: Which facial finding points to acromegaly rather than to hypothyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which facial finding points to acromegaly rather than to hypothyroidism?
body.explanation: Downward and forward growth of the mandible (prognathism) with teeth separation and malocclusion is acromegalic. Puffy face and eyelids, eyebrow loss and dry coarse skin are hypothyroid features.
option_notes: Forward jaw growth with teeth separation is acromegalic.
Loss of the outer eyebrows is hypothyroid.
Dry, coarse skin is hypothyroid; acromegalic skin is oily and sweaty.

title: Cushing's is suspected in a patient with morbid obesity, alcoholism and depression. Which confirmation test is optimal for them?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cushing's is suspected in a patient with morbid obesity, alcoholism and depression. Which confirmation test is optimal for them?
options: Low-dose dexamethasone test, 2 mg/day for 48 h
body.explanation: The low-dose test (2 mg/day for 48 h) is the optimal test for patients with psychiatric problems, morbid obesity or alcoholism.
option_notes: The optimal test in psychiatric illness, morbid obesity or alcoholism.
The 1 mg test gives more false positives in these patients.
A single morning cortisol is not enough.

title: Pyrosis (heartburn) is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Pyrosis (heartburn) is characterised by:
options: Retrosternal burning rising from the epigastrium to the throat
Triggering by bending forward or lying down
Burning descending from the throat to the epigastrium
body.explanation: Pyrosis is a retrosternal burning rising from the epigastrium to the throat, often postprandial or nocturnal, triggered by bending forward, lying down or heavy meals, and may be relieved by antacids.
option_notes: Correct: posture is a classic trigger.
Correct: may be relieved by antacids.
Wrong: the burning rises, it does not descend.

title: A 45-year-old man with acromegaly snores loudly and is sleepy during the day. Which manifestation is this?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 45-year-old man with acromegaly snores loudly and is sleepy during the day. Which manifestation is this?
options: Sleep apnoea, a respiratory manifestation of acromegaly
body.explanation: Respiratory manifestations of acromegaly: sleep apnoea (macroglossia and soft tissue thickening narrow the airway).
option_notes: Macroglossia and thick soft tissues narrow the airway.
Apoplexy is a sudden headache with visual loss.
Central hypothyroidism does not cause snoring this way.

title: What are Roth spots a classic sign of?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What are Roth spots a classic sign of?
body.explanation: Retinal red rings with a white centre, seen in only about 2 percent of endocarditis.
option_notes: Heart failure does not give Roth spots.
Roth spots are retinal haemorrhages of endocarditis.

title: Why is urine dark in cholestatic jaundice?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is urine dark in cholestatic jaundice?
options: Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble and passes into the urine
Unconjugated bilirubin passes freely into the urine
body.explanation: Dark urine is part of the cholestasis syndrome: conjugated bilirubin backs up into the blood and, being water-soluble, is filtered into the urine.
option_notes: Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble and filtered by the kidney.
Unconjugated bilirubin is bound to albumin and does not reach urine.

title: Features of subacute de Quervain thyroiditis listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Features of subacute de Quervain thyroiditis listed in the lecture include:
body.explanation: Self-limited thyroid inflammation; key factors: neck pain, tender firm enlarged thyroid, fever, palpitations; other factors: recent viral infection, myalgia, malaise, tremor.
option_notes: Correct: neck pain is a key diagnostic factor.
Wrong: it is painful; exophthalmos suggests Graves'.

title: Which drug can raise prolactin?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drug can raise prolactin?
body.explanation: Dopamine antagonists raise prolactin: phenothiazines, haloperidol, risperidone, metoclopramide.
option_notes: A dopamine antagonist, so it raises prolactin.

title: About colonoscopy in the work-up of constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About colonoscopy in the work-up of constipation:
options: It allows direct visualisation of the colon with biopsies if needed
It can identify polyps or strictures
It is a functional test for primary constipation
body.explanation: Colonoscopy, an initial test to rule out organic disease, directly visualises the colon to identify polyps, strictures; biopsies can be taken.
option_notes: Wrong: it is an initial test to rule out organic disease.

title: Regarding the types of GI bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the types of GI bleeding:
options: Melena is the vomiting of digested blood
Occult bleeding is always visible in the stools
Haematochezia is the emission of bright red blood from the anus
Haematemesis is the passage of black stools
body.explanation: Haematemesis = vomiting of blood; melena = black tarry digested blood in stools; haematochezia = bright red blood from the anus; occult bleeding is revealed only by anaemia or a positive FOBT.
option_notes: Wrong: melena is black tarry stools.
Wrong: occult bleeding is microscopic, revealed by anaemia or FOBT.
Wrong: haematemesis is vomiting of blood.

title: According to the pathophysiology diagram, glucocorticoid excess causes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the pathophysiology diagram, glucocorticoid excess causes:
body.explanation: The diagram lists eye: glaucoma; GI tract: peptic ulcerations; growth: decreased linear growth; bone: decreased bone formation and mass, osteoporosis.
option_notes: Wrong: bone formation and bone mass decrease.

title: A lump sensation in the throat without real difficulty swallowing is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A lump sensation in the throat without real difficulty swallowing is:
body.explanation: Always clarify what the patient means.
option_notes: Aphagia is total inability to swallow.
Globus is a lump sensation without real difficulty.

title: A man with cirrhosis, ascites and spider angiomas vomits a large amount of blood. What is the most likely source?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man with cirrhosis, ascites and spider angiomas vomits a large amount of blood. What is the most likely source?
body.explanation: Signs of liver disease or portal hypertension point to varices, which carry one of the worst prognoses.
option_notes: A fissure gives minor rectal bleeding.

title: What is the most characteristic GERD symptom?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the most characteristic GERD symptom?
body.explanation: Retrosternal burning rising to the throat, postprandial or nocturnal, triggered by bending or lying.
option_notes: Diarrhoea is not a reflux symptom.
Retrosternal burning rising to the throat is the hallmark.
Coughing up blood is a respiratory sign.
Dysphagia is an alarm sign, not the typical symptom.

title: A patient's blood glucose is 1.6 g/L. Should glucose appear in the urine?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient's blood glucose is 1.6 g/L. Should glucose appear in the urine?
options: No, glycosuria starts above about 1.8 g/L
Yes, any value above 1.26 g/L causes glycosuria
body.explanation: Glucose passes into the urine once blood sugar exceeds about 1.8 g/L, the threshold of tubular reabsorption.
option_notes: Below the renal threshold of about 1.8 g/L, there is no glycosuria.
1.26 g/L is the diagnostic threshold, not the renal one.
1.10 g/L is the normal fasting limit.
Glycosuria depends on blood glucose, not HbA1c.

title: Why is mucociliary clearance impaired in smokers?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is mucociliary clearance impaired in smokers?
body.explanation: Clearance is reduced by smoking and in bronchiectasis, chronic bronchitis, cystic fibrosis and primary ciliary dyskinesia.
option_notes: Smoking does not dry the pleura.
Smoke paralyses and destroys the cilia.

title: In the 'hyperthyroidism versus thyrotoxicosis' table, which condition gives thyrotoxicosis WITHOUT hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the 'hyperthyroidism versus thyrotoxicosis' table, which condition gives thyrotoxicosis WITHOUT hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: In thyroiditis the gland is not overproducing: hormone leaks out of damaged cells, so there is thyrotoxicosis without hyperthyroidism. Graves', toxic adenoma and toxic nodular goitre are true hyperthyroidism.
option_notes: Graves' disease is true hyperthyroidism (the gland overproduces).
Hormone leaks out of damaged cells, so the gland is not overproducing.
Toxic nodular goitre is true hyperthyroidism.

title: A peptic stricture typically presents with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A peptic stricture typically presents with:
options: Long reflux history, slow progression, mainly solids
Nasal regurgitation and cough at every meal
Paradoxical dysphagia from the very start
Sudden aphagia after eating a piece of meat
body.explanation: General state initially preserved.
option_notes: Reflux slowly narrows the oesophagus, so solids stick first.
This is a food bolus impaction.

title: The clinical assessment of diabetic neuropathy includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The clinical assessment of diabetic neuropathy includes:
options: Scores such as the DN4 questionnaire and Toronto score
Vibration sensation with a 128-Hz tuning fork
Vibration sensation with a 512-Hz tuning fork
body.explanation: Assessment: history, symptoms with DN4/Toronto, autonomic signs, then temperature, pinprick and vibration with a 128-Hz tuning fork.
option_notes: Not part of the assessment shown.

title: Investigation findings supporting Graves' disease include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Investigation findings supporting Graves' disease include:
options: Anti-TPO antibodies, which are described as the highly specific marker of the disease
Enlarged thyroid volume with 'hell-like' vascularisation on ultrasound
A fairly symmetric gland with very homogeneous tracer distribution on scintigraphy
body.explanation: Graves': TRAb highly specific; ultrasound shows enlarged volume with hell-like vascularisation; scintigraphy shows an enlarged symmetric gland with homogeneous tracer uptake.
option_notes: Wrong: TSH-receptor antibodies are the specific ones.
Correct: symmetric gland, homogeneous tracer distribution.

title: Conditions for measuring the aldosterone/renin ratio:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Conditions for measuring the aldosterone/renin ratio:
options: Stopping antihypertensives that interfere with the renin-angiotensin system
body.explanation: Conditions: normal sodium diet, discontinuation of anti-HTA drugs interfering with the renin-angiotensin system, fasting morning sample.
option_notes: Wrong: the diet must be normo-sodium.

title: Which causes intense liver pain?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which causes intense liver pain?
body.explanation: Abscess: localised, firm, smooth, intensely painful.
option_notes: An abscess is a localised, intensely painful liver.

title: A 25-year-old woman has had morning vomiting for two weeks. Which test should be part of the first work-up?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 25-year-old woman has had morning vomiting for two weeks. Which test should be part of the first work-up?
body.explanation: Morning vomiting is often seen in pregnancy, and hCG is an initial test in women of reproductive age.
option_notes: Correct: initial test in a woman of reproductive age.

title: On the chart, hepatocellular injury with AST:ALT > 2 suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the chart, hepatocellular injury with AST:ALT > 2 suggests:
body.explanation: AST:ALT > 2: alcoholic liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma, early viral hepatitis (per chart).
option_notes: Per the lecture slides (chart); some textbooks say an AST:ALT ratio > 2 points mainly to alcohol, while viral hepatitis usually has ALT > AST.

title: An HbA1c of 6.0% means:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An HbA1c of 6.0% means:
body.explanation: Normal below 5.7%, prediabetes 5.7 to 6.4%, diabetes 6.5% or more.

title: What Lovibond angle indicates clubbing?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What Lovibond angle indicates clubbing?
body.explanation: A Lovibond angle of 180 degrees or more; in the Schamroth test the diamond window between opposed nails disappears.
option_notes: A normal angle is under 180 degrees.
A normal angle is under 180 degrees.

title: A man with known acromegaly develops headaches and loses the outer half of both visual fields. What has happened?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man with known acromegaly develops headaches and loses the outer half of both visual fields. What has happened?
options: The GH-secreting tumour has grown above the sella and compresses the optic chiasm
The tumour has spread into the cavernous sinus
body.explanation: Suprasellar extension compresses the optic chiasm (optic-chiasmatic syndrome): bitemporal visual field loss.
option_notes: Upward growth compresses the chiasm: bitemporal loss.
Cavernous sinus spread gives diplopia and ptosis.
Apoplexy is sudden, with severe headache and ophthalmoplegia.
Retinopathy does not give bitemporal loss.

title: Indications for a work-up in constipation include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Indications for a work-up in constipation include:
options: Need to differentiate slow transit from outlet dysfunction
A single episode of hard stool
body.explanation: Indications: persistent/chronic constipation, failure of initial treatment, differentiating types, and alarm symptoms.

title: How is exudative diarrhoea diagnosed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is exudative diarrhoea diagnosed?
body.explanation: Protein loss into the gut, from lymphangiectasia, lymphoma, cirrhosis, UC.
option_notes: This measures protein lost into the gut.

title: Measuring blood glucose in a vomiting patient mainly rules out:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Measuring blood glucose in a vomiting patient mainly rules out:
body.explanation: Glucose levels: rule out diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

title: A pregnancy test (hCG) in vomiting is indicated:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A pregnancy test (hCG) in vomiting is indicated:
options: Only if the vomiting occurs during meals
Only if the patient is over 50
body.explanation: Pregnancy test (hCG): in women of reproductive age.
option_notes: Wrong: not a condition on the slide.
Wrong: that suggests a psychogenic cause.
Wrong: no such age condition on the slide.

title: Type 1 diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Type 1 diabetes:
options: Is due to beta-cell destruction by autoantibodies
Becomes apparent after about 90% of beta cells are destroyed
Is mainly caused by insulin resistance linked to android obesity
body.explanation: Type 1: total insulin deficiency from autoimmune destruction of beta cells; occurs after 90% of beta cells are destroyed.
option_notes: Wrong: insulin resistance is a type 2 mechanism.

title: Jaundice is defined as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Jaundice is defined as:
options: Yellow discolouration of the sclera and/or skin
body.explanation: Jaundice = excess bilirubin with yellow discolouration of the sclera and/or skin; it is a symptom of many diseases, not a disease itself.
option_notes: Viral hepatitis is only one possible cause.
Pruritus is an associated cholestasis symptom.

title: How does the asthenia of adrenal insufficiency typically behave?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How does the asthenia of adrenal insufficiency typically behave?
options: It increases during the day, peaks in the evening and with effort
It is worst on waking and improves during the day
body.explanation: Asthenia (physical, psychological and sexual) increases during the day and is maximal in the evening and during effort.
option_notes: Worse as the day goes on and with effort.
Morning-worst fatigue is not the AI pattern.
It is a constant symptom, not only with fever.
It is physical, psychological and sexual, with an organic cause.

title: Steps of the proctological examination include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Steps of the proctological examination include:
options: Inspection of the anal area and skin
body.explanation: The proctological exam includes inspection (anal area, skin) and digital examination.

title: Regarding constipation as a complaint:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding constipation as a complaint:
options: It is one of the most common gastrointestinal complaints
It is subdivided into primary and secondary forms
It is a rare complaint with a single etiology
Its evaluation does not require a systematic approach
body.explanation: Constipation is one of the most common GI complaints, with several subtypes (primary/secondary; slow transit/outlet dysfunction) and several etiologies; a systematic approach leads to diagnosis.
option_notes: Correct: one of the subtype pairs.
Wrong: a systematic approach leads to effective diagnosis.

title: Acetone breath and deep, fast (Kussmaul) breathing point to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Acetone breath and deep, fast (Kussmaul) breathing point to:
body.explanation: Shown in red on the symptom diagram (more common in type 1): smell of acetone and Kussmaul breathing are signs of ketoacidosis.
option_notes: Ketone bodies give the acetone smell; acidosis drives Kussmaul breathing.
Hypoglycaemia gives sweating and tremor, not acetone breath.
Heart failure gives dyspnoea, not acetone breath.

title: Which features suggest type 1 diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which features suggest type 1 diabetes?
options: Acute onset in a young person
body.explanation: Type 1: acute onset, under 40, hyperglycaemia symptoms, normal to thin, ketosis at onset, autoimmune history, no cardiovascular risk factors.
option_notes: Type 1 usually starts acutely in young people.
Patients are normal weight or thin.

title: Examples of upper GI endoscopy findings given in the lecture's diagnostic approach:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Examples of upper GI endoscopy findings given in the lecture's diagnostic approach:
body.explanation: The lecture's endoscopy examples are erosions, gastric ulcer, gastric cancer and pylorus obstruction. Cholecystitis is looked for with abdominal ultrasound, not endoscopy.
option_notes: Correct: endoscopy example in the lecture.
Correct: endoscopy example in the lecture.
Correct: endoscopy example in the lecture.
Wrong: shown by abdominal ultrasound, not endoscopy.

title: In the classification diagram of constipation, dyssynergic defecation belongs to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the classification diagram of constipation, dyssynergic defecation belongs to:
options: Primary colonic disorders of secondary constipation
body.explanation: Primary constipation: IBS-C, slow transit (myopathy, neuropathy), functional defecation disorders -> dyssynergic defecation.
option_notes: Wrong: slow transit splits into myopathy and neuropathy.
Wrong: neurologic: Parkinson, spinal cord injury, diabetes.

title: Which test diagnoses dyssynergic defecation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test diagnoses dyssynergic defecation?
body.explanation: Anorectal manometry measures anal and rectal pressures to diagnose outlet dysfunction.
option_notes: Manometry measures anal and rectal pressures.
Thyroid tests look for a secondary cause.
A blood count looks for anaemia.

title: Haemolytic causes on the differential chart include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Haemolytic causes on the differential chart include:
body.explanation: Haemolysis: G6PD, sickle cell anaemia, AIHA, MAHA.

title: A patient with long-standing hypothyroidism has a pericardial effusion on echocardiography. Per the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with long-standing hypothyroidism has a pericardial effusion on echocardiography. Per the lecture:
options: The effusion is rarely large enough to cause tamponade
It is a sign of thyroid cancer
body.explanation: Myxoedema pericarditis gives an effusion that is rarely large enough to cause tamponade. The other cardiovascular complications are myxoedema cardiomyopathy with heart failure and coronary disease linked to high cholesterol.
option_notes: Myxoedema pericarditis is rarely large enough to cause tamponade.
The effusion is a complication of hypothyroidism, not cancer.
It is listed among the complications of hypothyroidism.

title: What does palpation find in consolidation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does palpation find in consolidation?
body.explanation: Consolidation: increased fremitus, dullness, bronchial breath sounds and crackles.
option_notes: Decreased fremitus is fluid or air.
Absent fremitus is fluid or air.

title: Which germ causes invasive dysenteric diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which germ causes invasive dysenteric diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Invasive: Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter, with bloody mucus, fever, pain, tenesmus.
option_notes: ETEC makes a toxin and gives watery diarrhoea.
Shigella invades the mucosa and gives bloody diarrhoea.

title: How common is type 2 among people with diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How common is type 2 among people with diabetes?
body.explanation: Type 2 is 85 to 90%; type 1 is 10 to 15%.
option_notes: Type 1 and other types make up the rest.

title: What does a thyroid bruit indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does a thyroid bruit indicate?
body.explanation: A thyroid noise indicates abnormally high blood flow, sometimes with a thrill, in hyperthyroidism.
option_notes: Low flow gives no bruit; hypothyroidism is silent on auscultation.
High blood flow through the gland in hyperthyroidism makes the bruit, sometimes with a thrill.
A calcified nodule makes no sound.
A normal thyroid has no bruit.

title: Circumstances of discovery of diabetic coronary artery disease include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Circumstances of discovery of diabetic coronary artery disease include:
options: Acute complications of diabetes or glycaemic imbalance
Typical chest pain as the most common presentation
body.explanation: CoD: atypical pain (epigastric ache, exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, lipothymia), typical pain (uncommon), SMI, acute complications/imbalance, heart failure.

title: Which signs define a pleural fluid effusion? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which signs define a pleural fluid effusion? (choose all)
body.explanation: Dullness, reduced or abolished fremitus and reduced or abolished breath sounds.

title: In the neuropathic foot, deep (proprioceptive) sensation disorders are assessed by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the neuropathic foot, deep (proprioceptive) sensation disorders are assessed by:
body.explanation: Deep (proprioceptive) sensation: reflexes, tuning fork; monofilament tests superficial sensation.
option_notes: Listed on p57; reflexes pictured p56.

title: FSH and LH deficiency in hypopituitarism produces:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: FSH and LH deficiency in hypopituitarism produces:
body.explanation: On the chart FSH, LH deficiency leads to central hypogonadism.

title: What relieves stable angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What relieves stable angina?
body.explanation: Stable angina comes on with exercise or stress and is relieved by rest.
option_notes: Rest lowers oxygen demand and relieves it.
Lying flat does not relieve it.

title: An 80-year-old has painless bright red rectal bleeding. Which exam is key?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An 80-year-old has painless bright red rectal bleeding. Which exam is key?
body.explanation: Colonoscopy is the key exam for lower GI bleeding; in the elderly, polyps or cancer, diverticular disease and angiodysplasia are causes.
option_notes: The key exam for lower GI bleeding.
Bright red blood without shock points lower.
Capsule is for the small bowel if no source is found.
X-ray does not find the lesion.

title: Alarm signs (red flags) in a patient with reflux symptoms include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Alarm signs (red flags) in a patient with reflux symptoms include:
body.explanation: Red flags: dysphagia, odynophagia, GI bleeding (haematemesis, melena), iron deficiency anaemia, weight loss or anorexia, vomiting or signs of obstruction.
option_notes: Wrong: water brash is an ordinary digestive sign.

title: Skin signs sought in a jaundiced patient include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Skin signs sought in a jaundiced patient include:
body.explanation: Dermatological exam: sclera, skin, pruritus lesions, purpura, ecchymoses, spider angioma, palmar erythrosis, gynaecomastia, tattoos.

title: Which stool weight defines diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which stool weight defines diarrhoea?
body.explanation: With frequency over 3/day and water over 90%.
option_notes: Normal stool weight is above this.
Normal stool weight is above this.
Diarrhoea is over 300 g of stool a day.

title: About bilirubin:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About bilirubin:
options: It is an enzyme that helps digest lipids
It is a pigment from haemoglobin breakdown
Its derivatives colour urine and stool
body.explanation: Haemoglobin is degraded to bilirubin, conjugated in the liver, excreted in bile; urobilinogen (urine) and stercobilinogen (stool) derive from it.
option_notes: It is a pigment, not an enzyme.
Conjugated bilirubin goes to bile and gut.

title: About acromegaly:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About acromegaly:
options: It is GH hypersecretion in adults
body.explanation: Acromegaly is GH hypersecretion in adults; the mandible grows downward and forward (prognathism), the supraorbital ridges become prominent and the features coarsen.
option_notes: Wrong: it grows downward and forward (prognathism).

title: The slides describe the classic triad of hypopituitarism as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The slides describe the classic triad of hypopituitarism as:
body.explanation: Slide: 'Triad: pallor, depilation, depigmentation'.
option_notes: Hirsutism and dark skin are the opposite.
Correct: the triad on the slide.

title: Findings at upper GI endoscopy in GERD may include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Findings at upper GI endoscopy in GERD may include:
body.explanation: Endoscopic findings: peptic oesophagitis (erosions, ulcerations), peptic stricture (fibrotic narrowing), Barrett's oesophagus (metaplasia).

title: Features of pituitary apoplexy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Features of pituitary apoplexy:
options: Spontaneous haemorrhagic infarction of a pituitary tumour
It occurs in a normal gland without a tumour
Pituitary function is usually left intact
body.explanation: Apoplexy is spontaneous haemorrhagic infarction of a pituitary tumour, with headache, visual loss, ophthalmoplegia, meningismus and altered consciousness; it often causes pituitary insufficiency.
option_notes: Wrong: it is infarction of a pituitary tumour.
Wrong: it often causes partial or total insufficiency.

title: Acromegalic arthropathy is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Acromegalic arthropathy is:
options: Degenerative arthritis of the spine, hips and knees
Grouped with neural signs as articular and neural manifestations
Limited to the small joints, sparing the spine
body.explanation: Articular and neural manifestations: acromegalic arthropathy is degenerative arthritis of the spine, hips and knees.
option_notes: Wrong: it is described as degenerative.

title: Which clotting risk rises in Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which clotting risk rises in Cushing's syndrome?
body.explanation: There is a high risk of thrombosis.
option_notes: Hypercoagulability raises the risk of thrombosis.
Haemophilia is a congenital factor deficiency.
Bruising comes from fragile capillaries, but the stressed clotting risk is thrombosis.

title: Causes of endogenous Cushing syndrome and their share on the causes chart:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of endogenous Cushing syndrome and their share on the causes chart:
options: Adrenal carcinoma, accounting for 10-20% of cases
body.explanation: The causes chart gives pituitary 60-70%, ectopic hormones 5-10%, adrenal adenoma 10-20% and adrenal carcinoma 5-7%.

title: In the etiological history of GI bleeding, the physician asks about:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the etiological history of GI bleeding, the physician asks about:
options: Sudden or progressive onset, with or without pain
body.explanation: History: past peptic ulcer, liver disease, anticoagulants, NSAIDs, aspirin; onset sudden or progressive, with or without pain; associated asthenia, weight loss, abdominal pain, diarrhoea.

title: About the celiac panel in constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the celiac panel in constipation:
options: It is requested systematically in every patient
It is a functional test of anorectal function
body.explanation: Celiac panel (if indicated): tissue transglutaminase antibodies and total serum IgA.
option_notes: Wrong: it is a lab test to rule out organic disease.

title: Is the normal thyroid visible on inspection?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Is the normal thyroid visible on inspection?
body.explanation: The normal thyroid is not visible; a large goitre may be.
option_notes: A normal thyroid cannot be seen; only a goitre may be visible.
Only an enlarged gland (goitre) can be seen.
Sex does not make a normal gland visible.
Swallowing moves a goitre or nodule up, but a normal gland stays invisible.

title: Which are roles of thoracentesis? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are roles of thoracentesis? (choose all)
body.explanation: Confirm the effusion, show its gross appearance and obtain fluid for analysis.
option_notes: It samples the fluid for tests.

title: Vomiting of clear fluid suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Vomiting of clear fluid suggests:
body.explanation: Clear fluid: acid reflux or regurgitation.

title: Medications that can promote reflux include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Medications that can promote reflux include:
body.explanation: Drugs involved: nitrates, theophylline, anticholinergics, calcium channel blockers, progesterone; sedatives are also cited among causes.
option_notes: Correct: listed on the pathophysiology slide.
Wrong: not cited as lowering LES tone.

title: Regarding alarm signs in GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding alarm signs in GERD:
options: Alarm signs can be managed without endoscopy
body.explanation: Odynophagia is pain during swallowing (dysphagia is difficulty swallowing); the presence of any alarm sign requires endoscopic evaluation.
option_notes: Wrong: any alarm sign requires endoscopy.
Wrong: belching is a common digestive sign.

title: Regarding T3 and T4 production:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding T3 and T4 production:
options: T3 makes up about 1/15 of the produced thyroid hormones
T3 makes up about half of the produced thyroid hormones
T3 is the main thyroid hormone produced
T4 is the main thyroid hormone
body.explanation: T4 is the main thyroid hormone; T3 is 1/15 of the produced thyroid hormones.
option_notes: Correct: T3 is 1/15 of produced hormones.
Wrong: T4 is the main thyroid hormone.
Correct: T4 is the main thyroid hormone.

title: About melena:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About melena:
options: It may originate from the small intestine
It always indicates a lesion above the angle of Treitz
It may originate from the right colon
Charcoal and bismuth can mimic it
body.explanation: Melena usually indicates upper GI bleeding but may also originate from the small intestine or right colon; differential: iron, charcoal, bismuth or certain foods.
option_notes: Wrong: usually upper, but not always.

title: Regarding the pathophysiology and stages of diabetic retinopathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the pathophysiology and stages of diabetic retinopathy:
options: Hyperglycaemia leads to occlusion of retinal vessels
Retinal ischaemia leads to reactive proliferation of neovessels
Stages are non-proliferative, severe non-proliferative and proliferative
Fundus examination is reserved for patients with visual symptoms
body.explanation: Hyperglycaemia occludes retinal vessels; ischaemia drives neovessel proliferation; three stages are listed; screening by fundus is needed as signs are poor.
option_notes: Screening of at-risk asymptomatic patients is required.

title: Which is a left, not right, heart failure sign?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a left, not right, heart failure sign?
body.explanation: Left: pulmonary congestion, orthopnoea, PND, frothy cough. Right: peripheral congestion, oedema, ascites, liver congestion.
option_notes: Nocturnal dyspnoea comes from lung congestion (left).

title: About the diagnosis and management of pituitary apoplexy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the diagnosis and management of pituitary apoplexy:
options: Diagnosis rests on clinical features and pituitary imaging
Early transsphenoidal decompression is done within 8 days
Surgery should wait at least 3 months
body.explanation: Diagnosis is based on clinical features and pituitary imaging; it can cause panhypopituitarism; early transsphenoidal decompression within 8 days is advised.
option_notes: Wrong: diagnosis uses clinical features and pituitary imaging.

title: A patient with Graves' ophthalmopathy notices that his vision is getting blurred and dim, not double. What does this suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with Graves' ophthalmopathy notices that his vision is getting blurred and dim, not double. What does this suggest?
body.explanation: In Graves' ophthalmopathy a decrease in visual acuity means optic neuropathy, the most serious eye sign. Double vision comes from extraocular muscle dysfunction; lid retraction and chemosis do not reduce acuity.
option_notes: Falling visual acuity means optic nerve compression, the most serious eye sign.
Lid retraction does not reduce visual acuity.
Extraocular muscle dysfunction causes double vision, not dim vision.
Chemosis is conjunctival swelling and does not reduce acuity.

title: Which is a sign of right heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a sign of right heart failure?
body.explanation: Right heart failure: jugular distension, dependent oedema, ascites, hepatosplenomegaly, anorexia, GI distress.
option_notes: Frothy sputum is left heart failure.
Venous congestion distends the neck veins.

title: A man with Cushing's syndrome may present with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man with Cushing's syndrome may present with:
body.explanation: Reproductive dysfunction in Cushing's: folliculitis, acne, seborrhoea, hirsutism and alopecia; in men, lower libido, impotence and some gynaecomastia. Pigmented gums belong to primary adrenal insufficiency.
option_notes: Lower libido and impotence are listed in men.
Some gynaecomastia is listed in men.
Acne and seborrhoea are part of the skin changes.
Pigmented gums belong to primary adrenal insufficiency.

title: Systemic features of hypercortisolism shown on the Cushing body diagram include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Systemic features of hypercortisolism shown on the Cushing body diagram include:
options: Poor wound healing and easy bruising
body.explanation: The diagram labels moon face, acne, thin skin, weight gain, striae, pendulous abdomen, muscle weakness, poor wound healing, easy bruising, hypertension, cardiac hypertrophy, high blood sugar, menstrual irregularities, osteoporosis and skin ulcers.

title: HMG with neurological symptoms suggests?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: HMG with neurological symptoms suggests?
body.explanation: Hepatomegaly with neurological signs suggests Wilson's disease, a metabolic cause.
option_notes: Heart failure gives reflux and oedema, not neurological signs.
An abscess gives fever and pain.
Copper deposits in the liver and the brain give both signs.
An adenoma has no neurological signs.

title: What is kyphosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is kyphosis?
body.explanation: Kyphosis: posterior convexity of the dorsal spine. Lordosis: anterior lumbar convexity. Scoliosis: lateral deviation.
option_notes: An anterior lumbar curve is lordosis.
A funnel chest is pectus excavatum.
Kyphosis is a posterior dorsal curve.

title: In the differential diagnosis of vomiting:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the differential diagnosis of vomiting:
options: Gastro-oesophageal regurgitation is backward flow without nausea
Rumination is repeated regurgitation of food into the mouth without nausea
body.explanation: GER: backward flow into the oesophagus without nausea or the feeling of vomiting. Rumination: repeated regurgitation into the mouth without nausea.

title: Conditions clustered with hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Conditions clustered with hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes include:
body.explanation: Type 2 slide: hyperglycaemia with obesity, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, dyslipidaemia.

title: A 40-year-old with no risk factors for cancer has a thyroid nodule graded U2 on ultrasound. What is the next step?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 40-year-old with no risk factors for cancer has a thyroid nodule graded U2 on ultrasound. What is the next step?
body.explanation: U2 means benign. FNAC is done for all U3 to U5 lesions; U1 and U2 lesions need FNAC only if the patient is high risk for malignancy.
option_notes: U2 is benign: no FNAC unless the patient is high risk.
FNAC is for U3 to U5, or U1-U2 in high-risk patients.
Surgery is not indicated for a benign-looking nodule.
TRAb look for Graves' disease, not a nodule's nature.

title: Outlet dysfunction is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Outlet dysfunction is characterised by:
options: Frequent need for a digital maneuver to evacuate
An empty rectum on digital rectal examination
Colonic inertia as its main cause
body.explanation: Outlet dysfunction: difficulty in evacuation, often requires digital maneuver; DRE shows presence of stool.
option_notes: Wrong: DRE shows presence of stool.
Wrong: colonic inertia causes slow transit.

title: Regarding bowel habit in hyperthyroidism:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding bowel habit in hyperthyroidism:
options: Stools are often soft, but true diarrhoea is rare
body.explanation: Thyroid hormones stimulate gut motility: stools are frequently soft, but diarrhoea is rare. Constipation belongs to hypothyroidism.
option_notes: Faster gut motility gives frequent soft stools, but true diarrhoea is rare.
Profuse diarrhoea is not the rule.
Thyroid hormones do change bowel habit.

title: In moderate to severe ketoacidosis:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In moderate to severe ketoacidosis:
options: Kussmaul respiration is tachypnoea with deep inspirations
Mental status ranges from drowsiness to coma
Breathing is slow and shallow, with a long expiratory pause
body.explanation: Signs of acidosis: dehydration, Kussmaul respiration (tachypnoea with deep inspirations), pseudosurgical abdominal pain, altered mental status from drowsiness to coma.
option_notes: Wrong: Kussmaul is fast and deep.

title: Which ECG changes come with the hyperkalaemia of acute adrenal insufficiency?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which ECG changes come with the hyperkalaemia of acute adrenal insufficiency?
options: QRS prolongation and large T waves
body.explanation: Hyperkalaemia in acute AI causes ECG disorders (QRS prolongation, large T waves), with a risk of death.
option_notes: Hyperkalaemia widens QRS and peaks T waves.
Low voltage alone is not the hyperkalaemia pattern.

title: A patient has melena but a normal upper endoscopy. Where else can the blood come from?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient has melena but a normal upper endoscopy. Where else can the blood come from?
options: The rectum, as bright red blood only
body.explanation: Melena usually comes from the upper GI tract, but may also originate from the small intestine or the right colon.
option_notes: Slow small-bowel bleeding is digested into melena.
Right colon bleeding can turn black.
Rectal blood comes out bright red.

title: Above what volume is a female thyroid a goitre?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Above what volume is a female thyroid a goitre?
body.explanation: Goitre: over 18 cm³ in women, over 20 cm³ in men; thickness over 2.5 cm.
option_notes: Above 18 cm³ in women (above 20 cm³ in men) is a goitre.
40 cm³ is clearly a goitre, but the threshold is lower.

title: Which is a GERD alarm sign?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a GERD alarm sign?
body.explanation: Dysphagia, odynophagia, GI bleeding, iron deficiency anaemia, weight loss, vomiting: endoscopy needed.
option_notes: Belching is not an alarm sign.
Dysphagia is an alarm sign needing endoscopy.

title: In the hypo- versus hyperthyroidism table, features common to both include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the hypo- versus hyperthyroidism table, features common to both include:
options: Tremor of the hands and eyelids
body.explanation: Shared row: fatigue, muscle weakness, menstrual irregularity, enlarged thyroid (goitre). Tremor is in the hyperthyroid column.
option_notes: Wrong: tremor is listed for hyperthyroidism only.

title: Haematemesis indicates a lesion above what?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Haematemesis indicates a lesion above what?
body.explanation: Haematemesis points to the upper GI tract, proximal to the angle of Treitz.
option_notes: The rectum is far below; rectal bleeding comes out per anus.
The source can be anywhere above the angle of Treitz, not only the pylorus.
Haematemesis points to a lesion above the angle of Treitz.
The ileocaecal valve is in the lower tract.

title: Which feature suggests dysenteric diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which feature suggests dysenteric diarrhoea?
options: Bloody mucous stools with fever and tenesmus
body.explanation: Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter.
option_notes: Blood, mucus, fever and tenesmus mean mucosal invasion.

title: A patient has a pendulous abdomen with stretch marks, a moon face, muscle weakness and easy bruising. Per the slides, investigate:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient has a pendulous abdomen with stretch marks, a moon face, muscle weakness and easy bruising. Per the slides, investigate:
body.explanation: These are Cushing features; the slide says 'LOOK for Cortisol/ACTH axis'.
option_notes: Correct: Cushing features point to the cortisol/ACTH axis.
GH excess gives acromegalic features, not striae and moon face.
Prolactin excess gives galactorrhoea and hypogonadism.

title: Per the slides, type 1 diabetes typically features:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Per the slides, type 1 diabetes typically features:
options: A vital and definitive need for insulin therapy
Chronic complications assessed already at discovery
body.explanation: Type 1: acute onset, young, normal/thin, ketosis at onset, no family history, autoimmune history, no CV factors, vital definitive insulin; chronic complications assessed later.
option_notes: Correct: vital and definitive insulin therapy.
Wrong: assessed 'after'; at discovery is type 2.

title: Which patient features are listed as alarm symptoms?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which patient features are listed as alarm symptoms?
options: Persistent vomiting with inability to maintain oral intake
Vomiting relieved by changing head position
body.explanation: Elderly age, fever and persistent vomiting with inability to keep oral intake are alarm symptoms.

title: A known type 2 diabetic presents in ketoacidosis. What is the most likely explanation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A known type 2 diabetic presents in ketoacidosis. What is the most likely explanation?
options: An additional factor, such as an infection or intercurrent illness
Type 2 diabetes usually begins with ketoacidosis
body.explanation: In type 2 diabetes ketosis is usually absent; ketoacidosis occurs if there is an additional factor (infection, intercurrent disease). The lecture's conclusion: type 2 diabetes has no inaugural ketoacidosis.
option_notes: Ketoacidosis in type 2 needs an added factor such as infection.
Exercise is not the listed trigger.
Diet is not the listed trigger.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Secretory diarrhoea. Active secretion; persists during fasting (IBD, endocrine tumours, drugs).
option_notes: Another box. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.
This is the box at the arrow. Secretory: persists during fasting.
Another box. Malabsorptive: greasy, pale, foul stools.

title: On the ultrasound U-score for thyroid nodules:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the ultrasound U-score for thyroid nodules:
body.explanation: U1 normal, U2 benign, U3 indeterminate/equivocal, U4 suspicious, U5 malignant.

title: A patient with GERD-like symptoms has a normal endoscopy. Which test can confirm acid reflux?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with GERD-like symptoms has a normal endoscopy. Which test can confirm acid reflux?
body.explanation: A normal endoscopy does not exclude GERD (NERD). pH-metry, the reference test, is particularly useful in NERD.
option_notes: The reference test, useful in NERD.
A barium swallow looks for stricture or hernia.
Repeating endoscopy will not show NERD.

title: What prevents reflux at rest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What prevents reflux at rest?
body.explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter and the diaphragmatic crura form the anti-reflux barrier.
option_notes: The pylorus controls gastric emptying, not reflux.
The LES and the diaphragmatic crura form the anti-reflux barrier.
Saliva clears acid but does not prevent reflux.
The upper sphincter is not the main barrier.

title: Secretions of the adrenal cortex listed in the steroidogenesis reminder:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Secretions of the adrenal cortex listed in the steroidogenesis reminder:
body.explanation: The cortex produces 3 types of secretions: glucocorticoids (cortisol, deoxycortisol), mineralocorticoids (aldosterone, corticosterone) and androgens.
option_notes: Correct: as listed on the slide.
Correct: as listed on the slide (per the slides; textbooks note corticosterone also has glucocorticoid activity).
Wrong: catecholamines are medullary; the third cortical type is androgens.
Wrong: norepinephrine is a medullary catecholamine.

title: Which other symptoms can reveal diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which other symptoms can reveal diabetes?
body.explanation: Weight loss, polyuria and polydipsia, blurred vision, nausea or abdominal pain, paresthesia, fatigue, slow-healing cuts.
option_notes: Slow-healing cuts and sores are listed.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Anti-reflux barrier. The lower oesophageal sphincter and diaphragmatic crura prevent reflux at rest.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: What is a primary pneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is a primary pneumothorax?
body.explanation: Primary (primitive): no clinical or radiological lesion. Secondary: pre-existing lung damage.
option_notes: No underlying lung disease is found.

title: How does left heart failure strain the right ventricle?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How does left heart failure strain the right ventricle?
body.explanation: Backed-up blood raises pulmonary artery pressure, so the right ventricle must pump harder.
option_notes: Raised pulmonary pressure makes the right ventricle work harder.
The aorta is on the left side.
The coronaries are not blocked by this.

title: On CT, autoimmune adrenal insufficiency shows:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On CT, autoimmune adrenal insufficiency shows:
options: A small adrenal with cortical retraction
body.explanation: CT in AI assesses adrenal structure and size and tumoral aetiology; the example shows autoimmune involvement: small left adrenal (cortical retraction).
option_notes: Correct: caption of the CT image.

title: Biological clues of adrenal insufficiency include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Biological clues of adrenal insufficiency include:
body.explanation: Other tests: hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypercalcaemia is rare; fasting glucose low-normal; CBC: moderate normochromic normocytic anaemia.

title: A man has chest pain after heavy meals. Cardiac tests are normal, and antacids help. What is the likely explanation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man has chest pain after heavy meals. Cardiac tests are normal, and antacids help. What is the likely explanation?
options: Non-cardiac chest pain from GERD (pseudo-anginal pain)
body.explanation: GERD can cause non-cardiac chest pain that mimics angina; such atypical presentations may mislead the diagnosis.

title: Which way does the trachea move in a large effusion?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which way does the trachea move in a large effusion?
body.explanation: A large effusion opacifies the hemithorax, shifts the mediastinum and deviates the trachea away.
option_notes: Movement toward the lesion is retraction (collapse).

title: Which position is used for rectal examination?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which position is used for rectal examination?
body.explanation: Chest-to-knee or lateral (Sims) position, with gloves and lubricant (slide 18).
option_notes: Prone and flat is not used.
A seated patient cannot be examined rectally.

title: Regarding other tests in GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding other tests in GERD:
options: Manometry evaluates LES pressure and motility disorders
Impedancemetry is the reference test for acid reflux
Barium swallow looks for complications such as stenosis or hernia
body.explanation: Manometry evaluates LES pressure and motility; impedancemetry detects non-acid reflux; barium swallow is used for complications (stenosis, hernia).
option_notes: Wrong: pH-metry is the reference test for acid reflux.
Wrong: metaplasia is seen at endoscopy.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Acute diarrhoea. Under 2 weeks; choleriform (secretory) or dysenteric (invasive).
option_notes: Another box. Osmotic: stops with fasting (lactase deficiency, laxatives).
This is the box at the arrow. Acute: under 2 weeks.
Another box. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.

title: An aphthous ulcer of the oral mucosa may be seen in:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An aphthous ulcer of the oral mucosa may be seen in:
body.explanation: The slide gives aphthous ulcer of the oral mucosa with the example of inflammatory bowel diseases.
option_notes: Portal hypertension gives collateral veins (slide 12), not oral ulcers.
An aortic aneurysm is an auscultation finding (slide 17).

title: Atrophic glossitis is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Atrophic glossitis is characterised by:
options: Vitamin B12 deficiency as an example cause
A white fungal plaque on the tongue
Fissures at the corners of the mouth
body.explanation: Atrophic glossitis = inflammation of the tongue, e.g. vitamin B12 deficiency.

title: In type 2 diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In type 2 diabetes:
options: Ketoacidosis may occur with an additional factor such as infection
Hyperglycaemia symptoms appear mainly if very unbalanced
Insulin secretion is absent, so insulin therapy is vital from diagnosis
body.explanation: Type 2: ketoacidosis only with an additional factor (infection, intercurrent disease); hyperglycaemia symptoms if very unbalanced; insulin secretion persists; ketosis absent.
option_notes: Wrong: no inaugural ketoacidosis in type 2.

title: Regarding non-cholestatic jaundice in the strategy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding non-cholestatic jaundice in the strategy:
options: Haemolysis is the question to ask
body.explanation: Non-cholestatic (unconjugated) -> haemolysis? Corpuscular: usually extravascular; extracorpuscular: usually intravascular (per the slide).
option_notes: Per the lecture slides, extracorpuscular haemolysis is usually intravascular; some textbooks say immune (extracorpuscular) haemolysis is often extravascular.

title: A previously dry 7-year-old starts wetting the bed, drinks a lot and is losing weight. Which bedside tests come first?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A previously dry 7-year-old starts wetting the bed, drinks a lot and is losing weight. Which bedside tests come first?
options: Capillary glucose and a urine strip for glucose and ketones
body.explanation: New bedwetting means polyuria. With thirst and weight loss in a child, check capillary glucose and urine for glycosuria and ketones (type 1 diabetes, risk of ketoacidosis).
option_notes: Confirms hyperglycaemia and looks for ketosis.
Bone age is for growth problems.

title: Which emphysema type is the pink puffer?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which emphysema type is the pink puffer?
body.explanation: Panlobular: pink puffer. Centrilobular: blue bloater.
