option_notes: Chronic bronchitis is the blue bloater.
Panlobular emphysema is the pink puffer.

title: In primary adrenal insufficiency, calcified adrenals on imaging suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In primary adrenal insufficiency, calcified adrenals on imaging suggest:
body.explanation: Per the slides, adrenal tuberculosis shows calcifications on imaging (CT on slide 54); autoimmune Addison's is identified by anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies; bilateral haemorrhage shows large, heterogeneous glands.
option_notes: Wrong: the slides link autoimmune Addison's to anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies, not calcifications.
Wrong: adrenals are not the lesion.

title: Ocular signs of thyrotoxicosis listed with the general hyperthyroid manifestations are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Ocular signs of thyrotoxicosis listed with the general hyperthyroid manifestations are:
options: Retraction of the upper or lower eyelids
Fine tremor of the lightly closed lids
Chemosis with palpebral oedema and scleral injection
body.explanation: Ocular signs of thyrotoxicosis: lid retraction, lid lag, rarity of the blink, fine tremor of lightly closed lids. Chemosis belongs to Graves' ophthalmopathy.
option_notes: Correct: lid retraction is a thyrotoxicosis sign.
Correct: fine tremor of the lightly closed lids.
Wrong: chemosis is listed under Graves' ophthalmopathy.

title: A patient on morphine for cancer pain becomes constipated. How is this classified?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient on morphine for cancer pain becomes constipated. How is this classified?
options: Secondary constipation caused by a medication
body.explanation: Opioids are listed among the medications causing secondary constipation.
option_notes: A drug is an identifiable cause: secondary constipation.
Primary constipation has no identifiable cause.
Outlet dysfunction is a pelvic floor problem.
IBS-C has no organic or drug cause.

title: Which nerve problem affects up to half of patients with acromegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which nerve problem affects up to half of patients with acromegaly?
body.explanation: Soft tissue swelling at the wrist compresses the median nerve: pain and acroparesthesias.
option_notes: Soft tissue swelling at the wrist compresses the median nerve.
Bell's palsy is a facial nerve palsy, not linked to acromegaly.
Peroneal nerve palsy is not the typical nerve problem.

title: Mechanisms of hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes shown in the figure include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Mechanisms of hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes shown in the figure include:
options: Decreased glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue
Decreased renal glucose reabsorption, increasing glucosuria
body.explanation: Figure: increased hepatic glucose production, decreased muscle/adipose uptake, decreased incretin effect and increased glucose reabsorption feed hyperglycaemia.

title: Which hormone is often co-secreted with GH, so is measured too?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which hormone is often co-secreted with GH, so is measured too?
body.explanation: The slide lists prolactin (usual co-secretion) with IGF-1 and GH.
option_notes: Prolactin is usually co-secreted with GH.
ACTH is not co-secreted with GH.
Vasopressin comes from the posterior pituitary.

title: A sweating, tachycardic patient could have phaeochromocytoma or hyperthyroidism. Which finding favours phaeochromocytoma?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A sweating, tachycardic patient could have phaeochromocytoma or hyperthyroidism. Which finding favours phaeochromocytoma?
options: Attacks of headache with very high blood pressure and pallor
body.explanation: Both can cause sweating, palpitations, weight loss and heat intolerance; paroxysmal attacks with headache and BP surges point to phaeochromocytoma.
option_notes: Paroxysmal hypertension with headache is the phaeochromocytoma pattern.

title: Non-surgical acute abdomen causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Non-surgical acute abdomen causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Non-surgical: acute pancreatitis, biliary colic, peptic ulcer disease, acute gastritis. Intestinal obstruction is surgical.

title: When is vesicular breathing mainly heard?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When is vesicular breathing mainly heard?
options: Only at the end of expiration
body.explanation: Vesicular breathing is heard over both lungs, especially in inspiration and early expiration.
option_notes: Heard in inspiration and early expiration.

title: In the thyroid cancer staging figure:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the thyroid cancer staging figure:
options: T1a corresponds to a tumour of 0-1 cm
T2 corresponds to a tumour over 4 cm that is confined to the thyroid
T4a: invasion of other structures, surgery still possible
T1a means invasion of the trachea
body.explanation: Figure: T1a tumour 0-1 cm; T2 tumour 2-4 cm; T4a tumour invasion of other structures with surgical removal still possible.
option_notes: Correct: T4a definition on the figure.
Wrong: T1a is a small intrathyroid tumour.

title: First-step tests showing excessive cortisol secretion or a disturbed rhythm:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: First-step tests showing excessive cortisol secretion or a disturbed rhythm:
options: Serum cortisol cycle with high midnight cortisol
body.explanation: Initial tests: 24 h urinary free cortisol, midnight salivary cortisol, and serum cortisol cycle (high midnight cortisol). ACTH is used later to find the cause.
option_notes: Wrong: ACTH is a cause-finding test.

title: Comorbidities of high cortisol shown on the Lancet slide include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Comorbidities of high cortisol shown on the Lancet slide include:
body.explanation: Comorbidities: hypertension, glucose metabolism impairment, bone disease, infections, hypercoagulability.
option_notes: Cortisol causes glucose metabolism impairment (high sugar), not hypoglycaemia.

title: ACTH deficiency looks like Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) except for the absence of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: ACTH deficiency looks like Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) except for the absence of:
body.explanation: Table: ACTH deficiency is as in Addison's disease except lack of hyperpigmentation and hyperkalaemia; the cartoon says 'all the problems of primary Addison's except dark skin'.
option_notes: Weakness is present (shown on the cartoon).
Absent: no ACTH, so no dark skin.
Weight loss is present (shown on the cartoon).

title: According to the lecture definition, the hyperglycaemia of diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture definition, the hyperglycaemia of diabetes:
options: Results from absolute or relative deficient insulin secretion
May result from deficient insulin action
Is always due to autoimmune destruction of the pancreatic beta cells
body.explanation: Definition: chronic hyperglycaemia due to an absolute or relative deficiency of insulin secretion and/or insulin action (insulin resistance).
option_notes: Correct: absolute or relative secretion deficiency.
Correct: insulin action defect = insulin resistance.
Wrong: autoimmunity applies to type 1 only.

title: A newly diagnosed acromegalic patient: which examination is justified by one of the associations listed in the lecture?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A newly diagnosed acromegalic patient: which examination is justified by one of the associations listed in the lecture?
body.explanation: Gastrointestinal features of acromegaly include colonic polyps, so the colon is explored.
option_notes: Colonic polyps are associated with acromegaly.
The pituitary is imaged with MRI.

title: The adrenal medulla:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The adrenal medulla:
body.explanation: Per the diagram, the medulla (10-20%) contains chromaffin cells secreting catecholamines: epinephrine 80%, norepinephrine 20%.
option_notes: Wrong: weak androgens come from the zona reticularis of the cortex.

title: Which organs are dull to percussion?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which organs are dull to percussion?
body.explanation: Dull: liver, heart. Resonant: gastric air sac, left colonic angle, healthy lung.

title: Symptoms of moderate neuroglucopenia listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms of moderate neuroglucopenia listed in the lecture include:
body.explanation: Moderate neuroglucopenia: dizziness, drowsiness, irritability, confusion, personality changes, difficulty speaking, weakness, headache, blurred vision, impaired judgment.
option_notes: Kussmaul breathing is a sign of ketoacidosis.
Polyuria is a sign of hyperglycaemia.

title: Where is the needle inserted in thoracentesis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where is the needle inserted in thoracentesis?
body.explanation: In the zone of complete dullness, shaving the upper edge of the lower rib to avoid the intercostal bundle.
option_notes: The vessels and nerve run under each rib.
Above the lower rib avoids the intercostal bundle.

title: What are the two mechanisms of primary constipation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What are the two mechanisms of primary constipation?
body.explanation: Primary (functional) constipation: slow colonic transit or outlet dysfunction.
option_notes: These are not mechanisms of primary constipation.
Tumour and stricture cause secondary constipation.
Slow colonic transit or outlet dysfunction.
Drugs and diabetes cause secondary constipation.

title: Vomiting during meals suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Vomiting during meals suggests:
body.explanation: Vomiting during meals: psychogenic cause.

title: A patient taking haloperidol has a prolactin of 60 ng/mL. Per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient taking haloperidol has a prolactin of 60 ng/mL. Per the slides:
options: This level fits drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia, usually 25-100 ng/mL
Any prolactin above 50 ng/mL proves a prolactinoma
Drug-induced values are always above 200 ng/mL
body.explanation: Medication-induced hyperprolactinaemia is usually mild (25 to 100 ng/mL). Haloperidol is a dopamine antagonist listed among the causes.
option_notes: A mild level on a culprit drug does not prove a tumour.
Haloperidol, a dopamine antagonist, raises prolactin.
Only a few drugs (risperidone) push it above 200 ng/mL.

title: TSH deficiency in hypopituitarism:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: TSH deficiency in hypopituitarism:
body.explanation: Table: TSH deficiency is as in primary hypothyroidism, except lack of goitre.
option_notes: No goitre, since TSH drive is missing.

title: Regarding percussion sounds:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding percussion sounds:
options: Tympany is a hollow sound due to air
Dullness indicates a dense organ or fluid
body.explanation: Tympany = hollow sound = air; dull sound = dense organ or fluid.

title: Toxic causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Toxic causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Toxic: drug toxicity (chemotherapy, antibiotics, opioids), alcohol intoxication, toxic ingestion (heavy metals, toxins).

title: An 8 a.m. serum cortisol of 3 ug/dl means:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An 8 a.m. serum cortisol of 3 ug/dl means:
options: Dynamic tests are needed before any conclusion
body.explanation: 8 am cortisol < 5 ug/dl (80 nmol/l) means AI; > 18 ug/dl excludes AI; intermediate values need dynamic tests.
option_notes: Wrong: only intermediate values need them.

title: Which cranial nerves are examined in dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cranial nerves are examined in dysphagia?
body.explanation: Glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory, hypoglossal.
option_notes: V to VIII are mainly face and hearing.
IX to XII control the pharynx, larynx and tongue.
These are smell, vision and eye movements.

title: The foot pulses demonstrated on the peripheral artery disease slide are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The foot pulses demonstrated on the peripheral artery disease slide are:
body.explanation: The PAD slide shows palpation of the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses.

title: A 28-year-old woman on risperidone has galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea. Per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 28-year-old woman on risperidone has galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea. Per the slides:
options: Risperidone is a recognised cause of high prolactin
With risperidone, prolactin may exceed 200 ng/mL
High prolactin always means a prolactinoma
Her symptoms differ from those of a prolactinoma
body.explanation: Risperidone is a dopamine antagonist that can raise prolactin above 200 ng/mL, and PRL excess gives the same features whatever the cause.
option_notes: Wrong: many physiologic, drug and disease causes exist.
Wrong: manifestations are the same regardless of cause.

title: On which side of the patient does the doctor stand?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On which side of the patient does the doctor stand?
body.explanation: The patient lies flat; the doctor stands on the patient's right.
option_notes: The doctor stands on the patient's right.
The convention is the right side.
The head of the bed is not used for abdominal examination.
The foot of the bed is not used.

title: Lab tests for Cushing disease listed on the slides include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Lab tests for Cushing disease listed on the slides include:
options: Evening cortisol on the nycthemeral cycle
GH during a 75 g glucose tolerance test
body.explanation: Lab tests: free urinary/salivary cortisol, nycthemeral cycle with vesperal cortisol, 1 mg overnight dexamethasone test, and ACTH level.
option_notes: Listed: loss of the evening cortisol fall.
The OGTT with GH is the acromegaly work-up.

title: Features labelled on the Cushing syndrome drawing include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Features labelled on the Cushing syndrome drawing include:
body.explanation: The drawing labels thinning of hair, acne, moon face, red cheeks, increased body and facial hair, buffalo hump, thin skin and subcutaneous tissue, easy bruising and slow wound healing.
option_notes: Wrong: the skin and subcutaneous tissue are thin.

title: On ultrasound, a thyroid volume of 19 cm³ means:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On ultrasound, a thyroid volume of 19 cm³ means:
options: A goitre in a woman but not in a man
A goitre in a man but not in a woman
A normal gland in both sexes
body.explanation: Goitre thresholds: volume above 18 cm³ in women and above 20 cm³ in men. So 19 cm³ is a goitre only in a woman.
option_notes: 19 cm³ is above 18 cm³ (women) but below 20 cm³ (men).
The female threshold is the lower one, not the male.
In a man, 19 cm³ is still normal.
19 cm³ is above the female threshold of 18 cm³.

title: On thyroid ultrasound, the nodule characteristics to describe include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On thyroid ultrasound, the nodule characteristics to describe include:
options: Its hot or cold functional status, as judged by tracer uptake
body.explanation: Ultrasound describes nodule size, structure (liquid/solid), margins, vascularisation and calcifications (micro/macro), and searches for lymphadenopathy. Hot/cold is a scintigraphy finding.
option_notes: Correct: US structure liquid or solid.
Correct: aspect of margins and vascularisation.
Wrong: hot/cold nodules are defined on scintigraphy.

title: Which parasite is seen on stool microscopy in amoebic dysentery?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which parasite is seen on stool microscopy in amoebic dysentery?
body.explanation: Stool microscopy looks for RBCs, WBCs, mucus and parasites such as Entamoeba histolytica.
option_notes: Giardia causes watery diarrhoea without blood.
Taenia is a tapeworm, not a cause of dysentery.
Ascaris is a roundworm, not a cause of dysentery.

title: Which is NOT a red flag for dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is NOT a red flag for dysphagia?
options: Iron-deficiency anaemia on the blood count
Intermittent symptoms for 10 years with no weight loss
Age over 50 at the onset of dysphagia
Weight loss of more than 5 kg
body.explanation: The others require urgent referral.
option_notes: Long, stable symptoms without weight loss are reassuring.
Age over 50 is a red flag.
Weight loss over 5 kg is a red flag.

title: Regurgitation in GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regurgitation in GERD:
options: Is preceded by nausea and retching
Produces a hot, bitter taste in the mouth
Requires abdominal muscle effort like vomiting
body.explanation: Regurgitation is the effortless reflux of acidic gastric contents into the mouth, producing a hot, bitter taste and throat burning; often with heartburn, after meals or lying down.
option_notes: Wrong: nausea and retching precede vomiting, not regurgitation.
Correct: hot, bitter taste and throat burning.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Organic dysphagia. Obstruction (tumour, stricture): solids then liquids, constant and progressive.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Organic: solids then liquids, progressive.
Another box. Oesophageal phase: involuntary peristalsis.
Another box. Endoscopy: the first-line test.

title: Associated symptoms to look for in a constipated patient include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Associated symptoms to look for in a constipated patient include:
body.explanation: Associated symptoms: general (weight loss, fatigue), abdominal pain, vomiting, GI bleeding, extra-digestive symptoms.

title: Paradoxical dysphagia (liquids as much as solids) suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Paradoxical dysphagia (liquids as much as solids) suggests:
body.explanation: A motor disorder.
option_notes: Liquids as much as solids means a motor disorder.

title: What ECG change occurs in stable angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What ECG change occurs in stable angina?
body.explanation: Stable and unstable angina: ST depression (subendocardial). Prinzmetal: ST elevation (transmural).
option_notes: Subendocardial ischaemia depresses the ST segment.
ST elevation is transmural (Prinzmetal or infarction).
Q waves mean an old infarction.
Peaked T waves suggest hyperkalaemia or early infarction.

title: When should chronic complications be looked for in type 2 diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When should chronic complications be looked for in type 2 diabetes?
body.explanation: Type 2 is often diagnosed late, so complications are assessed when diabetes is discovered; in type 1, some years after.
option_notes: Type 2 is often diagnosed late, so complications may already exist.
Complications are often silent; screening does not wait for symptoms.

title: A 50-year-old taking NSAIDs for back pain has epigastric pain, vomits blood and then passes black stools. What is the most likely source?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 50-year-old taking NSAIDs for back pain has epigastric pain, vomits blood and then passes black stools. What is the most likely source?
body.explanation: Haematemesis and melena mean an upper GI source; NSAIDs cause peptic ulcers and drug-induced lesions.
option_notes: NSAIDs, epigastric pain, upper bleeding: peptic ulcer.
Haemorrhoids give bright red rectal blood.
Diverticula bleed in the lower tract.
Meckel's affects young patients and the small bowel.

title: Preparation for the proctological examination includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Preparation for the proctological examination includes:
body.explanation: Preparation: explain + consent, intimate calm room; position chest-to-knee or lateral (Sims); gloves + lubricant.

title: About occult or non-externalised bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About occult or non-externalised bleeding:
options: It may originate from any part of the digestive tract
Massive forms can present as shock without visible bleeding
Massive forms can be diagnosed by gastric aspiration or rectal exam
body.explanation: Occult bleeding is minimal chronic loss detected by FOBT or microcytic anaemia, from any part of the tract; massive non-externalised bleeding presents as shock, diagnosed by gastric aspiration or rectal exam.
option_notes: Correct: any level of the tract.

title: What does dysentery reflect?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does dysentery reflect?
body.explanation: It reflects the reaction of the rectum to inflammatory, infectious or neoplastic disorders.
option_notes: Dysentery is the rectum's reaction to inflammation, infection or a tumour.
A kidney stone gives flank colic, not dysentery.

title: Water brash means:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Water brash means:
body.explanation: An 'other digestive sign' of GERD.
option_notes: Nasal regurgitation suggests an oropharyngeal problem.
Water brash is a sudden flow of saliva.

title: Generalised visceromegaly in acromegaly includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Generalised visceromegaly in acromegaly includes:
body.explanation: Slide 17: thyromegaly and enlargement of the salivary glands, with enlargement of other organs (liver, heart, kidney).
option_notes: Wrong: liver, heart and kidneys enlarge.
Wrong: organs enlarge; atrophy is not described.

title: Neuroglycopenic signs of hypoglycaemia include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Neuroglycopenic signs of hypoglycaemia include:
body.explanation: Neuroglycopenic signs: confusion, drowsiness, speech difficulty, weakness, incoordination, headache, visual disturbance, behaviour changes, convulsions, loss of consciousness.
option_notes: Anxiety is listed as an adrenergic sign.

title: Where does systemic venous congestion show first in the neck?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where does systemic venous congestion show first in the neck?
body.explanation: Backed-up systemic venous blood distends the jugular veins.
option_notes: Tracheal shift is a chest sign.

title: Paroxysmal symptoms of phaeochromocytoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Paroxysmal symptoms of phaeochromocytoma:
options: Can be triggered by tumour compression
body.explanation: Paroxysmal symptoms are triggered by tumour compression, variable in frequency, duration and intensity: headaches, palpitations, pallor, profuse sweating, cooling of the extremities.

title: The systematic abdominal examination comprises:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The systematic abdominal examination comprises:
body.explanation: Systematic examination in 4 steps: inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation.

title: About gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in general:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in general:
options: It is an acute, self-limiting condition
It is a chronic and relapsing condition
Its severity depends only on how intense the heartburn is
It results from retrograde flow of gastric contents into the oesophagus
body.explanation: GERD results from retrograde flow of gastric contents into the oesophagus; it is chronic and relapsing, and its severity depends on oesophageal lesions or complications.
option_notes: Wrong: the slide calls it chronic and relapsing.
Correct: chronic and relapsing, affects quality of life.
Wrong: severity depends on lesions/complications (ulcers, stenosis, metaplasia).
Correct: this is the definition of the mechanism.

title: Regulation of cortisol secretion, per the diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regulation of cortisol secretion, per the diagram:
options: Cortisol exerts negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary
body.explanation: Hypothalamus -> CRH -> pituitary -> ACTH -> adrenals -> cortisol, with negative feedback of cortisol; stressors such as hypoglycaemia stimulate the hypothalamus.
option_notes: Correct: two negative feedback loops shown.
Wrong: hypoglycaemia is a stressor that stimulates the axis.

title: What share of cardiovascular disease is due to modifiable risk factors?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What share of cardiovascular disease is due to modifiable risk factors?
body.explanation: Over 70 percent of cardiovascular disease worldwide is caused by modifiable risk factors (PURE study).
option_notes: Over 70% is due to modifiable factors.

title: In diabetes, polydipsia is due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In diabetes, polydipsia is due to:
options: Excess ADH secretion causing water retention
Direct stimulation of the thirst centre by ketones
body.explanation: Hyperglycaemia review of symptoms: polyuria is due to glycosuria (osmotic diuresis) and polydipsia is due to polyuria.
option_notes: Wrong: not the mechanism on the slide.
Wrong: not the mechanism on the slide.
Wrong: not the mechanism on the slide.

title: Results that meet a diagnostic criterion for diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Results that meet a diagnostic criterion for diabetes:
options: Fasting glucose 1.30 g/L on two samples
Random glucose 2.3 g/L in a patient with no symptoms
body.explanation: FPG >=1.26 g/L on 2 samples, A1c >=6.5%, OGTT 2-h >=2 g/L, or random >=2 g/L only with classic symptoms or hyperglycaemic crisis.
option_notes: Wrong: random criterion requires classic symptoms or crisis.

title: Where does dependent oedema occur?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where does dependent oedema occur?
body.explanation: Fluid accumulates under the skin in regions lower than the heart: legs, ankles, arms.
option_notes: The chest wall is not a dependent area.
The scalp and neck are not dependent.
Gravity pulls fluid to areas below the heart.

title: Regarding diabetic neuropathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding diabetic neuropathy:
options: It is a heterogeneous group of disorders with diverse manifestations
It has the same frequency in type 1 as in type 2 diabetes
Diabetics are 15-40 times more likely to require a lower-limb amputation
Peripheral and autonomic forms are always symptomatic
body.explanation: Neuropathy is heterogeneous, equally frequent in T1 and T2, causes high morbidity (15-40x amputation risk), and may be subclinical or symptomatic.

title: The prognosis of GI bleeding depends on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The prognosis of GI bleeding depends on:
options: Variceal causes having a better prognosis than ulcers
The speed and adequacy of management
body.explanation: Prognosis depends on etiology (variceal and malignant causes worse), severity of initial bleeding, comorbidities, and speed and adequacy of management.

title: Gastrointestinal causes of secondary constipation include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Gastrointestinal causes of secondary constipation include:
body.explanation: GI disorders: colorectal cancer, benign tumours, strictures, congenital megacolon, extrinsic compressions, fissures, rectal prolapse, hemorrhoids.
option_notes: Wrong: a cause of primary slow transit constipation.

title: Symptoms associated with cholestasis syndrome include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms associated with cholestasis syndrome include:
body.explanation: Cholestasis: pruritus, dark urine, acholic stool, steatorrhoea, xanthoma/xanthelasma, symptoms of fat-soluble vitamins ADEK.

title: Other examinations in a constipated patient:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Other examinations in a constipated patient:
options: Pelvic examination in women may identify pelvic organ prolapse
Neurological examination may help rule out spinal cord injury
Neurological examination may help rule out autonomic dysfunction
Pelvic examination is the reference test for slow transit
body.explanation: Pelvic exam (women) may find gynecological causes such as pelvic organ prolapse; neurological exam rules out spinal cord injury or autonomic dysfunction.
option_notes: Wrong: slow transit is assessed by colonic transit studies.

title: A 70-year-old has a tender mass in the left iliac region. Which organ is most likely involved?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 70-year-old has a tender mass in the left iliac region. Which organ is most likely involved?
body.explanation: The left iliac region contains the descending and sigmoid colon.
option_notes: The descending and sigmoid colon lie in the left iliac region.
The appendix is in the right iliac region.
The gallbladder is in the right hypochondrium.
The spleen is in the left hypochondrium.

title: The hyperthyroid phase of thyroiditis is due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hyperthyroid phase of thyroiditis is due to:
options: Release of stored FT4 and FT3 after inflammation and cytolysis
Increased new hormone synthesis driven by a raised pituitary TSH secretion
body.explanation: Aggression (antibodies, viral, drugs) causes inflammation/cytolysis, releasing FT4 and FT3; the phase is auto-limited by stock depletion.

title: Above what duration are tests indicated in acute diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Above what duration are tests indicated in acute diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Tests only if severe dehydration, blood or pus, fever over 38°C, over 3 days, epidemic or immunosuppression.
option_notes: Tests are needed after 3 days of acute diarrhoea.

title: Abdominal palpation searches for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal palpation searches for:
options: A mass, which should be delineated
body.explanation: Palpation looks for a mass (delineate), tenderness, pain, hepatomegaly and splenomegaly.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Emergency measures. ICU, two large-bore IV lines, bloods and cross-match, fluids, oxygen, monitoring.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
ICU, two large-bore lines, bloods, fluids, oxygen.

title: The clinical picture of acute adrenal insufficiency includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The clinical picture of acute adrenal insufficiency includes:
options: Cardiovascular collapse with a thready pulse
Abdominal and lumbar fossa pain with vomiting
body.explanation: Cardiovascular collapse (major hypotension, pallor, sweating, cold extremities, thready pulse), intense digestive signs, neurological disorders up to coma and dehydration.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: pH monitoring. Reference test: GERD confirmed if oesophageal pH is below 4 for more than 5% of the time.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
The reference test: pH below 4 for more than 5% of the time.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Alarm signs. Dysphagia, odynophagia, bleeding, anaemia, weight loss, vomiting: endoscopy required.
option_notes: Dysphagia, odynophagia, bleeding, anaemia, weight loss, vomiting.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Which statements about nausea and vomiting match the lecture?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which statements about nausea and vomiting match the lecture?
options: They are among the most common gastrointestinal complaints
They always point to a digestive disease
They can signal neurological or systemic disease
body.explanation: One of the most common GI complaints, with several etiologies, from minor GI disease to serious neurological or systemic issues.
option_notes: Wrong: neurological and systemic causes exist.

title: A normal endoscopy in a patient with typical symptoms:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A normal endoscopy in a patient with typical symptoms:
body.explanation: Non-erosive reflux disease is common.
option_notes: Achalasia needs manometry, not a normal endoscopy, to diagnose.
A normal endoscopy does not suggest cancer.
A normal endoscopy does not exclude GERD.

title: Which are signs of cholestasis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are signs of cholestasis?
body.explanation: Pruritus, dark urine, pale stools, steatorrhoea.
option_notes: Bile salts in the skin cause itching.
Conjugated bilirubin in the urine darkens it.
Bradycardia alone is not a cholestasis sign.

title: Predisposing factors for GERD listed in the pathophysiology include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Predisposing factors for GERD listed in the pathophysiology include:
body.explanation: Predisposing factors: LES hypotonia, hiatal hernia, increased intra-abdominal pressure (obesity, pregnancy, tight clothing), delayed gastric emptying, certain foods or drugs.
option_notes: Wrong: it is delayed, not rapid, emptying.
Correct: delayed gastric emptying is listed.
Wrong: LES hypotonia, not hypertonia, predisposes.

title: A 29-year-old woman has amenorrhoea and galactorrhoea with a high prolactin. She also reports tiredness, cold intolerance and constipation. Which test should b…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 29-year-old woman has amenorrhoea and galactorrhoea with a high prolactin. She also reports tiredness, cold intolerance and constipation. Which test should be checked first?
body.explanation: Primary hypothyroidism can raise prolactin (hyperprolactinaemia is among its laboratory findings), and her symptoms fit hypothyroidism. Checking TSH and FT4 avoids blaming a pituitary tumour.
option_notes: Primary hypothyroidism can raise prolactin, and her symptoms fit it.
TRAb look for Graves' disease, not hypothyroidism.
Calcitonin is a thyroid cancer marker.

title: What do yellow plaques around the eyelids suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What do yellow plaques around the eyelids suggest?
body.explanation: Xanthelasma may signify hypercholesterolaemia, a cardiovascular risk factor, though it also occurs without it.
option_notes: Hyperthyroidism gives eye signs, not plaques.

title: CT scan or MRI in constipation is especially indicated when:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: CT scan or MRI in constipation is especially indicated when:
options: An obstruction or a tumour is suspected
The Bristol stool type must be determined
body.explanation: CT or MRI gives detailed imaging of abdominal structures, especially when an obstruction or tumour is suspected.
option_notes: Wrong: Bristol type comes from the history.

title: According to the lecture's conclusion:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture's conclusion:
options: Vomiting has a broad range of potential causes
A detailed history and examination are essential to find the cause
Extra-gastrointestinal causes should not be overlooked
Digestive causes can be assumed in every case
body.explanation: Conclusion: broad range of causes; detailed history and exam are essential; extra-GI causes should not be overlooked.
option_notes: Wrong: extra-GI causes must not be overlooked.

title: How deep is a grade 3 pitting oedema?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How deep is a grade 3 pitting oedema?
body.explanation: Grade 1: 2 mm. Grade 2: 3 to 4 mm. Grade 3: 5 to 6 mm. Grade 4: 8 mm.

title: What volume defines bronchorrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What volume defines bronchorrhoea?
body.explanation: Excessive expectoration: over 30 mL/day. Bronchorrhoea: over 100 mL/day.

title: Which findings suggest consolidation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which findings suggest consolidation?
body.explanation: Consolidation: dull, bronchial breathing, coarse crackles, increased vocal resonance.

title: Gastrointestinal causes of chronic vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Gastrointestinal causes of chronic vomiting include:
body.explanation: Chronic GI: pyloroduodenal stenosis, GERD, gastroparesis, chronic pancreatitis, IBS, chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction, coeliac disease, gastric cancer.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Osmotic diarrhoea. Osmotically active substances (lactase deficiency, laxatives); stops with fasting.
option_notes: Another box. Definition box: over 300 g/day, over 3 stools a day, over 90% water.
This is the box at the arrow. Osmotic: stops with fasting (lactase deficiency, laxatives).
Another box. Malabsorptive: greasy, pale, foul stools.
Another box. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.

title: On the differential chart, unconjugated bilirubin with raised reticulocytes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the differential chart, unconjugated bilirubin with raised reticulocytes:
body.explanation: Unconjugated -> CBC; retic up = haemolysis, next steps blood film and viral serology.

title: In a man with hyperprolactinaemia, the slides list:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a man with hyperprolactinaemia, the slides list:
body.explanation: In men the usual manifestations are those of hypogonadism: low libido (initial symptom), erectile dysfunction, gynaecomastia and infertility.
option_notes: Listed under men; shown in the photo on slide 9.
Wrong: that is a feature of acromegaly, not prolactin excess.

title: Muscle wasting in Cushing syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Muscle wasting in Cushing syndrome:
options: Is most prominent in the lower limbs
Goes with low fat-free mass and low total body protein
Mainly affects the small muscles of the hands
body.explanation: Muscle wasting is often proximal and most prominent in the lower extremities (myopathy); hypercortisolism is linked to low fat-free mass and low total body protein.

title: Urinary metanephrines are clearly raised but adrenal CT is normal. Which exam searches the whole body for an ectopic or multiple tumour?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Urinary metanephrines are clearly raised but adrenal CT is normal. Which exam searches the whole body for an ectopic or multiple tumour?
body.explanation: MIBG scintigraphy completes CT and MRI. It explores the whole body for multiple, ectopic or metastatic sites and can show small lesions missed by CT or MRI. Noriodocholesterol is used for aldosterone adenomas.
option_notes: MIBG explores the whole body for ectopic, multiple or metastatic tumours.
Noriodocholesterol is used for aldosterone adenomas.
Ultrasound is less sensitive than the CT already done.

title: About the nine regions of the abdomen:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the nine regions of the abdomen:
options: The middle row is right lumbar, umbilical, left lumbar
The epigastric region is in the upper middle
The hypogastric region is in the lower left
The umbilical region lies in the upper row
body.explanation: Upper row: right hypochondriac, epigastric, left hypochondriac; middle: right lumbar, umbilical, left lumbar; lower: right iliac, hypogastric, left iliac.

title: Which imaging test is used for a pituitary tumour?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which imaging test is used for a pituitary tumour?
body.explanation: MRI of the pituitary for prolactinoma, acromegaly and Cushing disease alike.
option_notes: MRI is the imaging test for pituitary tumours.

title: Deciding whether bleeding comes from the upper or the lower GI tract is which level of diagnosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Deciding whether bleeding comes from the upper or the lower GI tract is which level of diagnosis?
body.explanation: Three levels: positive (is it digestive bleeding), topographic (upper or lower), etiological (which lesion).
option_notes: Upper or lower is the topographic level.
Positive diagnosis confirms the bleeding is digestive.

title: What is TSH in primary hyperthyroidism (for example Graves' disease)?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is TSH in primary hyperthyroidism (for example Graves' disease)?
body.explanation: In primary hyperthyroidism TSH is suppressed and free T4 and/or T3 are raised (slide 20). Only the rare TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma gives a normal or high TSH.
option_notes: A raised TSH fits primary hypothyroidism or a TSH-secreting adenoma, not primary hyperthyroidism.
A normal TSH argues against primary hyperthyroidism.
High FT4/FT3 switch off pituitary TSH.
TSH is consistently low in primary hyperthyroidism.

title: Psychiatric features or complications of hypercortisolism include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Psychiatric features or complications of hypercortisolism include:
options: Euphoria, sometimes with delirium or mania
body.explanation: Psychiatric repercussions: euphoria with sometimes delirium or mania, depression with suicidal thoughts, emotional lability, paranoia; complications: insomnia, agitation, euphoria, maniac or depressive states.

title: The management of GI bleeding involves:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The management of GI bleeding involves:
body.explanation: GI bleeding is a medical and surgical emergency; management involves assessing severity, haemodynamic stabilisation, etiological diagnosis and specific (often endoscopic) treatment.

title: How many IV lines are placed in severe GI bleeding?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How many IV lines are placed in severe GI bleeding?
body.explanation: Two large-bore lines for filling and transfusion, plus group, crossmatch and bloods.
option_notes: One small line is not enough.
Two large-bore lines for fluids and transfusion.

title: Which are criteria for diagnosing diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are criteria for diagnosing diabetes?
options: Random glucose ≥ 2 g/L with classic symptoms
body.explanation: All four are diagnostic criteria. A single fasting value, or HbA1c over 7, is not the threshold.
option_notes: Fasting ≥ 1.26 g/L on two samples is a criterion.
Random ≥ 2 g/L with symptoms is a criterion.

title: About oral candidiasis:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About oral candidiasis:
options: It causes a white plaque on the tongue
It is an aphthous ulcer typical of IBD
body.explanation: Oral candidiasis: white plaque on the tongue (fungus infection).
option_notes: Slide 7: it is a fungus infection.
Aphthous ulcer is a different lesion.

title: Foods that decrease LES tone include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Foods that decrease LES tone include:
body.explanation: Foods that decrease LES tone: fats, chocolate, caffeine, alcohol, mint, spicy foods.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Melaena. Black, tarry, smelly stools of digested blood; usually upper GI; appears 6-8 h after bleeding starts.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Black, tarry, foul-smelling stools of digested blood.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Which are listed as chronic gastrointestinal causes of vomiting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are listed as chronic gastrointestinal causes of vomiting?
body.explanation: Gastric cancer, chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction and IBS are chronic GI causes; biliary colic is an acute non-surgical cause.

title: Abdominal palpation technique includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal palpation technique includes:
body.explanation: Palpation: supine with bent knees, superficial then deep, one hand or 2, all quadrants.
option_notes: Order is superficial first, then deep.

title: During a phaeochromocytoma attack, the patient may have:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During a phaeochromocytoma attack, the patient may have:
body.explanation: Attacks may include anxiety, tremors, sometimes vomiting, visual disorders, abdominal or chest pain; BP can be considerably higher than usual.
option_notes: Wrong: palpitations and high BP occur.

title: Alarm symptoms ('red flags') in constipation include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Alarm symptoms ('red flags') in constipation include:
options: Family history of inflammatory bowel disease
body.explanation: Red flags: rectal bleeding, weight loss, anemia, severe abdominal pain, family history of colorectal cancer or IBD.
option_notes: Wrong: bloating is a feature of slow transit and IBS-C.

title: In acute adrenal insufficiency:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In acute adrenal insufficiency:
options: Diagnosis is confirmed by the response to high-dose hydrocortisone
Hormone samples are taken without delaying treatment
body.explanation: Labs: hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia with ECG changes, haemoconcentration, hypoglycaemia; diagnosis confirmed by response to high-dose hydrocortisone, with assays done without delaying treatment.
option_notes: Wrong: hypoglycaemia is a lab sign.

title: Regarding the Cushing's syndrome case slide (Lancet 2023):
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the Cushing's syndrome case slide (Lancet 2023):
options: High cortisol may come from pituitary, adrenal or lung lesions
The patient improved 12 months after transsphenoidal surgery
Only pituitary tumours can raise cortisol
Bone disease is not a comorbidity
body.explanation: The figure shows pituitary, adrenal and lung sources of high cortisol, and the patient before and 12 months after transsphenoidal surgery.
option_notes: Adrenal and lung sources are also shown.

title: According to the Cushing disease axis diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the Cushing disease axis diagram:
options: Corticotropin releasing hormone from the hypothalamus stimulates ACTH
The adenoma is located in the anterior pituitary
Cortisol exerts negative feedback on hypothalamus and pituitary
ACTH acts mainly on the posterior pituitary
body.explanation: The diagram shows CRH (+) to an anterior pituitary adenoma, ACTH (+) to the adrenals, and cortisol (-) feedback to both hypothalamus and pituitary.
option_notes: Red (-) arrows return to hypothalamus and pituitary.
ACTH acts on the adrenal glands, not the posterior pituitary.

title: Which is an extrinsic cause of dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is an extrinsic cause of dysphagia?
body.explanation: Also mediastinal tumours and an enlarged left atrium.
option_notes: An aneurysm presses on the oesophagus from outside.
A stricture is in the wall.

title: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) is characterised by:
options: An organic lesion found on colonoscopy
body.explanation: IBS-C: abdominal discomfort, infrequent bowel movements, bloating, cramping, but no organic pathology.
option_notes: Wrong: no organic pathology is present.

title: Hypersecretion syndromes of the pituitary listed in the clinical presentation include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hypersecretion syndromes of the pituitary listed in the clinical presentation include:
options: Oxytocin hypersecretion from the anterior lobe
body.explanation: The slide lists prolactin, ACTH (Cushing disease), GH, TSH and FSH/LH hypersecretion.
option_notes: Oxytocin is a posterior pituitary hormone and is not in the list.

title: Which way do structures move in a retracted opacity?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which way do structures move in a retracted opacity?
body.explanation: Thoracic structures shift toward the collapsed side, with crowding of the ribs.
option_notes: Moving away is a space-occupying lesion.
Volume loss pulls structures toward it.

title: Imaging and other explorations listed for jaundice include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Imaging and other explorations listed for jaundice include:
body.explanation: Abdomino-pelvic ultrasound, CT, MRI, endoscopic ultrasound, liver biopsy, ERCP (therapeutic).

title: Early clinical warning signs of significant GI bleeding include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Early clinical warning signs of significant GI bleeding include:
body.explanation: Warning signs: pallor, cold extremities, restlessness, tachycardia. Severe forms: hypotension, polypnoea, oliguria, altered consciousness, mottling.
option_notes: Wrong: oliguria, not polyuria, marks severity.

title: Effects of cortisol shown on the regulation diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Effects of cortisol shown on the regulation diagram:
body.explanation: Metabolism: up gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, proteolysis, lipolysis; cardiovascular: up myocardial contractility, cardiac output and catecholamine pressor effect.

title: Which are causes of acute cough? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are causes of acute cough? (choose all)
body.explanation: Acute cough: infections, asthma exacerbation, pneumothorax, pleurisy, left heart failure, pulmonary embolism.
option_notes: Infection is a common acute cause.

title: Characteristics of constipation to specify during the interview include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Characteristics of constipation to specify during the interview include:
options: Duration of symptoms and any recent worsening
Need for manual maneuvers to evacuate stool
Nocturnal awakenings to pass watery stools
body.explanation: Specify chronicity, frequency, straining, consistency, incomplete evacuation, anorectal obstruction, manual maneuvers and current treatment (type of laxatives).
option_notes: Correct: current treatment, type of laxatives.
Wrong: watery stools are not a constipation characteristic.

title: Neurological causes of acute vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Neurological causes of acute vomiting include:
body.explanation: Neurological: increased ICP (head injury, stroke, tumour), meningitis, migraine, vestibular disorders.

title: Blood-stained vomiting (haematemesis) suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Blood-stained vomiting (haematemesis) suggests:
options: Active bleeding from the upper GI tract
body.explanation: Blood-stained vomit (haematemesis) suggests active upper GI bleeding.
option_notes: Wrong: a differential diagnosis, without blood.

title: Impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes occurs in Cushing syndrome in about:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes occurs in Cushing syndrome in about:
body.explanation: Other features: impaired glucose tolerance/diabetes mellitus (30%), hyperlipidaemia, increased susceptibility to infections.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Occult bleeding. Revealed only by anaemia or a positive faecal occult blood test.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Found only by anaemia or a faecal occult blood test.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Examination of the oral cavity includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Examination of the oral cavity includes:
body.explanation: Oral cavity: dental examination, gingiva, palate, internal face of cheeks, tongue, tonsil and uvula.

title: What suggests oropharyngeal dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What suggests oropharyngeal dysphagia?
body.explanation: Difficulty initiating, with cough or nasal regurgitation: neurological, muscular or ENT causes.
option_notes: Weight gain is not a sign.
A failed pharyngeal phase sends food to the airway or nose.

title: Oesophageal or gastric varices:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Oesophageal or gastric varices:
options: Are a lower GI bleeding cause
Are typical of young patients, like Meckel's diverticulum
body.explanation: Varices (oesophageal or gastric) are due to portal hypertension and are an upper GI cause; ulcers and varices predominate in adults.
option_notes: Wrong: they are an upper GI cause.
Wrong: ulcers and varices are cited in adults.

title: What defines a pleural fluid effusion?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What defines a pleural fluid effusion?
body.explanation: Fluid effusion syndrome: fluid in the pleural cavity, between the two pleural layers.
option_notes: Fluid between the two pleural layers.
Air in the pleura is pneumothorax.
Pus in the alveoli is pneumonia.

title: What separates angina from a heart attack?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What separates angina from a heart attack?
body.explanation: Angina is transient ischaemia without infarction; a heart attack is permanent damage.
option_notes: Duration alone does not separate them.
Angina is ischaemia without muscle death.
Both can radiate to the left arm.

title: Why does bitemporal hemianopia occur when the optic chiasm is compressed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why does bitemporal hemianopia occur when the optic chiasm is compressed?
options: The crossing nasal retinal fibres, which carry the temporal fields, are damaged
The uncrossed temporal fibres are damaged
The optic tracts behind the chiasm are cut
body.explanation: Pressure on the chiasm hits the fibres that cross there: they come from the nasal retinas, which see the temporal fields.
option_notes: Crossing nasal fibres carry the temporal fields.
Uncrossed fibres carry the nasal fields.
Optic tract damage gives a homonymous defect.

title: What is myxoedema coma?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is myxoedema coma?
body.explanation: Rare, in the elderly: weakness, stupor, hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoventilation, shock.
option_notes: The end stage of untreated hypothyroidism, mostly in the elderly.
A hyperthyroid crisis is thyroid storm, the opposite picture.
Myxoedema coma is not a cancer.
Bleeding into a goitre is a different event.

title: Outlet dysfunction is defined as impaired rectal evacuation due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Outlet dysfunction is defined as impaired rectal evacuation due to:
options: Accelerated colonic transit with liquid stools
Excess water secretion into the colonic lumen
Isolated reduction of right-sided colonic contractions
body.explanation: Outlet dysfunction: impaired rectal evacuation from inadequate rectal propulsive forces, increased resistance to evacuation, or both.
option_notes: Correct: either or both mechanisms per the slide.
Wrong: transit is not accelerated in outlet dysfunction.
Wrong: excess water absorption, not secretion, hardens stools.
Wrong: reduced colonic contractions describe slow transit.

title: What is the main consequence of left heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the main consequence of left heart failure?
body.explanation: Blood backs up into the pulmonary veins, fluid leaks into the lungs: dyspnoea, orthopnoea and crackles.
option_notes: Ascites is a right heart failure sign.
Blood backs up into the lungs.
Jaundice is not the main consequence.

title: Which is an extra-digestive GERD sign?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is an extra-digestive GERD sign?
body.explanation: Chronic cough, asthma-like symptoms, laryngitis, hoarseness, dental erosions, pseudo-anginal chest pain.
option_notes: Ascites is not linked to reflux.
Jaundice is not linked to reflux.
Acid reaching the airways causes chronic night cough.

title: Manifestations of hypokalaemia in aldosterone-producing adenoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Manifestations of hypokalaemia in aldosterone-producing adenoma:
body.explanation: Hypokalaemia causes fatigue and muscle cramps, polyuria and polydipsia, paresthesia and pseudo-paralysis.
option_notes: Wrong: purple striae are a sign of Cushing syndrome.

title: Enzymes raised in cholestasis include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Enzymes raised in cholestasis include:
body.explanation: Cholestasis enzymes: GGT, ALP, (5'nucleotidase).
option_notes: Not a cholestasis marker on the slide.

title: Nausea is defined as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Nausea is defined as:
options: An unpleasant, subjective sensation often associated with the urge to vomit
The forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth
The effortless return of food from the stomach into the mouth
A retrosternal burning sensation after meals
body.explanation: Nausea is an unpleasant, subjective sensation often associated with the urge to vomit, typically originating from the GI tract or the CNS.
option_notes: Wrong: that describes regurgitation or rumination.

title: What does scintigraphy show in toxic adenoma?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does scintigraphy show in toxic adenoma?
body.explanation: A hyperfixing hot nodule with reduced uptake elsewhere; no eye signs.
option_notes: The adenoma takes up tracer while the rest of the gland is suppressed.
Diffuse uptake is the Graves' pattern.
A cold nodule does not take up tracer; it is not toxic.
Tracer is taken up by the hot nodule.

title: How is occult bleeding revealed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is occult bleeding revealed?
body.explanation: Chronic minimal loss shows as iron deficiency anaemia or a positive faecal occult blood test.
option_notes: Iron deficiency anaemia or a positive faecal occult blood test.

title: In the 75 g glucose tolerance test used for acromegaly:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the 75 g glucose tolerance test used for acromegaly:
options: The test looks for inhibition of GH by glucose
Lack of GH inhibition supports acromegaly
It is used to measure prolactin suppression
body.explanation: The slide lists 'GH - inhibition in glucose tolerance 75 g test': glucose should suppress GH, and in acromegaly it does not.
option_notes: Inadequate suppression points to GH excess.
Wrong: GH is the hormone tested.

title: Conclusions of the lecture on constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Conclusions of the lecture on constipation:
options: The diagnosis of constipation is usually easy
The etiological diagnosis relies on thorough history and complete examination
Paraclinical exams are indicated to rule out an organic origin
Paraclinical exams are needed to make the diagnosis of constipation
body.explanation: Diagnosis is usually easy; etiology relies on history and complete examination; paraclinical exams rule out an organic origin.
option_notes: Wrong: diagnosis is clinical; tests look for organic causes.

title: Other lab changes due to excess cortisol include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Other lab changes due to excess cortisol include:
body.explanation: Other lab tests: impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes, polycythaemia, hyperleukocytosis with PNN, lymphopenia, hypokalaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia.

title: On the bilirubin physiology diagram, macrophages:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the bilirubin physiology diagram, macrophages:
options: Take up red cells and degrade haemoglobin
Also play a role in cholesterol metabolism
body.explanation: In macrophages haemoglobin becomes unconjugated bilirubin; macrophages play an important role in bilirubin and cholesterol metabolism.

title: Which belong to the acromegalic face?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which belong to the acromegalic face?
body.explanation: Prominent supraorbital ridges and frontal bossing, big nose, prognathism, teeth separation, deep nasolabial furrows, macroglossia, large lips, deep voice. Exophthalmos is Graves' disease.
option_notes: Frontal bossing with prominent supraorbital ridges is acromegalic.
Forward growth of the mandible is typical.
Soft tissue thickening enlarges the tongue and lips.

title: What does foul-smelling sputum suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does foul-smelling sputum suggest?
body.explanation: A foul odour points to anaerobic germs.
option_notes: Allergy does not cause a foul odour.

title: Why bend the knees during palpation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why bend the knees during palpation?
body.explanation: Supine with bent knees relaxes the abdominal wall; palpate lightly then deeply in all quadrants.
option_notes: Kidney palpation is a separate technique.
Reflexes are not tested this way.
Bent knees relax the abdominal wall.
Bending the knees does not move the liver.

title: On the fat-deposit drawing, the buffalo hump corresponds to the:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the fat-deposit drawing, the buffalo hump corresponds to the:
body.explanation: The drawing shows temporal, supraclavicular, dorsal scapular and episternal fat deposits; the dorsal scapular one is the buffalo hump between the shoulders.
option_notes: Wrong: in front of the sternum.

title: Why can acromegaly cause diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why can acromegaly cause diabetes?
options: GH opposes the action of insulin
GH destroys beta cells by autoimmunity
body.explanation: Diabetes mellitus or impaired glucose tolerance is among the metabolic abnormalities of acromegaly: GH is a counter-regulatory hormone that opposes insulin.
option_notes: Pituitary adenomas do not secrete glucagon.

title: Assessing the impact of vomiting on the patient includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Assessing the impact of vomiting on the patient includes:
body.explanation: Impact on patient: effect on appetite, hydration status, weight loss and overall physical condition.

title: What separates regurgitation from vomiting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What separates regurgitation from vomiting?
options: Regurgitation is effortless, without abdominal effort
Regurgitation brings up bile from the duodenum
body.explanation: Regurgitation is the effortless reflux of acidic gastric contents into the mouth, with a hot, bitter taste.
option_notes: It brings up acidic gastric contents.
Retching is an effort; regurgitation has none.

title: How should the patient be positioned for inspection?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How should the patient be positioned for inspection?
options: Lying flat in a dark room
body.explanation: Naked chest, seated or standing, in full light; watch the patient undress for dyspnoea.
option_notes: Bare chest in full light, seated or standing.

title: Causes of hypothyroidism listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of hypothyroidism listed in the lecture include:
body.explanation: Causes: iatrogenic (thyroidectomy+++, 131I, neck irradiation), drugs (antithyroid drugs, lithium, amiodarone, TKI, checkpoint inhibitors), thyroiditis, iodine deficiency, congenital, central.
option_notes: Correct: thyroidectomy is the main iatrogenic cause.

title: Diabetic ketoacidosis is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Diabetic ketoacidosis is characterised by:
body.explanation: DKA figure: glucose >13.88 mmol/L, pH <7.3, bicarbonate <18 mmol/L, ketonaemia, ketonuria, glycosuria. Note: page 33 prints 'Bicarbonate <7.3', which is the pH threshold; bicarbonate <18 mmol/L is per page 24 and textbooks.

title: What is an eventration?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is an eventration?
body.explanation: Eventration is a hernia on a surgical scar, seen on inspection.
option_notes: A liver mass is a different finding.
A vein dilatation is a collateral circulation.
A rash is a skin finding.
Eventration is a hernia through a surgical scar.

title: Which is a metabolic cardiovascular risk factor?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a metabolic cardiovascular risk factor?
body.explanation: Metabolic: hypertension, diabetes, cholesterol, waist-to-hip ratio. Others: tobacco, alcohol, poor diet, low physical activity, air pollution, depression.

title: A patient develops thyrotoxicosis a few weeks after a large dose of iodine (iodinated contrast). Which entity in the lecture's table fits?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient develops thyrotoxicosis a few weeks after a large dose of iodine (iodinated contrast). Which entity in the lecture's table fits?
body.explanation: Jod-Basedow is hyperthyroidism triggered by an iodine load; it is listed with the causes of true hyperthyroidism.
option_notes: An iodine load can trigger hyperthyroidism in a goitre: Jod-Basedow.
Struma ovarii is thyroid tissue in an ovarian tumour.
Riedel's is a fibrosing thyroiditis, not iodine-induced.

title: Which make up the classic hyperglycaemia syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which make up the classic hyperglycaemia syndrome?
body.explanation: Polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia and weight loss (not gain).
option_notes: Increased appetite compensates for cellular fasting.
The syndrome includes weight loss, not gain.

title: According to the lecture, early postprandial vomiting may suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture, early postprandial vomiting may suggest:
options: A gastric emptying disorder or gastroparesis
body.explanation: The slide links early postprandial vomiting to gastric emptying problems or gastroparesis, and late postprandial vomiting to duodenal or pyloric obstruction.
option_notes: Wrong: pyloric obstruction gives late postprandial vomiting.
Wrong: alcohol dependence gives morning vomiting.
Wrong: not listed for this timing.

title: What are the normal glucose values?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What are the normal glucose values?
options: Fasting under 1.10 g/L and under 1.40 g/L 2 hours after an OGTT
Fasting under 1.40 g/L and under 2 g/L after an OGTT
body.explanation: Physiological reminder slide: fasting under 1.10 g/L, under 1.40 g/L 2 hours after OGTT.
option_notes: Normal: fasting under 1.10 g/L and under 1.40 g/L 2 hours after OGTT.
1.26 g/L is the diabetes threshold, not the normal limit.

title: What causes superior vena cava syndrome most often?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes superior vena cava syndrome most often?
body.explanation: Obstruction of the SVC, most often by thrombus or tumour infiltration.
option_notes: A clot or tumour blocks the SVC.
An effusion does not block the SVC.

title: Acute gastritis causing vomiting is often due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Acute gastritis causing vomiting is often due to:
body.explanation: Acute gastritis (often due to NSAIDs).
option_notes: Wrong: listed as drug toxicity, not for gastritis.
Wrong: listed as drug toxicity, not for gastritis.

title: Which arm should not be used for blood pressure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which arm should not be used for blood pressure?
body.explanation: Avoid an arm with a medical problem or on the side of a mastectomy, to avoid lymphoedema; use a bare arm.
option_notes: The dominant arm can be used.
Cuff pressure on the mastectomy side risks lymphoedema.
The left arm can be used.
The non-dominant arm can be used.

title: Which chambers characterise diastolic failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which chambers characterise diastolic failure?
body.explanation: Diastolic heart failure has stiff, thick walls that cannot fill.
option_notes: Stretched, thin chambers are systolic failure.
Stiff, thick walls cannot fill properly.

title: A patient on haemodialysis for chronic kidney disease has galactorrhoea and mild hyperprolactinaemia. What is the likely cause?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient on haemodialysis for chronic kidney disease has galactorrhoea and mild hyperprolactinaemia. What is the likely cause?
body.explanation: Chronic renal insufficiency and severe liver failure are listed among the causes of hyperprolactinaemia.
option_notes: A mild rise with a known cause points to that cause first.
Apoplexy is sudden headache and visual loss.

title: Vomiting of undigested food suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Vomiting of undigested food suggests:
body.explanation: Undigested food suggests gastric emptying disorders such as gastroparesis or gastric outlet obstruction.

title: What causes a barrel chest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes a barrel chest?
body.explanation: Bilateral distension with a larger anteroposterior diameter: emphysema, asthma. Unilateral distension: pleurisy. Whole retraction: pachypleuritis.
option_notes: Pleurisy does not distend the chest.
Air trapping enlarges the AP diameter.
A tumour gives a local bulge.

title: What can mimic melena?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What can mimic melena?
body.explanation: Iron, charcoal, bismuth and some foods darken stools.
option_notes: Vitamin C does not blacken stools.
Iron darkens stools (also charcoal and bismuth).

title: Which chest pain radiates to the back in hypertensive men?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which chest pain radiates to the back in hypertensive men?
body.explanation: Aortic dissection: intense median retrosternal pain radiating to the back, typically in elderly hypertensive atheromatous men.
option_notes: Coronary pain radiates to the arm or jaw.
Pleurisy is lateral and worse on breathing.
Tearing pain to the back in a hypertensive man.
Oesophageal spasm is not typical of this.

title: A man has BMI 17, BP 100/60, glucose 0.65 g/l and pigmented gums and palmar creases; cortisol 3.1 ng/ml (N 30-200) and ACTH 300 pg/l (N 10-60). Per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man has BMI 17, BP 100/60, glucose 0.65 g/l and pigmented gums and palmar creases; cortisol 3.1 ng/ml (N 30-200) and ACTH 300 pg/l (N 10-60). Per the slides:
options: The diagnosis is primary adrenal insufficiency
The low glucose fits cortisol deficiency
High ACTH points to a pituitary cause
body.explanation: The clinical case concludes primary adrenal insufficiency: low cortisol with high ACTH and hyperpigmentation; hypoglycaemia reflects cortisol deficiency.
option_notes: Wrong: high ACTH means peripheral origin.

title: ENT and oral manifestations of GERD include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: ENT and oral manifestations of GERD include:
body.explanation: ENT/oral symptoms: dental erosions, gingivitis, chronic pharyngitis, laryngitis, globus pharyngeus, hoarseness or chronic dysphonia.

title: After pituitary surgery, a patient has adrenal insufficiency with pale skin, frequent hypoglycaemia and no hyperkalaemia. Why is there no hyperkalaemia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: After pituitary surgery, a patient has adrenal insufficiency with pale skin, frequent hypoglycaemia and no hyperkalaemia. Why is there no hyperkalaemia?
body.explanation: In secondary AI, the problem is ACTH. Aldosterone is mainly driven by the renin-angiotensin system, so it is conserved: hypotension, digestive signs and hyperkalaemia are rare, and there is no hyperpigmentation.
option_notes: Aldosterone depends on the renin-angiotensin system, not ACTH, so potassium stays normal.
ACTH is low in secondary AI.

title: Which conditions predispose to GERD?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which conditions predispose to GERD?
body.explanation: Obesity, pregnancy and tight clothing raise intra-abdominal pressure.
option_notes: Pregnancy raises abdominal pressure and progesterone relaxes the LES.
Anaemia is a possible consequence, not a cause.

title: On abdominal inspection, the examiner looks for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On abdominal inspection, the examiner looks for:
body.explanation: Inspection: surgical scars, hernia/eventration, collateral veins, bulge/asymmetry, dermatological lesions.

title: Why is the prothrombin time prolonged in cholestasis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is the prothrombin time prolonged in cholestasis?
body.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are malabsorbed; less vitamin K prolongs prothrombin time (ratio under 70 percent).
option_notes: Platelets do not lengthen the PT.
Low albumin does not explain it here.
Vitamin K is fat-soluble and needs bile to be absorbed.

title: What does the X-ray show in acute bronchitis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does the X-ray show in acute bronchitis?
body.explanation: Acute bronchitis: dry then productive cough; exam and X-ray are often normal.

title: What is Pancoast-Tobias syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is Pancoast-Tobias syndrome?
body.explanation: Horner syndrome, an apical tumour and bone lysis.
option_notes: An apical tumour invading the sympathetic chain causes Horner.

title: Systolic heart failure means the heart cannot do what?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Systolic heart failure means the heart cannot do what?
body.explanation: Systolic: can't pump; stretched, thin chambers. Diastolic: can't fill; stiff, thick chambers.
option_notes: Failure to fill is diastolic failure.

title: The hormonal pattern of aldosterone-producing adenoma on the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hormonal pattern of aldosterone-producing adenoma on the slides:
options: High aldosterone, low renin, ratio above 64
Normal ratio below 64 with high renin
body.explanation: Normal aldosterone/renin ratio is <64; in adenoma, aldosterone is high and renin low with a ratio >64.
option_notes: Correct: per the slide (units not given; cut-offs vary with assay units in textbooks).

title: What sound is a pleural rub compared to?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What sound is a pleural rub compared to?
body.explanation: A pleural rub, heard at the end of inspiration from inflamed pleura, sounds like a foot creaking in fresh snow.
option_notes: A rub sounds like walking on fresh snow.

title: Risk factors for diabetic ketoacidosis include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Risk factors for diabetic ketoacidosis include:
options: Improper management of an intercurrent infection
Intense physical activity, delayed meals or insufficient food intake
body.explanation: Risk factors on the DKA figure: omission of insulin, improper management of intercurrent infection, new-onset diabetes. Intense exercise is a cause of hypoglycaemia.
option_notes: Correct: DKA can reveal new diabetes.
Wrong: listed as a hypoglycaemia cause.

title: Primary constipation is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Primary constipation is characterised by:
options: A recent onset as a complication of an underlying disease
body.explanation: Primary constipation is often chronic and isolated: functional constipation, with two mechanisms (slow transit, outlet dysfunction).
option_notes: Wrong: recent onset with an underlying condition defines secondary constipation.

title: The main aims of the work-up in constipation are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The main aims of the work-up in constipation are:
options: If primary, to differentiate slow transit from outlet dysfunction
To confirm the diagnosis of constipation itself
To replace the patient history and clinical examination
body.explanation: Work-up aims: rule out secondary constipation; if primary, differentiate slow transit from outlet dysfunction.
option_notes: Wrong: the diagnosis of constipation is usually easy clinically.
Wrong: history and exam remain the basis.

title: Neurological causes of secondary constipation include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Neurological causes of secondary constipation include:
body.explanation: Neurological disorders: Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury, stroke.
option_notes: Wrong: anismus is a cause of primary outlet dysfunction.

title: When does Prinzmetal angina typically occur?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When does Prinzmetal angina typically occur?
body.explanation: It can occur at rest, often at night, triggered by emotional stress, smoking or cocaine.
option_notes: Spasm occurs at rest, often at night.

title: In a standard synacthen test, cortisol rises to 14 µg/dL at 60 minutes. How is this interpreted?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a standard synacthen test, cortisol rises to 14 µg/dL at 60 minutes. How is this interpreted?
options: The test must be repeated with dexamethasone
body.explanation: Cortisol is measured at T0 and T60 after 250 µg tetracosactide IM. An insufficient rise, below 18 µg/dL, confirms adrenal insufficiency.
option_notes: A peak below 18 µg/dL confirms adrenal insufficiency.
A normal response reaches at least 18 µg/dL.
Dexamethasone is not part of the synacthen test.
Synacthen tests adrenal reserve, not cortisol excess.

title: What does a bitonal cough suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does a bitonal cough suggest?
body.explanation: Bitonal cough: compression or paralysis of the recurrent nerve. Painful cough: pleural or parietal involvement.
option_notes: Pleural involvement gives a painful cough.
Recurrent nerve palsy paralyses one vocal cord, giving two tones.

title: Globus pharyngeus refers to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Globus pharyngeus refers to:
options: A sensation of a lump or foreign body in the throat
body.explanation: Globus pharyngeus is the sensation of a lump or foreign body, listed among ENT manifestations of GERD.
option_notes: Correct: definition on the ENT slide.

title: On the slide 'Vascular injury and diabetes / Glycemic control and macrovascular disease':
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the slide 'Vascular injury and diabetes / Glycemic control and macrovascular disease':
options: Vascular injury was a non-issue until the detection of insulin, then an increasing concern
ACCORD, ADVANCE and VADT are trials of glycaemic control and vascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes
The trials shown studied only children with type 1 diabetes
Erectile dysfunction is not shown among vascular targets
body.explanation: The figure states vascular injury became a concern after insulin was discovered and cites ACCORD, ADVANCE and VADT on intensive glucose control in type 2 diabetes.
option_notes: All three concern type 2 diabetes in adults.

title: Which are severity signs in GI bleeding?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are severity signs in GI bleeding?
body.explanation: Pallor, cold extremities, tachycardia; severe: hypotension, polypnoea, oliguria, altered consciousness, mottling.
option_notes: Low blood pressure shows severe blood loss.
Low urine output shows poor perfusion.
Severe bleeding gives tachycardia and cold skin.
Altered consciousness is a severity sign.

title: A pituitary adenoma extends above the sella. What is the usual first visual field defect?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A pituitary adenoma extends above the sella. What is the usual first visual field defect?
options: Bitemporal loss starting in the upper fields
Loss of the lower nasal fields
body.explanation: Suprasellar extension compresses the optic chiasm from below: bitemporal visual loss begins in the superior field portions (bitemporal superior quadrantanopia), then bitemporal hemianopia.
option_notes: Chiasm pressure from below starts in the upper temporal fields.
The lower nasal fields are not the first hit.
A central scotoma is an optic nerve sign.
Complete blindness in one eye is not the first sign.

title: About phaeochromocytoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About phaeochromocytoma:
options: It is a tumour of chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla
It is a curable cause of hypertension
It is a tumour of the adrenal cortex
body.explanation: Definition: tumours of chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla (phaeochromocytomas) or extra-adrenal (paragangliomas) secreting catecholamines; a curable cause of hypertension.
option_notes: Wrong: it arises from the medulla.

title: A patient with undiagnosed, slowly developing adrenal insufficiency gets pneumonia and collapses. How does the lecture describe this?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with undiagnosed, slowly developing adrenal insufficiency gets pneumonia and collapses. How does the lecture describe this?
options: Latent adrenal insufficiency revealed by an intercurrent illness
A new disease unrelated to the adrenals
body.explanation: Acute adrenal insufficiency is the natural evolution of slow AI and can reveal latent AI during an intercurrent illness (infection, trauma, surgery).
option_notes: It is the same adrenal disease.
Adrenal crisis must be considered in shock.

title: On the lecture's summary slide, vomiting is called chronic when it lasts more than:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the lecture's summary slide, vomiting is called chronic when it lasts more than:
body.explanation: Summary slide: acute under 2 weeks, chronic over 3 weeks.
option_notes: Correct: acute is under 2 weeks, chronic over 3 weeks.
Wrong: far too short; acute is under 2 weeks.
