title: Which drive mortality in low-income but not high-income countries?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drive mortality in low-income but not high-income countries?
body.explanation: Poor diet, low education, household air pollution and low strength are major drivers in low-income countries.
option_notes: Diet and household air pollution weigh more in poor countries.

title: A 30-year-old man has gynaecomastia, infertility and low libido. Which hormone disorder should be looked for, according to the lecture?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 30-year-old man has gynaecomastia, infertility and low libido. Which hormone disorder should be looked for, according to the lecture?
body.explanation: In men, hyperprolactinaemia presents as hypogonadism: low libido first, then erectile dysfunction, gynaecomastia and infertility.
option_notes: In men, hyperprolactinaemia presents as hypogonadism.
Acromegaly does not give this picture.
Central hyperthyroidism does not give this picture.
Apoplexy is sudden headache and visual loss.

title: How is exudative diarrhoea diagnosed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is exudative diarrhoea diagnosed?
body.explanation: Loss of plasma proteins into the gut.
option_notes: This measures protein lost into the gut.
Breath tests look for lactose intolerance or bacterial overgrowth.
A barium enema is an imaging test, not for protein loss.

title: In which ways can pituitary disease show itself?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In which ways can pituitary disease show itself?
options: Insufficiency of one or more axes
body.explanation: The lecture's three headings: hypersecretion for each axis, pituitary insufficiency, mass effect.
option_notes: Each axis can be hypersecreted (prolactin, GH, ACTH, TSH, FSH/LH).
One or more axes can fail (pituitary insufficiency).
A tumour can compress nearby structures.
Hyperpigmentation is not a general sign of pituitary disease.

title: When does left coronary flow mainly occur?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When does left coronary flow mainly occur?
body.explanation: Left coronary flow peaks in diastole, when the contracting muscle no longer compresses the vessels.
option_notes: Contracting muscle squeezes the vessels in systole.
The heart relaxes in diastole and the vessels open.

title: Causes of hypoglycaemia listed in the lecture include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of hypoglycaemia listed in the lecture include:
body.explanation: Etiologies listed: insulin or sulfonylurea overdose, delayed meal, insufficient food intake and intense physical activity.
option_notes: Insulin omission is a risk factor for ketoacidosis, not hypoglycaemia.

title: How long does a chronic cough last?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How long does a chronic cough last?
body.explanation: Acute: under 3 weeks. Subacute: 3 to 8 weeks. Chronic: over 8 weeks.

title: What causes Prinzmetal angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes Prinzmetal angina?
body.explanation: Vasospastic (Prinzmetal) angina comes from coronary artery spasm, with or without atherosclerosis.
option_notes: Coronary spasm closes the artery temporarily.
A fixed plaque causes stable angina.

title: A patient with Parkinson's disease has long-standing constipation. How is it classified?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with Parkinson's disease has long-standing constipation. How is it classified?
body.explanation: Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury and stroke are neurological causes of secondary constipation.
option_notes: A neurological disease is an identifiable cause.
Primary constipation has no identifiable cause.
Rectocele is a structural outlet cause.

title: What stool weight defines diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What stool weight defines diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Over 300 g/day, more than 3 stools a day, water over 90 percent of stool weight.
option_notes: Diarrhoea is over 300 g of stool a day.
Normal stool weight is above this.
Normal stool weight is above this.

title: Which weight loss is a red flag?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which weight loss is a red flag?
body.explanation: Red flags: age over 50, rapid progression, weight loss over 5 kg, iron deficiency anaemia, caustic, GERD or radiation history.
option_notes: Too small to be a red flag.
Too small to be a red flag.
Weight loss over 5 kg is a red flag.

title: What is the sublingual treatment of angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the sublingual treatment of angina?
body.explanation: Nitroglycerin under the tongue, plus long-acting nitrates, aspirin, beta blockers and calcium channel blockers.
option_notes: Aspirin is swallowed, as an antiplatelet.
Sublingual nitroglycerin dilates the vessels quickly.

title: What is paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea?
body.explanation: The patient wakes 1 to 2 hours after falling asleep with air hunger or a feeling of drowning.
option_notes: Sitting relieves breathlessness in heart failure.
Waking up breathless 1 to 2 hours after falling asleep.

title: Xanthelasma and xanthoma in a jaundiced patient:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Xanthelasma and xanthoma in a jaundiced patient:
options: Are linked to the cholestasis syndrome
Fit with the hypercholesterolaemia of cholestasis
body.explanation: Xanthoma/xanthelasma are listed among cholestasis symptoms, and hypercholesterolaemia is a cholestasis laboratory finding.

title: An HbA1c of 50 mmol/mol is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An HbA1c of 50 mmol/mol is:
options: Above the diabetes threshold of 48 mmol/mol
body.explanation: HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, that is 48 mmol/mol, is a diagnostic criterion.
option_notes: It is above the prediabetes range.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Upper GI endoscopy. First-line test: sees the mucosa and takes biopsies to exclude cancer.
option_notes: Another box. Organic: solids then liquids, progressive.
This is the box at the arrow. Endoscopy: the first-line test.
Another box. Oropharyngeal: hard to start the swallow, cough, nasal regurgitation.

title: Which items belong to the history of a vomiting patient?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which items belong to the history of a vomiting patient?
options: Medication type, dosage and date of the last intake
Date of the last menstrual period and contraception
body.explanation: History: age, medical and surgical (especially digestive) history, medications, toxic exposure, recent travel, similar cases in contacts, menstrual history and contraception.

title: Which signs make up Horner's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which signs make up Horner's syndrome?
body.explanation: Miosis, ptosis with apparent enophthalmos, and loss of sweating on the same side of the face.
option_notes: Miosis, ptosis and loss of sweating on one side.
Exophthalmos is not part of it.

title: Which are complications of cough? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are complications of cough? (choose all)
body.explanation: Syncope, ruptured bullae (pneumothorax), rib fracture, incontinence, hernia, vomiting, insomnia.

title: In the clinical presentation of diabetic nephropathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the clinical presentation of diabetic nephropathy:
options: The history covers type and duration of diabetes, urinary tract infection and glycaemic balance
Examination looks for oedema, hypertension and urine strip findings
Haematuria with flank pain is the typical presentation
body.explanation: History: type and history of diabetes, UTI, glycaemic balance. Exam: asymptomatic disease, oedema, HTN, urine strip.

title: Symptoms of adrenal insufficiency listed on the slides include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms of adrenal insufficiency listed on the slides include:
body.explanation: GI disturbances (nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea), hypoglycaemia from cortisol deficiency, depressive or psychotic disorders and amenorrhoea are listed.

title: Which symptom favours hypothyroidism over hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which symptom favours hypothyroidism over hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: From the comparison table: hypothyroidism gives cold sensitivity, weight gain, dry skin and constipation; hyperthyroidism gives heat sensitivity, brittle hair, frequent stools and tremor.
option_notes: Cold sensitivity is typical of hypothyroidism.
Fine, brittle hair is listed under hyperthyroidism.

title: On cervical examination, the thyroid:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On cervical examination, the thyroid:
options: Is fixed and does not move with swallowing
Is examined as part of the oral cavity
Is examined during the proctological examination
body.explanation: Thyroid examination: the gland is mobile with swallowing.
option_notes: It is part of the cervical exam.
It is part of the cervical examination (slide 8).

title: What share of hemoptysis is idiopathic?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What share of hemoptysis is idiopathic?
body.explanation: About 15 percent have no cause found; causes include cancer, tuberculosis, bronchiectasis, hydatid cyst, valvulopathy and embolism.

title: Why is unstable angina an emergency?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is unstable angina an emergency?
body.explanation: The tissue is alive but ischaemic, with a high risk of myocardial infarction.
option_notes: It mainly threatens the heart, not the brain.

title: Organs projecting onto the left hypochondriac region include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Organs projecting onto the left hypochondriac region include:
body.explanation: Left hypochondriac: spleen, colon, left kidney, pancreas.
option_notes: Appendix is in the right iliac region.

title: Drugs that can raise prolactin include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Drugs that can raise prolactin include:
body.explanation: Pharmacologic causes include dopamine antagonists (phenothiazines, haloperidol, risperidone, metoclopramide, reserpine, methyldopa, opioids), MAO inhibitors, IV cimetidine, verapamil and TRH.
option_notes: Wrong: levodopa increases dopamine, which inhibits prolactin.

title: On the 'Road to type 2 diabetes' chart, values in the prediabetes range include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the 'Road to type 2 diabetes' chart, values in the prediabetes range include:
options: HbA1c 5.5% measured on a single sample
body.explanation: Prediabetes: A1c 5.7-6.4%, fasting 100-125 mg/dL, OGTT 140-199 mg/dL. Diabetes: A1c >=6.5%; normal A1c <5.7%.

title: In the 'Main symptoms of diabetes' figure, symptoms marked as more common in type 1 include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the 'Main symptoms of diabetes' figure, symptoms marked as more common in type 1 include:
options: Smell of acetone on the breath
Blurred vision, the eye symptom shown on the figure
body.explanation: Red items (more common in type 1): lethargy, stupor, acetone breath, Kussmaul breathing, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting. Blurred vision is not marked red.
option_notes: Correct: Kussmaul hyperventilation shown in red.
Correct: gastric symptoms shown in red.
Wrong: blurred vision is not marked type 1-specific.

title: The standard synacthen test consists of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The standard synacthen test consists of:
options: Cortisol at T0 and T60 after 250 ug tetracosactide IM
Cortisol the morning after 1 mg dexamethasone at midnight
GH after a 75 g oral glucose load
body.explanation: Cortisolaemia is measured at T0 and T60 min after IM injection of 250 ug tetracosactide; an insufficient rise (< 18 ug/dl) confirms adrenal insufficiency.
option_notes: Wrong: high-dose DXM test for Cushing's cause.

title: Neurological causes of chronic vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Neurological causes of chronic vomiting include:
body.explanation: Chronic neurological: chronic migraine, intracranial tumours, chronic increased ICP.

title: Epigastric pain may come from which organs projecting onto that region?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Epigastric pain may come from which organs projecting onto that region?
body.explanation: The epigastric region contains the stomach, part of the liver, the pancreas, the duodenum, the spleen and the adrenal glands.
option_notes: The stomach lies in the epigastrium.
The pancreas projects onto the epigastrium.
The duodenum projects onto the epigastrium.
The sigmoid colon lies in the left iliac and hypogastric regions.

title: Inspection findings listed on the slides include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Inspection findings listed on the slides include:
body.explanation: Slide 12 lists collateral veins, abdominal bulge/asymmetry and dermatological lesions under inspection.

title: Which situations typically trigger heartburn?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which situations typically trigger heartburn?
body.explanation: Heartburn is often postprandial or nocturnal, triggered by bending forward, lying down or heavy meals.
option_notes: An empty stomach is not a typical trigger.

title: What albumin level defines an exudate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What albumin level defines an exudate?
body.explanation: Exudate: albumin over 30 g/L, inflammatory. Transudate: under 30 g/L, mechanical.

title: How is chronic bronchitis defined?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is chronic bronchitis defined?
body.explanation: A productive morning cough with mucous sputum, at least 3 months a year for 2 consecutive years.
option_notes: One episode of blood is haemoptysis.
Productive cough 3 months a year for 2 consecutive years.

title: Characteristics of the neuropathic foot include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Characteristics of the neuropathic foot include:
options: Cold, pale foot with absent pulses
body.explanation: Neuropathic feet: hot, dry skin with hyperkeratosis, superficial and deep sensory disorders, deformities (hammer, claw toes).

title: Which skin changes are typical of acromegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which skin changes are typical of acromegaly?
options: Thick skin with increased oiliness and sweating
Thin, fragile skin with easy bruising
body.explanation: Acromegaly gives thickening of the skin with increased oiliness and sweating.
option_notes: GH excess thickens the skin and increases sweating.
Thin fragile skin with bruising is Cushing's.
Pigmented gums are primary adrenal insufficiency.

title: A thyrotoxic patient could have Graves' disease or a toxic adenoma. Which finding points to Graves' disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A thyrotoxic patient could have Graves' disease or a toxic adenoma. Which finding points to Graves' disease?
body.explanation: Tachycardia, tremor and a low TSH are part of the thyrotoxicosis syndrome common to every cause. Ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos, chemosis, diplopia) belongs to Graves'; toxic adenoma has no ocular signs.
option_notes: Tachycardia is part of thyrotoxicosis from any cause.
A low TSH is common to every cause of thyrotoxicosis.
Ophthalmopathy is specific to Graves'; toxic adenoma has no eye signs.
Tremor is part of thyrotoxicosis from any cause.

title: What is the first step in the aetiological strategy?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the first step in the aetiological strategy?
body.explanation: The first step is to separate cholestatic (conjugated) from non-cholestatic (unconjugated) jaundice.
option_notes: Biopsy is not the first step.
ERCP comes later and is therapeutic.
First separate cholestatic from non-cholestatic jaundice.
Biology and ultrasound come before CT.

title: Which cause right heart failure? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which cause right heart failure? (choose all)
body.explanation: Left heart failure, septal defects and chronic lung disease.
option_notes: Left heart failure is the commonest cause.
Hyperlipidaemia is not a direct cause.

title: Manifestations of diabetic autonomic neuropathy include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Manifestations of diabetic autonomic neuropathy include:
body.explanation: Autonomic: postural hypotension, resting tachycardia, loss of sweating, gastroparesis, diabetic diarrhoea, bladder atony, erectile dysfunction.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Haematochezia. Bright red blood per anus; usually lower GI, or massive upper bleeding.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Which blood change accompanies chronic hypoxia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which blood change accompanies chronic hypoxia?
body.explanation: Chronic hypoxia leads to polycythaemia, along with pulmonary hypertension, systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.
option_notes: Hypoxia stimulates red cells, not anaemia.
White cells are not the response.
Low oxygen drives EPO and more red cells.

title: About spleen palpation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About spleen palpation:
options: It is done deep under the ribs
An enlarged spleen moves with breathing
A normal spleen is easy to feel
body.explanation: Spleen: deep under the ribs, hard to examine when normal; splenomegaly easy, moves with breath.
option_notes: Normal spleen is hard to examine.

title: Which test is used to look for a peptic stricture or a hiatal hernia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test is used to look for a peptic stricture or a hiatal hernia?
body.explanation: Among the other tests, the barium swallow is used for complications such as stenosis and hernia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Predisposing factors. LES hypotonia, hiatal hernia, raised abdominal pressure, slow gastric emptying, foods and drugs.
option_notes: LES hypotonia, hiatal hernia, abdominal pressure, foods and drugs.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome:
options: Can come from a corticotroph pituitary adenoma
Can come from ectopic ACTH or CRH secretion
Can come from an adrenal carcinoma
body.explanation: ACTH-dependent Cushing: normal or elevated ACTH, of pituitary origin (corticotroph adenoma) or ectopic/paraneoplastic ACTH or CRH secretion (small cell lung cancer, neuroendocrine tumours).

title: During auscultation of the abdomen, the examiner may hear:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During auscultation of the abdomen, the examiner may hear:
body.explanation: Slide 17: abdominal auscultation listens for bowel movement sounds and over the arteries (aorta, renal, iliac, femoral), where an abnormal sound (bruit) suggests e.g. an aortic aneurysm.
option_notes: Heard over the chest (pleura), not the abdomen.
Slide 17: abnormal arterial sound, e.g. aortic aneurysm.
Slide 17: bowel movement sounds are the first thing listened for.
Heard over the upper airway, not the abdomen.

title: A 40-year-old man's shoe and ring sizes have increased, with coarse features and sweating. Why is this acromegaly rather than gigantism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 40-year-old man's shoe and ring sizes have increased, with coarse features and sweating. Why is this acromegaly rather than gigantism?
options: The GH excess started in adulthood
body.explanation: Acromegaly is GH hypersecretion in adults, which enlarges the hands, feet and face. Gigantism is GH excess in childhood, before growth stops.
option_notes: GH excess in an adult is acromegaly; in a child, gigantism.
Prolactin does not separate the two.

title: Which is a cough receptor zone outside the chest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cough receptor zone outside the chest?
body.explanation: Tussigenic zones include the external auditory canal, pharynx, larynx, trachea, carina and large bronchi, plus pleura, mediastinum, pericardium, diaphragm, oesophagus and stomach.
option_notes: The retina is not a cough zone.
The ear canal (vagus branch) can trigger cough.
The spleen is not a cough zone.
The kidney is not a cough zone.

title: What can long-standing hepatic congestion lead to?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What can long-standing hepatic congestion lead to?
body.explanation: Painful hepatosplenomegaly can progress to cardiac cirrhosis and liver failure.
option_notes: Chronic congestion damages the liver into cardiac cirrhosis.

title: Which is a late sign of SVC syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a late sign of SVC syndrome?
body.explanation: Late: permanent oedema of face, neck and thorax, collateral veins, telangiectasia and cyanosis worse on coughing. Early: dizziness, tinnitus, headache, eyelid oedema, jugular turgor.
option_notes: The SVC drains the upper body.
Blocked upper-body drainage swells the face and neck.

title: A long-standing diabetic patient has had vomiting of undigested food after meals for two months. The most likely cause is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A long-standing diabetic patient has had vomiting of undigested food after meals for two months. The most likely cause is:
body.explanation: Chronic course, undigested food and diabetes point to gastroparesis, a chronic GI cause often associated with diabetes.
option_notes: Wrong: vomiting during meals would suggest it.
Wrong: a complication, not a cause.

title: Abdominal examination findings in constipation, as described in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal examination findings in constipation, as described in the lecture:
options: Palpation looks for tenderness and masses
Dullness on percussion is suggestive of fecal loading
Tympany on percussion is suggestive of fecal loading
body.explanation: Inspection: distension; palpation: tenderness, masses; percussion: tympany indicates gas, dullness suggests fecal loading.

title: A high prolactin result: which lab step checks it is not macroprolactin?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A high prolactin result: which lab step checks it is not macroprolactin?
body.explanation: Prolactin assay with PEG precipitation, then pituitary MRI.
option_notes: PEG precipitation removes macroprolactin to check the real prolactin level.
The OGTT is used to confirm acromegaly.
The insulin tolerance test explores GH and ACTH reserve.

title: A man with a known macroadenoma suddenly has a severe headache, visual loss, ophthalmoplegia, neck stiffness and drowsiness. Which statement is correct?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A man with a known macroadenoma suddenly has a severe headache, visual loss, ophthalmoplegia, neck stiffness and drowsiness. Which statement is correct?
options: It is pituitary apoplexy, an emergency that often leaves pituitary insufficiency
It is a migraine and needs no imaging
It is the usual slow mass effect of a prolactinoma
Surgery should be delayed for at least a month
body.explanation: Pituitary apoplexy is a haemorrhagic infarction of the tumour: fulminant, a medical emergency, frequently followed by partial or total pituitary insufficiency. Early transsphenoidal decompression is done within 8 days.
option_notes: Haemorrhagic infarction of the tumour: an emergency, often followed by pituitary insufficiency.
Early transsphenoidal decompression is done within 8 days.

title: Clinical examination of the adrenal glands:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Clinical examination of the adrenal glands:
options: Normal adrenals are not accessible to clinical examination
A very large tumour may become accessible
It searches for signs of hormonal hypo- or hypersecretion
Normal adrenals are palpated by bimanual flank palpation
body.explanation: In the physiological state the adrenals are not accessible to examination, unless the tumour is very large; the exam looks for signs of hormonal hypo- or hypersecretion.
option_notes: Correct: 'unless the tumor is so large'.
Correct: the aim of the examination.
Wrong: normal adrenals cannot be examined.

title: Zenker's diverticulum is best seen on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Zenker's diverticulum is best seen on:
body.explanation: A pulsion diverticulum of the pharynx.
option_notes: Ultrasound does not see the pharynx.
Contrast fills and outlines the pouch.

title: Which lower GI cause is typical in the young?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which lower GI cause is typical in the young?
body.explanation: Ulcers and varices in adults, polyps or cancer in the elderly, Meckel's in the young.
option_notes: Diverticular disease is commoner in the elderly.
Colorectal cancer is commoner in the elderly.
Angiodysplasia is commoner in the elderly.
Meckel's diverticulum is typical in the young.

title: How can diabetes be discovered?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How can diabetes be discovered?
options: By chance on a routine test
At an acute or chronic complication
Always at the very start of the disease
body.explanation: Accidental diagnosis, hyperglycaemia symptoms, or acute or chronic complications. Diagnosis comes on average 2 to 3 years after onset.
option_notes: Accidental diagnosis on a routine test.
Diabetes can be revealed by a complication.
Diagnosis comes on average 2 to 3 years after onset.

title: During liver palpation, a deep inspiration:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During liver palpation, a deep inspiration:
options: Raises the diaphragm, hiding the liver
Flattens the diaphragm, lowering the liver
Pushes the liver toward the left flank
body.explanation: Deep breath fills the lungs, flattens the diaphragm and lowers the liver towards the abdomen.
option_notes: Liver moves down towards the abdomen.

title: What does percussion find in emphysema?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does percussion find in emphysema?
body.explanation: Barrel chest, polypnoea, diffuse hyperresonance, decreased fremitus and reduced breath sounds.

title: Why is the hyperthyroid phase of thyroiditis (for example de Quervain) self-limited?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is the hyperthyroid phase of thyroiditis (for example de Quervain) self-limited?
options: The stock of stored hormone runs out
The gland starts taking up more iodine
TSH rises and switches the gland off
body.explanation: Inflammation and cell destruction release the stored FT4 and FT3. Once that stock is depleted, the toxic phase stops (auto-limited).
option_notes: Destroyed cells release their stored hormone; once it is used up, the toxic phase stops.
Thyroiditis is not driven by TSH receptor antibodies.
Iodine uptake is low in thyroiditis, not high.
TSH is suppressed during the toxic phase.

title: On a urine test strip, findings relevant to diabetes and its complications include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On a urine test strip, findings relevant to diabetes and its complications include:
body.explanation: Strips detect glycosuria; ketonuria confirms ketosis in DKA; proteinuria on strips can reveal diabetic nephropathy.
option_notes: Correct: glycosuria appears once blood glucose exceeds ~1.8 g/L (renal threshold).
Correct: ketonuria with urine test strip.
Wrong: not measured on urine strips.

title: What defines diabetes mellitus?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What defines diabetes mellitus?
options: Chronic hyperglycaemia from a lack of insulin secretion and/or action
A single high glucose after a meal
body.explanation: Chronic hyperglycaemia due to an absolute or relative deficiency of insulin secretion and/or insulin action (insulin resistance).
option_notes: Chronic hyperglycaemia from deficient insulin secretion and/or action.
One high value after a meal is not chronic hyperglycaemia.
Glycosuria is a consequence, not the definition.
Diabetes is defined by high glucose.

title: Abundant, greasy, pale, foul-smelling stools suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abundant, greasy, pale, foul-smelling stools suggest:
body.explanation: With weight loss, anaemia, bone pain.
option_notes: Fat malabsorption gives greasy, pale, foul stools.
Motor diarrhoea is urgent, not greasy.

title: If resistance rises at constant pressure, what happens?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: If resistance rises at constant pressure, what happens?
body.explanation: From Q = ΔP / R, higher resistance at the same pressure means lower flow.
option_notes: Higher R with the same ΔP gives less flow.

title: Regarding ultrasound and urinary tree X-ray of the adrenals:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding ultrasound and urinary tree X-ray of the adrenals:
options: Ultrasound detects tumours larger than 5 cm
Urinary tree X-ray studies the adrenal area for calcifications
body.explanation: Ultrasound has bad resolution, does not visualise normal adrenals and detects tumours >5 cm; X-ray of the urinary tree studies the adrenal area (calcifications).
option_notes: Wrong: it does not visualise normal adrenals.

title: What is false diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is false diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Small hard stools totalling under 300 g/day; distinguish from incontinence and non-faecal discharge.
option_notes: Large watery volumes are true diarrhoea.
Nocturnal stools suggest an organic cause, not false diarrhoea.
Frequent small hard stools under 300 g/day are false diarrhoea.

title: On ultrasound, a thyroid lobe measures 5 cm high, 2 cm wide and 2.8 cm thick. What does this show?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On ultrasound, a thyroid lobe measures 5 cm high, 2 cm wide and 2.8 cm thick. What does this show?
options: A goitre, because the thickness is above 2.5 cm
A goitre, because the height is above 4 cm
body.explanation: Normal: height 4-6 cm, width 1.5-2.5 cm, thickness 1.5-2.5 cm. A thickness above 2.5 cm means goitre.
option_notes: Thickness above 2.5 cm defines a goitre.
A thickness of 2.8 cm is above normal.
A height of 4 to 6 cm is normal.
The lobe is enlarged, not atrophic.

title: About adrenal insufficiency (AI):
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About adrenal insufficiency (AI):
options: Primary AI is a lesion of both adrenal glands
Secondary AI is due to impaired corticotropic control
Primary AI is a lesion of one adrenal gland
It is always a total deficit of every adrenal hormone
body.explanation: AI is a more or less complete deficit of glucocorticoids and/or mineralocorticoids and/or androgens; primary = lesion of both adrenals; secondary = impaired corticotropic control.
option_notes: Wrong: deficit is more or less complete.

title: What does the P wave represent?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does the P wave represent?
body.explanation: P: atrial depolarisation (right atrium slightly first). QRS: ventricular depolarisation. T: ventricular repolarisation.
option_notes: The AV delay is the PR segment.
The P wave is atrial depolarisation.

title: Abdominal ultrasound in a vomiting patient evaluates:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal ultrasound in a vomiting patient evaluates:
body.explanation: Ultrasound evaluates the gallbladder, liver, pancreas and kidneys, and can show cholecystitis or appendicitis.
option_notes: Wrong: cerebral CT is used for that.

title: The zona fasciculata:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The zona fasciculata:
options: Is part of the adrenal medulla
body.explanation: The zonation diagram shows zona fasciculata -> cortisol, a steroid hormone of the cortex.
option_notes: Wrong: aldosterone comes from the zona glomerulosa.
Wrong: it is a zone of the cortex.
Wrong: catecholamines come from the medulla.

title: Which are signs of infective endocarditis? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are signs of infective endocarditis? (choose all)
body.explanation: Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, splinter haemorrhages and Roth spots.
option_notes: Osler nodes are an endocarditis sign.
Janeway lesions are an endocarditis sign.
Pectus carinatum is a chest deformity.

title: About peptic stricture as a complication of GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About peptic stricture as a complication of GERD:
options: It is a metaplasia with cancer risk
It is the main cause of chronic cough
body.explanation: Peptic stricture: fibrosis and narrowing causing dysphagia. Barrett's is the metaplasia with cancer risk.
option_notes: Wrong: cough is a respiratory complication, not stricture.

title: What is TSH in primary hypothyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is TSH in primary hypothyroidism?
body.explanation: TSH is markedly raised; free T4 and T3 are low.
option_notes: In primary hypothyroidism the pituitary raises TSH to push the failing gland.
A normal TSH argues against primary hypothyroidism.

title: Thyroid function tests are done in vomiting to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Thyroid function tests are done in vomiting to:
options: Rule out hyperthyroidism when clinically suspected
Rule out hypothyroidism in every patient
body.explanation: Thyroid function tests: rule out hyperthyroidism if clinical suspicion arises.
option_notes: Wrong: hyperthyroidism, and only if suspected.
Wrong: hypercalcaemia is a metabolic cause, not a thyroid test.

title: In an elderly constipated patient, percussion of the left iliac fossa is dull. What does this suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In an elderly constipated patient, percussion of the left iliac fossa is dull. What does this suggest?
body.explanation: On percussion, tympany suggests gas, and dullness suggests faecal loading.
option_notes: Dullness suggests a colon filled with stool.
Ileus is suggested by absent bowel sounds.

title: Stretch marks in Cushing syndrome are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Stretch marks in Cushing syndrome are:
options: Found on the abdomen, axillae and breasts
Thin, white and under 1 mm wide
body.explanation: Skin atrophy: pink or purple stretch marks, large (>1 cm), on the abdomen, axillary area and breasts.
option_notes: Wrong: they are pink or purple and large.

title: Regarding hypoglycaemia as defined in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding hypoglycaemia as defined in the lecture:
options: It is defined by a blood glucose level <= 0.7 g/L
It is directly or indirectly responsible for 2 to 4% of deaths due to diabetes
It is defined by a blood glucose below 0.5 g/L in all diabetics
body.explanation: Hypoglycaemia is an abnormal fall in blood glucose, defined by <= 0.7 g/L (ADA), a dreaded complication responsible for 2-4% of diabetes deaths, needing emergency treatment +++.
option_notes: ADA threshold quoted on the slide.
Stated as directly or indirectly responsible for 2-4% of deaths.
Wrong threshold; the slide uses <= 0.7 g/L.

title: What do abdominal collateral veins suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What do abdominal collateral veins suggest?
body.explanation: Collateral veins are a sign of portal hypertension.
option_notes: Collateral veins are a sign of portal hypertension.
Heart failure gives oedema and hepatomegaly.
Appendicitis gives right iliac fossa pain.

title: When is the diagnosis of GERD clinical?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When is the diagnosis of GERD clinical?
body.explanation: Typical forms are diagnosed clinically; tests are for atypical cases, red flags, poor response or age over 50.
option_notes: Heartburn with regurgitation is enough in a typical case.
Endoscopy is for alarm signs, atypical cases or age over 50.
pH-metry is for atypical or resistant cases.

title: Pathological changes in diabetic peripheral neuropathy include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Pathological changes in diabetic peripheral neuropathy include:
options: Ischaemia of the vessels that supply the nerves
Segmental demyelination affecting the Schwann cell, slowing nerve conduction
Axonal hypertrophy that speeds up nerve conduction
Autoimmune anti-myelin antibodies as the main mechanism
body.explanation: Two pathologic changes: ischaemia of nerve-supplying vessels and segmental demyelination of Schwann cells slowing conduction.
option_notes: Not on the slide; hyperglycaemia is the driver.

title: Which test is recommended after recent antibiotics?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test is recommended after recent antibiotics?
body.explanation: Clostridium difficile toxin assay for recent antibiotic use.
option_notes: HIV is not linked to recent antibiotics.
Thyroid tests do not look for an infection.
Colonoscopy alone does not identify the toxin.
Antibiotics favour C. difficile, so the toxin is tested.

title: An advantage of upper GI endoscopy given in the lecture is that it:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An advantage of upper GI endoscopy given in the lecture is that it:
options: Combines diagnosis with the option of immediate biopsy
Measures serum potassium during the exam
body.explanation: Endoscopy combines diagnostic evaluation with the option for immediate biopsy.
option_notes: Wrong: the cerebral CT and neurological exam look for raised ICP.
Wrong: electrolytes are a lab test.
Wrong: that is the hCG test.

title: What does hyperresonance indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does hyperresonance indicate?
body.explanation: Hyperresonance: excess air (pneumothorax, emphysema). Dullness: pleurisy, pachypleuritis, consolidation.

title: What X-ray shows a hydropneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What X-ray shows a hydropneumothorax?
body.explanation: Mixed syndrome: a pleural opacity surmounted by a hyperlucent area devoid of markings.
option_notes: Fluid below, air above, with a flat level.

title: Which scales grade dyspnoea? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which scales grade dyspnoea? (choose all)
body.explanation: NYHA and the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scale.

title: Which drugs are listed in the lecture as causes of hypothyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drugs are listed in the lecture as causes of hypothyroidism?
body.explanation: Drug-induced hypothyroidism: antithyroid drugs, lithium, amiodarone, tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) and checkpoint inhibitors. Levothyroxine is the treatment, not a cause.
option_notes: Amiodarone is a listed cause of drug-induced hypothyroidism.
Checkpoint inhibitors are a listed cause.
Levothyroxine treats hypothyroidism; it does not cause it.

title: A patient with a pituitary adenoma has right eyelid ptosis. Which structure is being compressed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with a pituitary adenoma has right eyelid ptosis. Which structure is being compressed?
options: The oculomotor nerve in the cavernous sinus
body.explanation: Lateral extension into the cavernous sinus compresses cranial nerves III, IV and VI, causing diplopia; ptosis comes from the oculomotor nerve (III), which lifts the eyelid.
option_notes: The oculomotor nerve lifts the eyelid; it runs in the cavernous sinus.
Chiasm compression causes visual field loss.
Abducens palsy causes diplopia, not ptosis.
The posterior pituitary has no role in eyelid movement.

title: Which is a cause of a cavitary syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cause of a cavitary syndrome?
body.explanation: Tuberculous cavern, lung abscess, excavated cancer, ruptured hydatid cyst.
option_notes: An effusion is a fluid syndrome.
A TB cavern is a cavity.

title: Which second-line test screens for coeliac disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which second-line test screens for coeliac disease?
body.explanation: Confirmed by duodenal biopsies.
option_notes: HIV serology is another second-line test, not for coeliac disease.
Ferritin does not diagnose coeliac disease.

title: All of these are listed as manifestations of acromegaly EXCEPT:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: All of these are listed as manifestations of acromegaly EXCEPT:
body.explanation: Acromegaly gives diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance, not hypoglycaemia. Colonic polyps, hypertension with LVH, hypercalciuria, type IV hypertriglyceridaemia and goitre are all on the slide.
option_notes: GH raises glucose: diabetes, not hypoglycaemia.

title: Imaging in phaeochromocytoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Imaging in phaeochromocytoma:
options: CT and MRI are the examinations of choice for localisation
MIBG scintigraphy searches the whole body for ectopic sites and metastases
Ultrasound is the examination of choice
body.explanation: CT and MRI localise the tumour (intra-abdominal or thoracic in almost all cases); MIBG completes them by whole-body search for multiple, ectopic or metastatic lesions, even very small ones.

title: On the lecture's summary slide, the metabolic and systemic causes of vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the lecture's summary slide, the metabolic and systemic causes of vomiting include:
body.explanation: Metabolic/systemic: uraemia, DKA, electrolyte disorders, hepatic failure, endocrine (pregnancy, adrenal insufficiency). Gastric outlet obstruction is gastrointestinal.

title: About the DN4 questionnaire:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the DN4 questionnaire:
options: A total score of 4/10 is the cut-off for neuropathic pain
It asks about burning, painful cold and electric shocks
It includes examination items: hypoaesthesia to touch and prick, and pain caused by brushing
body.explanation: DN4: 10 items (7 interview, 3 examination); cut-off for neuropathic pain is 4/10.
option_notes: 19 is the maximum of the Toronto score.

title: Which findings favour Cushing's syndrome over simple obesity?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which findings favour Cushing's syndrome over simple obesity?
options: Fat spread evenly over the limbs
body.explanation: Cushing's: truncal obesity with thin limbs (proximal amyotrophy), wide purple striae, thin skin and bruising.
option_notes: Proximal amyotrophy is typical of cortisol excess.
Wide purple striae point to Cushing's.
Thin skin and bruising point to Cushing's.
In Cushing's the limbs are thin, not fat.

title: What must progressive dysphagia in an adult be assumed to be?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What must progressive dysphagia in an adult be assumed to be?
body.explanation: Until proven otherwise, investigated by upper endoscopy.
option_notes: Achalasia is usually not progressive in this way.
Globus is not a real swallowing difficulty.
Progressive dysphagia in an adult is cancer until proven otherwise.
GERD gives heartburn; a stricture comes later.

title: Regarding physiological versus pathological reflux:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding physiological versus pathological reflux:
options: Physiological reflux is transient and postprandial
Pathological reflux is by definition asymptomatic
Physiological reflux causes no mucosal damage
Pathological reflux involves frequent or prolonged episodes
body.explanation: Physiological reflux is transient, postprandial, asymptomatic, with no mucosal damage; pathological reflux has frequent or prolonged episodes causing symptoms, inflammation or complications.
option_notes: Wrong: pathological reflux causes symptoms, inflammation or complications.
Correct: no mucosal damage in physiological reflux.

title: Positions used for the digital rectal examination in constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Positions used for the digital rectal examination in constipation:
options: Squatting during straining, to look for rectal prolapse
body.explanation: Squatting during straining to check for rectal prolapse; knee-chest or left lateral position.
option_notes: Wrong: the slide lists squatting, knee-chest or left lateral.
Wrong: not listed on the slide.

title: The hormone pattern of autoimmune (primary) adrenal insufficiency is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hormone pattern of autoimmune (primary) adrenal insufficiency is:
options: High ACTH, low cortisol, low aldosterone
Low ACTH, low cortisol, normal aldosterone
High ACTH, high cortisol, normal aldosterone
Low ACTH, high cortisol, low aldosterone
body.explanation: Slide 61: autoimmune AI = high ACTH (hyperpigmentation), low cortisol + low aldosterone; secondary AI = low ACTH, low cortisol, normal aldosterone.

title: Per the illustrated rectal examination sequence:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Per the illustrated rectal examination sequence:
options: Apply gentle pressure to the anus before advancing
Assess anal tone while advancing the finger
Sweep the rectum clockwise and anticlockwise
body.explanation: Slide 19 steps: examine skin, lubricate right index, gentle pressure, advance and assess anal tone, clockwise then anticlockwise sweeps, clean off lubricant.

title: Which heart failure has stiff, thick chambers?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which heart failure has stiff, thick chambers?
body.explanation: Diastolic: can't fill, stiff thick chambers. Systolic: can't pump, stretched thin chambers.
option_notes: Systolic chambers are stretched and thin.
Diastolic chambers are stiff and thick.

title: Which lab abnormality occurs in hypothyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which lab abnormality occurs in hypothyroidism?
body.explanation: Organ-damage tests in hypothyroidism: macrocytic anaemia, dilutional hyponatraemia, hypercholesterolaemia, hyperprolactinaemia (slide 40).
option_notes: Cholesterol rises, not falls, in hypothyroidism.

title: Which layer suffers ischaemia in stable angina?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which layer suffers ischaemia in stable angina?
body.explanation: Stable angina causes subendocardial ischaemia, releasing adenosine and bradykinin, which cause pain.
option_notes: The subendocardium is the most vulnerable layer.

title: After a course of antibiotics, a patient has a white plaque on the tongue. What is the most likely cause?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: After a course of antibiotics, a patient has a white plaque on the tongue. What is the most likely cause?
body.explanation: Oral candidiasis is a fungal infection that leaves a white plaque on the tongue.
option_notes: Candida gives a white plaque on the tongue.

title: Which antibodies are specific to Graves' disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which antibodies are specific to Graves' disease?
body.explanation: Positive TSH receptor antibodies (TRAb, TSI) are highly specific.
option_notes: Anti-TPO antibodies point to Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Anti-thyroglobulin antibodies are used for Hashimoto's, not Graves'.
TSH receptor antibodies (TRAb, TSI) are highly specific to Graves'.
Antinuclear antibodies belong to systemic autoimmune disease such as lupus.

title: Recent antibiotic use with diarrhoea suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Recent antibiotic use with diarrhoea suggests:
body.explanation: A key point of the history.
option_notes: Cholera is not linked to antibiotics.
Giardia is a parasite unrelated to antibiotics.
Coeliac disease is unrelated to antibiotics.

title: Coronary artery disease in a diabetic may be discovered through:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Coronary artery disease in a diabetic may be discovered through:
options: Atypical chest pain such as epigastric ache or exertional dyspnoea
Typical angina-like chest pain, which is the usual presentation in diabetics
body.explanation: CoD: atypical chest pain (epigastric ache, exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, lipothymia), uncommon typical pain, silent ischaemia, acute complications, heart failure.
option_notes: Wrong: typical chest pain is uncommon.

title: A 28-year-old woman with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a normal build and no family history of diabetes develops polyuria over 2 weeks, with ketones in the urine. W…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 28-year-old woman with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a normal build and no family history of diabetes develops polyuria over 2 weeks, with ketones in the urine. Which type fits best?
options: Type 1, as suggested by a personal history of autoimmune disease and ketosis
Type 2, since autoimmunity is typical of type 2
Type 2, because the onset is acute
body.explanation: Type 1: acute onset in a young, normal-to-thin person, ketosis at onset, no family history and a history of autoimmune disease. Autoantibodies and other autoimmune diseases point to type 1.
option_notes: Autoimmune history, normal build, acute onset and ketosis: type 1.
Autoimmunity points to type 1, not type 2.
Acute onset fits type 1, not type 2.

title: In arginine vasopressin deficiency:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In arginine vasopressin deficiency:
options: The cause is a hypothalamic-pituitary disruption
Polyuria comes first and drives polydipsia
The kidney fails to respond to normal AVP
body.explanation: Diagram: (1) hypothalamic-pituitary disruption, (2) deficient AVP release, (3) polyuria, (4) polydipsia.

title: Which drugs cause constipation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drugs cause constipation?
body.explanation: Opioids, antidepressants, antihistamines and iron.
option_notes: Antibiotics are not the listed cause.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Haematemesis. Vomiting red or black blood; lesion above the angle of Treitz.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Vomiting red or black blood; lesion above the angle of Treitz.

title: Which diarrhoea stops with fasting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which diarrhoea stops with fasting?
body.explanation: Osmotic and motor diarrhoea stop with fasting; secretory and malabsorptive persist.
option_notes: Exudative diarrhoea does not depend on eating.
No osmotic load when fasting, so it stops.

title: A patient drinks about 5 litres a day and urinates a lot. Which simple test separates diabetes mellitus from other causes of polyuria?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient drinks about 5 litres a day and urinates a lot. Which simple test separates diabetes mellitus from other causes of polyuria?
options: Blood glucose with a urine strip for glucose
body.explanation: Diabetic polyuria comes from glycosuria (osmotic diuresis); a high glucose with glycosuria separates it from causes without hyperglycaemia.
option_notes: Hyperglycaemia with glycosuria confirms diabetes mellitus.
Cortisol does not separate the causes.

title: Defecography in constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Defecography in constipation:
options: Identifies rectal prolapse or structural defects
Measures pressures in the anal sphincter and rectum
body.explanation: Defecography identifies rectal prolapse or structural defects.
option_notes: Wrong: that is thyroid function tests.

title: What is the main cause of endemic goitre?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the main cause of endemic goitre?
body.explanation: Iodine deficiency is the main cause of endemic goitre and myxoedematous cretinism.
option_notes: Graves' gives a goitre with hyperthyroidism, not endemic goitre.
Thyroid cancer is not a cause of endemic goitre.
Iodine deficiency is the main cause of endemic goitre.
Amiodarone affects thyroid function but does not cause endemic goitre.

title: Toxic multinodular goitre:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Toxic multinodular goitre:
options: Occurs in older patients with long-standing euthyroid multinodular goitre
May extend substernally, so signs of compression must be sought
Shows multiple functioning nodules or patchy uptake on scintigraphy
Typically presents with exophthalmos and diplopia in young women aged 20 to 40 years
body.explanation: It emerges slowly in older patients with long-standing euthyroid MNG; the goitre may be large and substernal (look for compression); scintigraphy shows multiple functioning nodules or patchy uptake.
option_notes: Correct: older patients, long-standing euthyroid MNG.
Correct: may extend substernally; look for compression.
Correct: multiple functioning nodules or patchy distribution.
Wrong: eye signs and young women suggest Graves'.

title: After several bouts of forceful vomiting, a patient vomits fresh blood but stays stable. The most likely complication is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: After several bouts of forceful vomiting, a patient vomits fresh blood but stays stable. The most likely complication is:
body.explanation: Forceful vomiting tearing the mucosa at the gastro-oesophageal junction, leading to bleeding: Mallory-Weiss.
option_notes: Wrong: a cause, not a complication.
Wrong: gives fever, cough and dyspnoea.

title: A diabetic with an ACR of 150 mg/g (AER around 150 mg/24 h) is classified as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A diabetic with an ACR of 150 mg/g (AER around 150 mg/24 h) is classified as:
body.explanation: A1 ACR < 30 mg/g; A2 30-300 mg/g; A3 > 300 mg/g; nephrotic syndrome usually > 2200 mg/24 h.

title: Which are infectious causes of dysentery? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are infectious causes of dysentery? (choose all)
body.explanation: Entamoeba, CMV, E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella.
option_notes: Entamoeba is a parasite that invades the colon.

title: Clinical features that may be seen in thyroid cancer include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Clinical features that may be seen in thyroid cancer include:
options: Stridor, an inspiratory sign of upper airway obstruction
Exophthalmos with chemosis and diplopia as the presenting signs
body.explanation: Most common presentation is a nodule/mass; features include hoarseness, cervical lymphadenopathy and stridor (harsh high-pitched inspiratory sound of upper airway obstruction).
option_notes: Correct: stridor indicates upper airway obstruction.

title: What is the normal QRS duration?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the normal QRS duration?
body.explanation: Normal adult QRS is 0.08 to 0.12 s; longer is a wide QRS.
option_notes: Too long; this is a wide QRS.

title: In confirmed adrenal insufficiency, an 8 a.m. ACTH that is high means:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In confirmed adrenal insufficiency, an 8 a.m. ACTH that is high means:
body.explanation: Etiologic workup first step: 8 am ACTH high = peripheral origin; normal or low = central origin.
option_notes: Wrong: central origin has normal or low ACTH.
Wrong: pituitary causes have low ACTH.
Wrong: ACTH is raised by loss of feedback.

title: Which causes a retracted consolidation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which causes a retracted consolidation?
body.explanation: Retracted: intrinsic or extrinsic bronchial stenosis, parenchymal destruction. Non-retracted: pneumonia, infarction, tuberculous pneumonia.
option_notes: A blocked bronchus collapses the lung behind it.

title: During a 75 g OGTT, a patient with a high IGF-1 keeps a high GH level. What does this show?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During a 75 g OGTT, a patient with a high IGF-1 keeps a high GH level. What does this show?
options: Acromegaly: GH is not suppressed by glucose
body.explanation: Work-up: IGF-1 and GH during a 75 g glucose tolerance test; glucose normally inhibits GH, and lack of inhibition confirms acromegaly.
option_notes: No GH suppression with a high IGF-1 confirms acromegaly.
The test looks at GH, not only glucose.

title: What does the X-ray show in a pleural effusion?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does the X-ray show in a pleural effusion?
options: A cavity with a fluid level
body.explanation: Homogeneous density with a meniscus margin and blunting of the costophrenic angle.
option_notes: Fluid rises along the wall: a meniscus.
A cavity with a level is an abscess.

title: In a patient with a suspicious thyroid lump, which history items must be checked carefully?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a patient with a suspicious thyroid lump, which history items must be checked carefully?
options: Family history and exposure to radiation
body.explanation: The work-up of a suspicious lump starts with a full clinical review, carefully evaluating family history and any exposure to radiation, then the examination and thyroid function tests.
option_notes: Family history and radiation exposure must be checked carefully.
A viral infection points to subacute thyroiditis, not cancer risk.
Diet alone is not the key history item for a suspicious lump.
The pill is not a thyroid cancer risk factor.

title: Which exam confirms the diagnosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which exam confirms the diagnosis?
body.explanation: Endoscopy shows inflammation, ulcers and bleeding and allows targeted biopsy.
option_notes: A chest X-ray does not see the colon.
Endoscopy shows the lesions and allows biopsies.

title: A 35-year-old man has headaches, low libido and erectile dysfunction. Prolactin is very high and he has bitemporal visual field loss. What does the visual loss…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 35-year-old man has headaches, low libido and erectile dysfunction. Prolactin is very high and he has bitemporal visual field loss. What does the visual loss tell you?
options: It is unrelated to the tumour
body.explanation: Mass effects of a prolactinoma happen with macroadenomas only. Prolactinomas are classed as micro or macro/invasive on MRI.
option_notes: Mass effect with field loss means a macroadenoma.
Microadenomas are too small to reach the chiasm.
Visual loss shows a tumour, not a drug effect.
Bitemporal loss is caused by the tumour pressing the chiasm.

title: Upper GI endoscopy in a vomiting patient is indicated for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Upper GI endoscopy in a vomiting patient is indicated for:
options: Complications such as upper GI bleeding, oesophagitis or gastritis
body.explanation: Indications: suspected mucosal lesion, obstruction, complications (upper GI bleeding, oesophagitis or gastritis).

title: Myxoedema coma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Myxoedema coma:
options: Is associated with hypoglycaemia and hyponatraemia
Is a frequent and benign condition, mostly seen in young adults
body.explanation: Rare end stage of untreated hypothyroidism, in the elderly: weakness, stupor, hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoventilation, then shock and death.
option_notes: Wrong: rare and can lead to shock and death.

title: On percussion of the normal abdomen:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On percussion of the normal abdomen:
options: Most of the abdomen is tympanic
The hypogastrium is dull if the bladder is full
The left iliac region is always dull
body.explanation: All the abdomen is tympanic except the right hypochondriac quadrant (liver) and the hypogastric region if the bladder is full.
option_notes: Not an exception on the slide.

title: In the diagnostic algorithm for constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the diagnostic algorithm for constipation:
options: The first step is history, physical examination and digital rectal examination
With alarm symptoms, functional tests are done first
Without alarm symptoms, functional tests point toward primary constipation
With alarm symptoms, the work-up points toward primary constipation
body.explanation: After history, exam and DRE: alarm symptoms -> colonoscopy, imaging, labs (secondary); no alarm symptoms -> functional tests (primary).
option_notes: Wrong: alarm symptoms lead to colonoscopy, imaging, labs.
Wrong: alarm symptoms lead toward secondary constipation.

title: A woman has a pale face and a completely hairless axilla, as in the lecture photos. This fits:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A woman has a pale face and a completely hairless axilla, as in the lecture photos. This fits:
body.explanation: The photos follow the hypopituitarism slide: pallor and depilation are part of the triad pallor, depilation, depigmentation.
option_notes: Acromegaly gives coarse, oily, sweaty skin.
Not associated with pallor and depilation on the slides.

title: The paraclinical work-up of peripheral artery disease includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The paraclinical work-up of peripheral artery disease includes:
options: Arterial Doppler of the lower limbs
CT angiography systematically in every patient
body.explanation: ABI, arterial Doppler; CT angiography/MRA only if candidate for angioplasty or bypass. ABI measurement is pictured on p76.
option_notes: Only if angioplasty or bypass is considered.

title: Which drug lowers LES tone?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drug lowers LES tone?
body.explanation: Nitrates, theophylline, anticholinergics, calcium channel blockers, progesterone, sedatives.
option_notes: Paracetamol does not affect LES tone.
Amoxicillin does not affect LES tone.
Nitrates relax smooth muscle, including the LES.

title: According to the lecture, what does the patient say in English to test tactile fremitus?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the lecture, what does the patient say in English to test tactile fremitus?
body.explanation: Toy boat in English, 44 in Arabic, 33 in French, while the examiner feels the vibrations.
option_notes: The Arabic phrase, not the English one.
The English phrase given in the lecture.
Used to examine the throat, not fremitus.

title: How many regions is the abdomen divided into?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How many regions is the abdomen divided into?
body.explanation: The abdomen is described in 9 regions (slide 9): three rows of three, from the hypochondriac and epigastric regions down to the iliac and hypogastric regions.
option_notes: No standard scheme uses six regions.
The lecture divides the abdomen into 9 regions.

title: On the Bristol Stool Form Scale:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the Bristol Stool Form Scale:
options: Type 1 = separate hard lumps, like nuts, hard to pass
Type 4 = like a sausage or snake, smooth and soft
Type 7 = watery, no solid pieces, entirely liquid
Type 2 = soft blobs with clear-cut edges
body.explanation: Type 1 hard lumps like nuts; type 4 smooth soft sausage; type 7 entirely liquid. Soft blobs are type 5.
option_notes: Wrong: type 2 is sausage-shaped but lumpy.

title: What triad defines acute cholangitis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What triad defines acute cholangitis?
body.explanation: Acute cholangitis: pain, fever and jaundice.

title: Which GI symptoms occur in right heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which GI symptoms occur in right heart failure?
body.explanation: GI tract congestion causes anorexia, GI distress and weight loss.
option_notes: Bloody stools are not a congestion sign.
Gut congestion causes anorexia and discomfort.

title: Why does a high midnight cortisol support Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why does a high midnight cortisol support Cushing's syndrome?
options: Cortisol normally falls to its lowest at night; that circadian dip is lost
Cortisol is normally highest at midnight
It shows the adrenal is enlarged
body.explanation: Initial tests look for excessive cortisol secretion and disruption of its circadian rhythm (high midnight cortisol).
option_notes: Loss of the night-time dip is a sign of cortisol excess.
Cortisol peaks in the early morning, not at midnight.
It is a hormone test, not imaging.

title: A patient with a phaeochromocytoma that secretes all the time has hypertension resistant to treatment. Which other finding is possible?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with a phaeochromocytoma that secretes all the time has hypertension resistant to treatment. Which other finding is possible?
body.explanation: With permanent secretion, hypertension of variable level, resistant to usual treatment, is sometimes associated with orthostatic hypotension. Hypermetabolism gives weight loss, fever, thermophobia and glucose intolerance.
option_notes: Permanent secretion can come with orthostatic hypotension.
Hypermetabolism gives weight loss and heat intolerance.

title: Regarding the diagnosis of Cushing disease:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the diagnosis of Cushing disease:
options: High cortisol with inadequate dexamethasone suppression defines hypercortisolism
Hypercortisolism with a non-suppressed ACTH points to an ACTH-dependent cause such as Cushing disease
Pituitary MRI usually shows a macroadenoma compressing the chiasm
Normal suppression after dexamethasone confirms the disease
body.explanation: Slide 14: high cortisol + inadequate suppression in the DXM test = hypercortisolism; with an ACTH that is not suppressed, the cause is ACTH-dependent, and in Cushing disease pituitary MRI usually shows an ACTH-secreting microadenoma. Ectopic ACTH also gives a non-suppressed ACTH (adrenal lecture).
option_notes: A non-suppressed ACTH means an ACTH-dependent cause: Cushing disease or ectopic ACTH.
Inadequate, not normal, suppression points to hypercortisolism.

title: What equation links flow, pressure and resistance?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What equation links flow, pressure and resistance?
body.explanation: Flow equals the pressure difference divided by resistance.

title: Which angina type gives ST elevation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which angina type gives ST elevation?
body.explanation: Transmural ischaemia from spasm gives ST elevation; stable and unstable give ST depression.
option_notes: Spasm causes transmural ischaemia: ST elevation.

title: Toxic and drug-induced causes of chronic vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Toxic and drug-induced causes of chronic vomiting include:
body.explanation: Long-term medication side effects (NSAIDs, opioids, antibiotics) and chronic alcohol use.

title: Physical examination findings and their orientation in GI bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Physical examination findings and their orientation in GI bleeding:
options: Epigastric tenderness suggests ulcer or gastritis
Signs of portal hypertension suggest varices
Rectal examination checks for haemorrhoids, fissure or rectal mass
body.explanation: Epigastric tenderness -> ulcer or gastritis; signs of liver disease or portal hypertension -> varices; rectal exam confirms melena/haematochezia and looks for haemorrhoids, fissure or rectal mass.
option_notes: Wrong: varices are suggested by portal hypertension signs.

title: Which causes diastolic left heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which causes diastolic left heart failure?
body.explanation: Diastolic causes: long-standing hypertension, aortic stenosis, hypertrophic and restrictive cardiomyopathy.
option_notes: The thick, stiff wall fills poorly.

title: Boerhaave syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Boerhaave syndrome:
options: Is caused by a sudden rise in intra-abdominal pressure from forceful vomiting
Leads to leakage of contents into the mediastinum
body.explanation: Boerhaave: oesophageal rupture, life-threatening, from a sudden increase in intra-abdominal pressure during forceful vomiting, with leakage into the mediastinum.

title: What height above the sternal angle is positive?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What height above the sternal angle is positive?
body.explanation: A sustained rise over 4 cm above the sternal angle after pressure on the liver is positive.
option_notes: A sustained rise over 4 cm is positive.
A visible vein alone is not enough.

title: Cushing's syndrome is confirmed and the 8 a.m. plasma ACTH is undetectable. What is the next step?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cushing's syndrome is confirmed and the 8 a.m. plasma ACTH is undetectable. What is the next step?
options: Chest CT to look for an ectopic source
body.explanation: Low ACTH means ACTH-independent Cushing's (a cortisol-secreting adrenal tumour), so the next step is adrenal localising studies.
option_notes: Low ACTH means an adrenal source: image the adrenals.
Pituitary MRI is for ACTH-dependent Cushing's.
The high-dose test is for ACTH-dependent cases.
An ectopic source makes ACTH, so ACTH would be high.

title: How does chronic lung disease cause right heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How does chronic lung disease cause right heart failure?
body.explanation: Hypoxia constricts pulmonary arterioles, raising pulmonary pressure and causing right ventricular hypertrophy and failure: cor pulmonale.
option_notes: Systemic pressure affects the left heart.
Hypoxia narrows lung arteries and raises pulmonary pressure.

title: How is acromegaly confirmed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How is acromegaly confirmed?
options: High IGF-1 and no GH suppression during a 75 g OGTT
body.explanation: IGF-1, then GH during a 75 g glucose load: GH above 0.4 µg/L confirms it. Prolactin is also measured because it is often co-secreted.
option_notes: A single random GH is unreliable because GH is pulsatile.
High IGF-1 and GH not suppressed by a glucose load confirm it.
GHRH is not the confirmation test.
Prolactin is often co-secreted (high), and it does not confirm acromegaly.

title: About 24-hour oesophageal pH-metry:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About 24-hour oesophageal pH-metry:
options: It is the reference test for pathological acid reflux
It is particularly useful in atypical symptoms or NERD
It is mainly used to detect non-acid reflux
body.explanation: 24h pH monitoring is the reference test for pathological acid reflux, particularly useful when symptoms are atypical or in NERD.
option_notes: Wrong: non-acid reflux is detected by impedancemetry.

title: Which are oral signs of deficiency?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are oral signs of deficiency?
body.explanation: Glossitis (B12) and angular cheilitis (iron).
option_notes: A gum tattoo is not a deficiency sign.
Tonsil stones are not a deficiency sign.

title: What is the most common cause of right heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the most common cause of right heart failure?
body.explanation: Right heart failure is often caused by left heart failure, making it biventricular.
option_notes: Left heart failure raises lung pressure and then strains the right heart.
Pneumonia is not the most common cause.
Anaemia is not the most common cause.
Hyperthyroidism is not the most common cause.

title: In the lecture's sequence, the stimuli first activate:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the lecture's sequence, the stimuli first activate:
body.explanation: Stimuli activate the vomiting centre, then the abdominal vagal afferents, then the diaphragm and abdominal muscles contract and the LES relaxes.
option_notes: Wrong: the LES relaxes at the end of the sequence.

title: What is the leading cause of death worldwide?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the leading cause of death worldwide?
body.explanation: Cardiovascular disease causes about 17.7 million deaths a year.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Oesophageal dysphagia. Food sticks behind the sternum; mechanical or motor disorders.
option_notes: Another box. Oesophageal phase: involuntary peristalsis.
This is the box at the arrow. Oesophageal: food sticks behind the sternum.
Another box. Organic: solids then liquids, progressive.
Another box. Endoscopy: the first-line test.

title: Which valve disease is linked to AFib?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which valve disease is linked to AFib?
body.explanation: Structural causes: hypertension, coronary disease, valvular disease especially mitral, heart failure and cardiomyopathy.
option_notes: Mitral disease enlarges the left atrium.

title: Plasma ACTH at 8-9 a.m. in confirmed Cushing syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Plasma ACTH at 8-9 a.m. in confirmed Cushing syndrome:
options: Low ACTH points to an ACTH-independent cause
After low ACTH, the next step is adrenal localising studies
An inappropriately normal ACTH rules out an ACTH-secreting tumour
High ACTH points to an adrenal adenoma
body.explanation: Low ACTH means ACTH-independent Cushing (adrenal tumours), then adrenal localising studies; high or inappropriately normal ACTH means an ACTH-secreting neoplasm (pituitary or ectopic), then HDDST.
option_notes: Wrong: inappropriately normal ACTH also suggests ACTH secretion.

title: A 35-year-old has a painful, tender, firm thyroid two weeks after a flu-like illness, with palpitations. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 35-year-old has a painful, tender, firm thyroid two weeks after a flu-like illness, with palpitations. What is the most likely diagnosis?
body.explanation: Neck pain, a tender firm gland and a recent viral infection are the features of de Quervain thyroiditis, with a transient toxic phase.
option_notes: Painful gland after a viral illness.
Toxic adenoma is a painless nodule.
Hashimoto's is usually painless and hypothyroid.

title: A young woman has secondary amenorrhoea and a mildly raised prolactin. What must be ruled out before thinking of a pituitary tumour?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A young woman has secondary amenorrhoea and a mildly raised prolactin. What must be ruled out before thinking of a pituitary tumour?
body.explanation: Pregnancy is the first physiological cause of hyperprolactinaemia and of amenorrhoea. Nipple stimulation, exercise, stress and sleep can also raise prolactin.
option_notes: Pregnancy is the first physiological cause of high prolactin and amenorrhoea.
Acromegaly is not the first thing to rule out.
Apoplexy is a sudden emergency, not this picture.
Cushing's disease does not explain a high prolactin.

title: Which blood count findings fit Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which blood count findings fit Cushing's syndrome?
body.explanation: Cortisol excess gives polycythaemia, a high white count with neutrophils (PNN) and lymphopenia, plus hypokalaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia and impaired glucose tolerance.

title: Once anterior hypophyseal insufficiency (AHI) is diagnosed, the slides say to request:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Once anterior hypophyseal insufficiency (AHI) is diagnosed, the slides say to request:
body.explanation: Slide: the diagnosis of AHI should lead to pituitary imaging: pituitary MRI.
option_notes: Not the imaging named for AHI.
Not the imaging named for AHI.
Not the imaging named for AHI.

title: Loss of axillary and pubic hair in hypopituitarism is due to absence of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Loss of axillary and pubic hair in hypopituitarism is due to absence of:
body.explanation: Slide: loss of axillary and pubic hair, due to the absence of adrenal and gonadal androgens.
option_notes: Not the cause given on the slide.
Vasopressin deficiency causes polyuria, not hair loss.

title: Slow transit constipation is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Slow transit constipation is characterised by:
options: Fewer than 3 bowel movements per week
Frequent need for digital maneuvers to evacuate
body.explanation: Slow transit: <3 BM/week, bloating, abdominal pain, hard stools; causes colonic inertia, spastic colon.
option_notes: Wrong: digital maneuvers characterise outlet dysfunction.

title: Which is a differential of right-sided hepatomegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a differential of right-sided hepatomegaly?
body.explanation: Right: liver ptosis, Riedel lobe, colon flexure, right kidney, gallbladder. Left: stomach, transverse colon, pancreatic body.
option_notes: The stomach lies on the left.
The pancreatic body is a left-sided differential.
The transverse colon is a left-sided differential.
A Riedel lobe is a normal tongue-like extension of the right lobe that can mimic hepatomegaly.

title: Which are signs of hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are signs of hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: Heat intolerance, fine tremor, tachycardia, weight loss.
option_notes: Increased heat production makes patients intolerant of heat.
A fine tremor of the hands is typical.

title: The cervical examination in digestive semiology includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The cervical examination in digestive semiology includes:
body.explanation: Cervical exam: lymph nodes (left supraclavicular ++), thyroid, vascular auscultation; the oesophagus is not accessible.
option_notes: Not listed; thyroid is assessed for mobility with swallowing.

title: Physiological effects of corticosteroids:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Physiological effects of corticosteroids:
options: Adrenal androgens have a minor role compared with gonadal sex hormones
Adrenal androgens are the main source of sex hormones
Glucocorticoids have no effect on growth
Glucocorticoids act only on carbohydrate metabolism
body.explanation: Glucocorticoids: metabolic actions (carbohydrate, protein, lipid, hydro-electrolytic), neurologic and muscular effects, growth; adrenal androgens: minor role compared with gonadal sex hormones.
option_notes: Correct: as stated on the slide.
Wrong: growth is one of the listed effects.
Wrong: also protein, lipid and hydro-electrolytic metabolism.

title: A 55-year-old obese man with hypertension has a fasting glucose of 1.35 g/L on two check-up samples. He has no symptoms. Which statement is correct?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 55-year-old obese man with hypertension has a fasting glucose of 1.35 g/L on two check-up samples. He has no symptoms. Which statement is correct?
options: This is an accidental diagnosis, and chronic complications should be assessed now
He does not have diabetes because he has no symptoms
Complications cannot exist yet since diabetes was just found
Ketoacidosis is the usual way type 2 diabetes is revealed
body.explanation: Diabetes can be found by chance. Diagnosis comes on average 2 to 3 years after the real onset, so in type 2 diabetes chronic complications are assessed at discovery.
option_notes: Found by chance, and complications may already be present.
Two fasting values ≥ 1.26 g/L make the diagnosis.
Diagnosis comes 2 to 3 years after onset, so complications may exist.

title: In the Toronto clinical neuropathy score:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the Toronto clinical neuropathy score:
options: A total of 9 indicates moderate neuropathy
A total of 6 indicates no neuropathy
Sensory testing is performed on the heel
body.explanation: Reflex absent = 2, reduced = 1; total 0-19; <= 5 none, 6-8 mild, 9-11 moderate, >= 12 severe; sensory testing on the first toe.

title: Which part of the chest is barely sensitive to pain?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which part of the chest is barely sensitive to pain?
body.explanation: The lung and tracheobronchial tree are weakly sensitive; the pleura, mediastinum and chest wall are intensely sensitive.
option_notes: The parietal pleura is very sensitive.
The lung itself has few pain fibres.

title: A thin 19-year-old has had 3 weeks of thirst, frequent urination and weight loss. Today he has vomiting, abdominal pain, fruity breath and deep, rapid breathin…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A thin 19-year-old has had 3 weeks of thirst, frequent urination and weight loss. Today he has vomiting, abdominal pain, fruity breath and deep, rapid breathing. What is the most likely situation?
options: Type 2 diabetes revealed by a hyperosmolar state
body.explanation: Young, thin, acute onset with hyperglycaemia symptoms, then ketosis (fruity breath, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain) and Kussmaul breathing: type 1 diabetes revealed by ketoacidosis.
option_notes: Young, thin, acute symptoms then ketoacidosis: type 1.
A hyperosmolar state occurs in older type 2 patients, without ketosis.
Fruity breath and Kussmaul breathing are not gastroenteritis.
Hypoglycaemia does not cause thirst and polyuria.

title: Non-cardiac chest pain in GERD:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Non-cardiac chest pain in GERD:
options: Is a typical oesophageal symptom alongside heartburn
body.explanation: Cardiac/thoracic symptom: non-cardiac chest pain mimicking angina; such atypical presentations may mislead diagnosis and delay management.
option_notes: Wrong: it is an extra-digestive (atypical) manifestation.
