Wrong: it is non-cardiac by definition.
Wrong: not among the red flags.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Oral phase. Voluntary transport of the bolus to the oropharynx.
option_notes: Another box. Oesophageal phase: involuntary peristalsis.
This is the box at the arrow. Oral phase: voluntary.
Another box. Endoscopy: the first-line test.

title: Regarding the clinical features of hyperprolactinaemia:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the clinical features of hyperprolactinaemia:
options: They are the same whatever the cause of the prolactin excess
Galactorrhoea may be spontaneous or induced
Galactorrhoea is always permanent, never intermittent
Mass effect is seen with microadenomas
body.explanation: The slide states that the manifestations of PRL excess are the same regardless of the cause; galactorrhoea can be spontaneous/induced and permanent/intermittent. Mass effects occur with macroadenomas only.
option_notes: Slide: same manifestations regardless of cause.
Wrong: it can be permanent or intermittent.
Wrong: mass effect occurs with macroadenomas only.

title: Per the clinical orientation table, a hepatomegaly due to cirrhosis is typically:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Per the clinical orientation table, a hepatomegaly due to cirrhosis is typically:
options: Irregular or nodular at the surface
body.explanation: Clinical orientation table: cirrhosis gives a firm or hard liver with a sharp or irregular border, an irregular or nodular surface and no pain. A soft, smooth, painful liver is cardiac; intense pain points to an abscess.
option_notes: Wrong: soft and smooth fits the cardiac liver.
Wrong: pain is absent in cirrhosis; intense pain suggests an abscess.

title: Physical examination findings of mild ketoacidosis include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Physical examination findings of mild ketoacidosis include:
options: Capillary blood glucose usually below 1.10 g/L
body.explanation: Mild DKA: capillary glucose usually >2.50 g/L, ketonuria on strip, high ketonaemia. Coma belongs to severe forms.
option_notes: Wrong: that is a normal fasting value.

title: Why are stools pale (acholic) when the bile duct is completely blocked?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why are stools pale (acholic) when the bile duct is completely blocked?
options: Bilirubin no longer reaches the gut, so no stercobilinogen colours the stool
Too much bilirubin is excreted in stool
Iron is lost in the stool
body.explanation: Bilirubin excreted into the gut becomes urobilinogen and stercobilinogen, which colours stool. With an obstruction, none reaches the gut.
option_notes: No bilirubin in the gut means no stercobilinogen.
Bilirubin cannot reach the gut, so less is excreted.
Blood darkens stool; it does not make it pale.
Iron is unrelated to stool pallor here.

title: Which drug is given for a suspected peptic ulcer bleed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drug is given for a suspected peptic ulcer bleed?
body.explanation: NSAIDs and aspirin are causes.
option_notes: PPIs reduce acid and help ulcer healing.

title: In moderate to severe ketoacidosis, signs of extracellular dehydration listed are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In moderate to severe ketoacidosis, signs of extracellular dehydration listed are:
body.explanation: Extracellular dehydration: dry skin, arterial hypotension, tachycardia. Intracellular: thirst, dry mucous membranes, sunken eyes.

title: Per the lecture's classification, conditions listed as microvascular complications are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Per the lecture's classification, conditions listed as microvascular complications are:
body.explanation: The microvascular slide lists retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy and cardiomegaly with heart failure; stroke is macrovascular.
option_notes: Per the lecture slides; many textbooks call it diabetic cardiomyopathy rather than microangiopathy.

title: Non-digestive infectious causes of acute vomiting listed in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Non-digestive infectious causes of acute vomiting listed in the lecture:
body.explanation: Infectious: sepsis and pyelonephritis.

title: Which sputum is typical of acute pulmonary oedema?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which sputum is typical of acute pulmonary oedema?
body.explanation: Frothy sputum is white, fluid and aerated, sometimes salmon-pink. Pearly (Laennec) sputum is seen in asthma.
option_notes: Fluid in the alveoli gives frothy, pink sputum.
Chocolate sputum suggests an amoebic abscess.

title: A 32-year-old woman has normal stool frequency but strains, feels incompletely emptied and sometimes presses with her fingers to pass stool. Which type of cons…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 32-year-old woman has normal stool frequency but strains, feels incompletely emptied and sometimes presses with her fingers to pass stool. Which type of constipation is this?
body.explanation: Outlet dysfunction: difficulty evacuating, often needing a digital manoeuvre, with a sense of incomplete evacuation.
option_notes: Difficulty evacuating with digital manoeuvres is typical.
Slow transit gives fewer than 3 stools a week with bloating.
IBS-C centres on abdominal discomfort and bloating.

title: Acute adrenal insufficiency can be triggered by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Acute adrenal insufficiency can be triggered by:
body.explanation: Acute AI: natural evolution of slow AI, revealed by an intercurrent illness (infection, trauma, surgery), therapeutic error (stopping treatment, diuretics, laxatives, salt-free diet) or haemorrhage on healthy adrenals.

title: Autoantibodies and other autoimmune diseases point to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Autoantibodies and other autoimmune diseases point to:
body.explanation: On the comparison table, associated autoimmune diseases and autoantibodies are present in type 1 only.
option_notes: Autoantibodies and autoimmune diseases point to type 1.
They are present in type 1 only.

title: A brief reflux after a meal, with no symptoms and no mucosal damage, is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A brief reflux after a meal, with no symptoms and no mucosal damage, is:
body.explanation: Physiological reflux is transient, postprandial and asymptomatic, with no mucosal damage.
option_notes: Pathological reflux is frequent or prolonged, causing symptoms or lesions.

title: Which test screens for celiac disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test screens for celiac disease?
body.explanation: Second-line tests: TSH, HIV, anti-transglutaminase, stool parasitology; then EGD with duodenal biopsies.
option_notes: HIV serology is a different test.
Ferritin shows iron deficiency, not coeliac disease.
Anti-transglutaminase antibodies screen for coeliac disease.

title: Dysphagia to solids then liquids, progressive, suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Dysphagia to solids then liquids, progressive, suggests:
body.explanation: Such as cancer or peptic stricture.
option_notes: Achalasia affects liquids from the start.
A growing narrowing blocks solids first, then liquids.

title: Emergency measures in GI bleeding include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Emergency measures in GI bleeding include:
options: Hospitalisation in an emergency or intensive care unit
Withholding fluids until endoscopy is done
Gastric tube and urinary catheter for monitoring
Monitoring haemoglobin only, without urine output
body.explanation: Measures: ICU/emergency admission, two large-bore IV lines, work-up, vascular filling (crystalloids, transfusion), oxygen, gastric tube and urinary catheter, continuous surveillance of BP, pulse, urine output and mental status.
option_notes: Wrong: vascular filling with crystalloids is given.
Wrong: urine output is part of surveillance.

title: Which food lowers LES tone?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which food lowers LES tone?
body.explanation: Fats, chocolate, caffeine, alcohol, mint and spicy foods lower LES tone.

title: Which is a sign of increased work of breathing?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a sign of increased work of breathing?
body.explanation: Accessory muscle use, nasal flaring, intercostal, subcostal and suprasternal retractions, grunting, pursed lips, paradoxical breathing.
option_notes: Nasal flaring shows extra effort to breathe.

title: Menstrual disorders caused by hyperprolactinaemia include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Menstrual disorders caused by hyperprolactinaemia include:
body.explanation: Slide 8 lists menstrual disorders as primary or secondary amenorrhoea and oligomenorrhoea: prolactin excess reduces or stops cycles.
option_notes: Not listed: prolactin excess reduces cycles.
Not listed: oligomenorrhoea (fewer cycles) is described.

title: In a synacthen test, cortisol rises to 22 µg/dL at 60 minutes. How is this read?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a synacthen test, cortisol rises to 22 µg/dL at 60 minutes. How is this read?
body.explanation: An insufficient rise, below 18 µg/dL, confirms adrenal insufficiency; a rise to 18 or more is normal.
option_notes: Confirmation needs a peak below 18 µg/dL.

title: During the act of vomiting:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During the act of vomiting:
options: The diaphragm and abdominal muscles contract strongly
Stomach contents are forcefully ejected through the mouth
body.explanation: Strong contractions of the diaphragm and abdominal muscles plus relaxation of the LES lead to forceful ejection of stomach contents through the mouth.

title: Which is a management option for AFib?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a management option for AFib?
body.explanation: Management follows the ABC pathway: stroke prevention, rhythm control, ablation, left atrial appendage occlusion.

title: In the classification table, features of type 1 compared with type 2 diabetes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the classification table, features of type 1 compared with type 2 diabetes:
options: Hyperglycaemia symptoms are marked +++ in type 1
Familial history is stronger in type 1
Cardiovascular risk factors are present in type 1
body.explanation: Table: type 1 has +++ hyperglycaemia symptoms, autoantibodies, frequent ketosis; familial history is +++ in type 2; CV risk factors are type 2.
option_notes: Wrong: + in type 1 vs +++ in type 2.
Wrong: CV risk factors - in type 1.

title: Which clinical setting raises prolactin as a side effect of a test?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which clinical setting raises prolactin as a side effect of a test?
options: A 75 g oral glucose tolerance test
body.explanation: The TRH stimulation test is listed among the causes of hyperprolactinaemia, because TRH stimulates prolactin release.

title: The frequency of type 1 diabetes among diabetics, per the table, is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The frequency of type 1 diabetes among diabetics, per the table, is:
body.explanation: Table: type 1 10-15%, type 2 85-90%.

title: How does long-standing hypertension cause heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How does long-standing hypertension cause heart failure?
body.explanation: Higher arterial pressure makes pumping harder, causing hypertrophy, squeezed coronaries, higher oxygen demand and weaker contractions.
option_notes: Hypertension does not rupture the cusps.
Pumping against high pressure thickens, then weakens, the muscle.

title: Which conditions can cause hyperprolactinaemia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which conditions can cause hyperprolactinaemia?
body.explanation: Physiological (pregnancy, nursing, stress...), hypothyroidism, chronic renal insufficiency and severe liver failure are on the lecture's table.
option_notes: Pregnancy and nursing raise prolactin physiologically.
Hyperthyroidism is not listed as a cause.

title: Regarding the pelvic floor and defecation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the pelvic floor and defecation:
options: Pelvic floor muscles should contract during normal defecation
In outlet dysfunction, pelvic floor muscles contract or fail to relax
This obstruction causes a sensation of incomplete evacuation
Outlet dysfunction is a form of secondary constipation
body.explanation: Normally the pelvic floor relaxes to let stool pass; in outlet dysfunction it contracts or fails to relax, obstructing expulsion with a feeling of incomplete evacuation.
option_notes: Correct: paradoxical contraction or failure to relax.
Wrong: it is a mechanism of primary (functional) constipation.

title: A positive Schellong test is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A positive Schellong test is:
options: A fall in systolic BP of at least 20 mmHg within 3 min of standing
A fall in diastolic BP of at least 10 mmHg within 3 min of standing
A fall in systolic BP of 10 mmHg after 10 min
A rise in BP on standing
body.explanation: Systolic hypotension is present in about 90%, with orthostatic dizziness or syncope; positive Schellong = SBP fall >= 20 mmHg or DBP fall >= 10 mmHg within 3 min of standing.

title: Part of the oral cavity examination in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Part of the oral cavity examination in the lecture:
body.explanation: The internal face of the cheeks is part of the oral cavity exam; thyroid, nodes and vascular auscultation belong to the cervical examination.

title: Why can a normal haemoglobin be misleading?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why can a normal haemoglobin be misleading?
options: It measures iron rather than blood loss
In acute bleeding, haemodilution has not yet occurred
body.explanation: A normal Hb does not rule out recent bleeding.
option_notes: Hb measures haemoglobin concentration, not iron.
Haemodilution has not yet happened, so Hb is still normal.
Hb does not rise in acute bleeding.
The analyser is not the issue.

title: Hypoglycaemia may be discovered:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hypoglycaemia may be discovered:
options: Incidentally on self-monitoring of blood glucose, with no symptoms
Through complications such as seizures or coma
Only in patients who are not treated with insulin
body.explanation: Circumstances of discovery: clinical symptoms, incidental finding on self-monitoring (asymptomatic), or complications such as seizures and coma.
option_notes: HbA1c is not mentioned as a mode of discovery.
Insulin overdose is itself a leading cause.

title: Which examination is mandatory in chronic diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which examination is mandatory in chronic diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Along with hydration, nutrition and extra-abdominal signs.
option_notes: The rectal exam is always done (mass, impaction, blood).

title: Which are associated with acromegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are associated with acromegaly?
body.explanation: Sleep apnoea, colonic polyps, hypertension, LVH, and diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance (not hypoglycaemia).
option_notes: Macroglossia and thick soft tissues narrow the airway.
GH excess causes hypertension and LVH.
GH raises glucose: diabetes, not hypoglycaemia.

title: A young woman has low BMI, bilateral lid retraction and proptosis, a diffuse soft non-tender goitre and fine tremor. Expected results include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A young woman has low BMI, bilateral lid retraction and proptosis, a diffuse soft non-tender goitre and fine tremor. Expected results include:
options: Raised TSH reflecting loss of negative feedback
body.explanation: This Graves' case shows thyrotoxicosis + goitre + eye signs; hyperthyroidism gives suppressed TSH, raised FT4/FT3, and TRAb are specific.
option_notes: Correct: TSH is suppressed in hyperthyroidism.
Wrong: TSH is suppressed, not raised.

title: General items of the physical examination in jaundice include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: General items of the physical examination in jaundice include:
body.explanation: Physical exam: GCS, PS, BMI, asterixis, foetor hepaticus, oedema, vitals.

title: What are the four steps of the chest examination?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What are the four steps of the chest examination?
body.explanation: Inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation, then signs are grouped into syndromes.
option_notes: Imaging is not a step of the exam.
Wrong order, and imaging is not a step.

title: Which electrolyte disorder causes constipation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which electrolyte disorder causes constipation?
body.explanation: Hypercalcaemia and hypokalaemia are metabolic causes.
option_notes: Hyponatraemia is not the listed cause.
Hypomagnesaemia is not the listed cause.

title: Where does dysenteric pain often focus?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where does dysenteric pain often focus?
body.explanation: Severe cramps along the colon, often focused on the left iliac fossa, with an urgent urge to defecate.
option_notes: The right hypochondrium suggests the liver or gallbladder.
Colonic cramps of dysentery focus on the left iliac fossa (sigmoid and rectum).
Umbilical pain suggests the small bowel.

title: A 38-year-old woman has central obesity, wide purple striae, proximal muscle weakness and hypertension. Which is the best first screening test?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 38-year-old woman has central obesity, wide purple striae, proximal muscle weakness and hypertension. Which is the best first screening test?
body.explanation: The first step is to confirm hypercortisolism. The 1 mg overnight dexamethasone test is the best screening test (24 h urinary free cortisol and midnight salivary cortisol also help). ACTH, imaging and the high-dose test come after, to find the cause.
option_notes: The best screening test: confirm hypercortisolism first.
ACTH is measured once hypercortisolism is confirmed, to find the cause.
The high-dose test separates the causes; it is not for screening.

title: What is right heart failure from lung disease called?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is right heart failure from lung disease called?
body.explanation: Right heart failure secondary to chronic pulmonary problems is cor pulmonale.
option_notes: Cor pulmonale is right heart failure from lung disease.
Tamponade is fluid compressing the heart.
Dressler syndrome is pericarditis after a heart attack.

title: What lies directly above the pituitary gland?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What lies directly above the pituitary gland?
body.explanation: Sella turcica below, optic chiasm above, cavernous sinuses on both sides.
option_notes: The cavernous sinuses lie on each side, not above.
The optic chiasm lies just above the gland.
The sphenoid sinus lies below the sella.
The fourth ventricle is in the posterior fossa, far from the pituitary.

title: Which are signs of pulmonary oedema? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are signs of pulmonary oedema? (choose all)
body.explanation: Dyspnoea, orthopnoea, PND, crackles and frothy sputum.
option_notes: Fluid in the alveoli gives crackles.
Jaundice is not a lung sign.

title: When is abdominal CT indicated?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When is abdominal CT indicated?
body.explanation: Severe or atypical symptoms, suspected perforation or abscess, or an inconclusive diagnosis.
option_notes: CT is for complications such as perforation or abscess.
It is not needed in every case.
It is not limited to children.

title: Which are true of pituitary apoplexy?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are true of pituitary apoplexy?
options: Sudden, severe headache with visual loss and ophthalmoplegia
body.explanation: Bleeding into a pituitary tumour: fulminant, emergency, often partial or total pituitary insufficiency; early transsphenoidal decompression.
option_notes: The fulminant picture of bleeding into a tumour.
It needs urgent care and early decompression.
Partial or total pituitary insufficiency often follows.

title: What is orthopnoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is orthopnoea?
body.explanation: Orthopnoea: dyspnoea in decubitus. Platypnoea: dyspnoea on moving from supine to upright.
option_notes: Breathlessness on sitting up is platypnoea.

title: Laboratory findings of the cholestasis syndrome include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Laboratory findings of the cholestasis syndrome include:
body.explanation: Cholestasis: conjugated bilirubin, GGT, ALP, hypercholesterolaemia, prolonged PT, 5'nucleotidase.
option_notes: Slide 16: 'conjugated or unconjugated or both' is for jaundice in general; cholestasis raises conjugated bilirubin, so an isolated unconjugated rise is not cholestatic.

title: What does endothelial dysfunction lead to?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does endothelial dysfunction lead to?
body.explanation: Impaired NO, oxidative stress, inflammation and leucocyte adhesion drive atherosclerosis, plaque rupture and atherothrombosis.
option_notes: Less NO and more inflammation drive atherosclerosis and thrombosis.

title: What is a pneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is a pneumothorax?
body.explanation: Air in the pleural space presses on and collapses the lung.
option_notes: Air in the pleural space collapses the lung.
Pus in the lung is an abscess.

title: What causes the polyuria of diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What causes the polyuria of diabetes?
body.explanation: Polyuria is due to glycosuria (osmotic diuresis); polydipsia follows the polyuria.
option_notes: Glucose in the urine pulls water: osmotic diuresis.
Drinking follows polyuria; it does not cause it.
Kidney failure is not the mechanism.

title: What separates regurgitation and rumination from true vomiting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What separates regurgitation and rumination from true vomiting?
options: No nausea or feeling of vomiting
body.explanation: Both occur without nausea or the feeling of vomiting, unlike vomiting which is usually preceded by nausea and is an active process.
option_notes: Wrong: blood is not the distinguishing feature.
Wrong: fever is not the distinguishing feature.
Wrong: bile is not the distinguishing feature.

title: Where do clots form in atrial fibrillation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where do clots form in atrial fibrillation?
body.explanation: Stagnant blood in the left atrial appendage forms clots that can cause embolic stroke.
option_notes: Blood stagnates in the left atrial appendage.

title: Circumstances of discovery of diabetic nephropathy include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Circumstances of discovery of diabetic nephropathy include:
body.explanation: CoD: systematic annual check-up, oedematous/nephrotic syndrome, hypertension, proteinuria with strips.

title: Which is a cause of motor diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cause of motor diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Motor: hyperthyroidism, diabetes, carcinoid, gastrectomy, IBS; post-prandial and urgent.

title: Regarding the liver and spleen on examination:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the liver and spleen on examination:
options: The normal spleen is easily felt in every patient
The liver cannot be examined at all
The normal spleen is hard to examine
body.explanation: Liver and spleen are listed as partially accessible; the spleen is hard to examine when normal and easy to feel when enlarged.
option_notes: Slide 3: liver and spleen partially accessible.
Normal spleen is hard to examine.
Liver is partially accessible and palpated under right ribs.
Slide 15: hard to examine when normal.

title: Secondary adrenal insufficiency differs from primary by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Secondary adrenal insufficiency differs from primary by:
options: Hypotension and digestive signs are rare
body.explanation: Secondary AI: no hyperpigmentation (ACTH deficiency, pale depigmentation); hypoglycaemia is more frequent; hypotension and digestive disorders are rare as mineralocorticoid secretion is preserved; no hyperkalaemia.

title: A 26-year-old woman has galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea. Her pregnancy test is negative. She has been taking metoclopramide for nausea, and her prolactin is 70 n…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 26-year-old woman has galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea. Her pregnancy test is negative. She has been taking metoclopramide for nausea, and her prolactin is 70 ng/mL. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia from a dopamine antagonist
body.explanation: Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist. Drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia is usually mild, about 25 to 100 ng/mL; only a few agents (such as risperidone) push it above 200 ng/mL.
option_notes: A dopamine antagonist causing mild hyperprolactinaemia (25-100 ng/mL).
A mild level with a culprit drug points to the drug first.
Adrenal insufficiency does not cause galactorrhoea.

title: What distinguishes Pierre Marie osteoarthropathy from simple clubbing?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What distinguishes Pierre Marie osteoarthropathy from simple clubbing?
body.explanation: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy: painful clubbing, hypertrophic extremities with effusions, vasomotor disorders, arthralgia and periostitis of long bones; hereditary or paraneoplastic.

title: Regarding diabetic foot wounds and gangrene:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding diabetic foot wounds and gangrene:
options: Neuropathic foot wounds may go undetected, get infected and lead to gangrene
In peripheral vascular disease, foot wounds heal slowly, contributing to gangrene
Foot ulcers are typically very painful, so they are noticed early
Gangrene is classed only as a microvascular complication
body.explanation: Neuropathy lets wounds go unnoticed and get infected; PVD slows healing; gangrene appears in the macroangiopathy section.
option_notes: Neuropathy makes them painless and undetected.
Gangrene is shown under macroangiopathy (p75, p41).

title: A 45-year-old woman has weight gain, cold intolerance, a hoarse voice and night-time tingling in her hands. Which diagnosis links these?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 45-year-old woman has weight gain, cold intolerance, a hoarse voice and night-time tingling in her hands. Which diagnosis links these?
body.explanation: Hoarseness and carpal tunnel syndrome are among the signs of hypothyroidism shown in the lecture, with weight gain and cold sensitivity.
option_notes: All four fit hypothyroidism, including carpal tunnel.
Graves' gives weight loss and heat intolerance.
Acromegaly causes carpal tunnel but not cold intolerance and weight gain.
Subacute thyroiditis starts with painful thyrotoxicosis.

title: On the diabetes semiology slide, diabetic neuropathy is shown as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the diabetes semiology slide, diabetic neuropathy is shown as:
options: Pain, tingling or numbness in the hands or feet
Painless proximal muscle hypertrophy of both thighs
Episodes of fever with neck pain
body.explanation: The semiology slide lists paresthesia; the neuropathy figure shows pain, tingling or numbness in hands or feet, often related to diabetes.
option_notes: Correct: shown on the neuropathy panel.

title: On the diabetic retinopathy images, growth of abnormal blood vessels characterises:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the diabetic retinopathy images, growth of abnormal blood vessels characterises:
body.explanation: NPDR image labels aneurysm, hard exudate and haemorrhage; the proliferative image labels growth of abnormal vessels (neovessels from ischaemia).
option_notes: A lens disorder, not shown on fundus image.

title: A non-secreting pituitary macroadenoma compresses the pituitary stalk, and prolactin is mildly raised. What explains the high prolactin?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A non-secreting pituitary macroadenoma compresses the pituitary stalk, and prolactin is mildly raised. What explains the high prolactin?
body.explanation: A lesion of the hypophyseal stalk (stalk effect) raises prolactin, so a non-secreting adenoma can come with mild hyperprolactinaemia. The slides list nonsecretory adenoma with the pituitary tumours.
option_notes: Compressing the stalk blocks dopamine, so prolactin rises.
A second tumour is not needed to explain it.

title: What X-ray line marks a pneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What X-ray line marks a pneumothorax?
body.explanation: A thin opaque line around the collapsed lung is the visceral pleura, with a hyperlucent area devoid of markings beyond it.
option_notes: The visceral pleura line outlines the collapsed lung.
The angle is where fluid collects.

title: In panhypopituitarism, the slides match each deficiency to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In panhypopituitarism, the slides match each deficiency to:
options: GH: short stature or features of low GH in adults
body.explanation: The panhypopituitarism chart: GH - short stature/low GH features; FSH/LH - central hypogonadism; TSH - central hypothyroidism; ACTH - central ACI; PRL - failure of postpartum lactation.

title: Further history items for jaundice are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Further history items for jaundice are:
options: Family history of jaundice or cancer
body.explanation: All are listed on the medical history slide.

title: What is the normal respiratory rate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the normal respiratory rate?
body.explanation: Normal breathing is calm, regular and unconscious at about 16 cycles per minute.
option_notes: About 16 breaths per minute is normal.

title: What is Cushing's disease?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is Cushing's disease?
body.explanation: Cushing's disease is the pituitary cause; Cushing's syndrome is cortisol excess of any cause.
option_notes: Any cortisol excess is Cushing's syndrome.
An adrenal tumour gives ACTH-independent Cushing's syndrome.
Ectopic ACTH is an ACTH-dependent cause but not 'Cushing's disease'.
Cushing's disease is the pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma.

title: In the thyroid dysfunction aetiology table, subacute thyroiditis and painless thyroiditis are classified as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the thyroid dysfunction aetiology table, subacute thyroiditis and painless thyroiditis are classified as:
options: Hyperthyroidism from hormone overproduction by a functional nodule
body.explanation: The table splits thyrotoxicosis into hyperthyroidism (Basedow, pregnancy, functional nodule) and destructive thyroiditis (subacute, painless).
option_notes: Wrong: the hypothyroid (insufficiency) column holds Hashimoto's disease; subacute and painless thyroiditis sit under thyrotoxicosis.
Wrong: normal column holds simple goitre and tumours.
Wrong: functional nodule is a separate hyperthyroid cause.

title: What is the normal liver span on the midclavicular line?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the normal liver span on the midclavicular line?
body.explanation: The upper limit is found by percussion from top down; normal right liver span is under 12 cm.
option_notes: Too small; a normal liver spans more than this.
The normal span on the midclavicular line is under 12 cm.
25 cm would be a very large liver.
20 cm is enlarged, and the limit is not a fixed value.

title: A child from a remote mountain area with iodine-poor food has a goitre, short stature and intellectual delay. What is the most likely picture?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A child from a remote mountain area with iodine-poor food has a goitre, short stature and intellectual delay. What is the most likely picture?
body.explanation: Iodine deficiency is the main cause of endemic goitre and of myxoedematous cretinism.
option_notes: Iodine deficiency causes endemic goitre and myxoedematous cretinism.
Graves' gives hyperthyroidism, not growth and intellectual delay.
Toxic multinodular goitre is a disease of older adults.
Riedel's thyroiditis is a rare fibrosing thyroiditis in adults.

title: A 40-year-old man's rings and shoes no longer fit, his skin is thick, oily and sweaty, and his face has coarsened. Most likely diagnosis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 40-year-old man's rings and shoes no longer fit, his skin is thick, oily and sweaty, and his face has coarsened. Most likely diagnosis?
body.explanation: GH excess after growth has stopped: big hands and feet, coarse face, oily sweaty skin. Gigantism is GH excess before the growth plates close.
option_notes: Gigantism is GH excess before the growth plates close, in children.
GH excess in an adult: big hands and feet, coarse face, oily skin.
Hypothyroidism does not enlarge hands and feet.
Paget disease enlarges bones (skull) but does not cause these soft tissue changes.

title: What is the ratio of AFib to flutter?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the ratio of AFib to flutter?
body.explanation: About 50 to 60 million have AFib versus 2 to 6 million with flutter.
option_notes: About 9 AFib cases for each flutter case.

title: Which liver is hard, nodular and painful?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which liver is hard, nodular and painful?
body.explanation: Neoplastic: diffuse or localised, hard, irregular, nodular, painful.
option_notes: A tumour gives a hard, irregular, nodular liver that can be painful.
Cholestasis gives a smooth, firm liver.
Storage disease gives a smooth, painless liver.
A normal liver is not palpable or is soft.

title: Which drugs provoke spasm to diagnose Prinzmetal?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drugs provoke spasm to diagnose Prinzmetal?
body.explanation: A provocative test with ergonovine or acetylcholine.
option_notes: These are used in other tests.

title: In most adults, the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis develop:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In most adults, the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis develop:
options: Only after the patient becomes comatose
body.explanation: Gradual onset of signs and symptoms (a few days), except in children, pregnant women, the elderly, or a malfunctioning insulin pump.
option_notes: Correct: gradual onset, a few days.
Wrong: onset is gradual; faster in listed exceptions.
Wrong: that describes the 2-3 year diagnostic delay of diabetes.
Wrong: mild forms precede altered consciousness.

title: Foot-care advice for patients with diabetic neuropathy includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Foot-care advice for patients with diabetic neuropathy includes:
options: Clean feet daily and use moisturising lotions
Perform daily foot self-examination, using a mirror if needed
Check shoes for tears and sharp edges
Inspect for redness, cuts, swelling and blisters
Walk barefoot to improve foot sensation
body.explanation: Active prevention: daily cleaning and moisturiser, daily self-exam with a mirror, check shoes, inspect for redness, cuts, swelling, blisters.
option_notes: Not advised; contradicts protecting insensate feet.

title: About the zonation of the adrenal gland:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the zonation of the adrenal gland:
options: The cortex makes up 80-90% of the gland
The medulla makes up 40-50% of the gland
body.explanation: The zonation diagram shows a cortex of 80-90% (glomerulosa -> aldosterone, fasciculata -> cortisol, reticularis -> weak androgens) and a medulla of 10-20%.
option_notes: Wrong: reticularis makes weak androgens; cortisol comes from the fasciculata.

title: In the 'Pituitary and friends' summary, oxytocin acts on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the 'Pituitary and friends' summary, oxytocin acts on:
body.explanation: The summary slide shows oxytocin arrows to the uterus and to the mammary gland (with prolactin).
option_notes: Shown: oxytocin and prolactin to mammary gland.
The kidney is the target of ADH.
The thyroid is the target of TSH.

title: Which are first-line tests in chronic diarrhoea? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which are first-line tests in chronic diarrhoea? (choose all)
body.explanation: CBC, CRP, electrolytes, liver tests, electrophoresis, calcium, vitamin D, ferritin, albumin.
option_notes: Colonoscopy comes after the first-line tests.
Capsule endoscopy is a later test.

title: Non-haemolytic unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia may be due to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Non-haemolytic unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia may be due to:
body.explanation: Non-haemolytic (error in conjugation): Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, neonatal jaundice.

title: Cardiovascular causes of acute vomiting listed in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cardiovascular causes of acute vomiting listed in the lecture:
body.explanation: Cardiovascular: myocardial infarction and aortic dissection.

title: A 68-year-old with a long-standing euthyroid multinodular goitre now has palpitations and weight loss. The goitre is large and extends behind the sternum. Besi…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 68-year-old with a long-standing euthyroid multinodular goitre now has palpitations and weight loss. The goitre is large and extends behind the sternum. Besides thyroid tests, what must the examination look for?
body.explanation: This is a toxic multinodular goitre: older patient, slow move from the non-toxic to the toxic phase, a goitre that can be large and substernal. The slides say to look for signs of compression.
option_notes: A large substernal goitre can compress the trachea, oesophagus or veins.
Exophthalmos belongs to Graves', not to multinodular goitre.
A thyroglossal cyst is a midline congenital lump, not this picture.
Lid lag can occur in any thyrotoxicosis but is not the specific concern here.

title: About secondary constipation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About secondary constipation:
options: It is more recent in onset
It is usually chronic and isolated
It may be associated with non-digestive conditions
body.explanation: Secondary constipation is more recent, occurs as a symptom or complication of an underlying condition, digestive or non-digestive.
option_notes: Wrong: chronic and isolated describes primary constipation.
Wrong: it results from an identifiable condition.

title: Which features favour hemoptysis over haematemesis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which features favour hemoptysis over haematemesis?
body.explanation: Hemoptysis: respiratory history, coughing, bright red frothy blood. Haematemesis: vomiting, dark non-aerated blood, food debris.
option_notes: Bright red, frothy blood with cough is haemoptysis.
Dark blood with food is haematemesis.

title: A patient had a long nosebleed overnight and vomits dark blood in the morning. What must be considered before an upper GI source?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient had a long nosebleed overnight and vomits dark blood in the morning. What must be considered before an upper GI source?
body.explanation: Differential diagnoses of haematemesis: haemoptysis, swallowed epistaxis, gingival bleeding and coloured food or drugs.
option_notes: Blood from the nose can be swallowed then vomited.

title: What does high ACTH with cortisol excess indicate?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does high ACTH with cortisol excess indicate?
body.explanation: ACTH-dependent (high ACTH): pituitary or ectopic source. ACTH-independent (low ACTH): adrenal source.
option_notes: An adrenal adenoma gives a low ACTH.
High ACTH: pituitary or ectopic source.
High ACTH with high cortisol is not normal.

title: A 50-year-old woman has a firm goitre and hypothyroidism. Which antibody result fits Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 50-year-old woman has a firm goitre and hypothyroidism. Which antibody result fits Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
options: Negative antibodies with a hot nodule
body.explanation: The etiological antibody tests for hypothyroidism are anti-TPO and anti-Tg. Stimulating TSH receptor antibodies are the Graves' marker; anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies belong to Addison's disease.
option_notes: Anti-TPO and anti-Tg are the antibodies of Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Stimulating TSH receptor antibodies are the Graves' marker.
Anti-21-hydroxylase antibodies belong to Addison's disease.
A hot nodule fits a toxic adenoma, not hypothyroidism.

title: In cardiac autonomic neuropathy, per the slides:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In cardiac autonomic neuropathy, per the slides:
options: Orthostatic hypotension is sought by measuring BP supine and after 3 minutes standing
Orthostatic hypotension is a fall of 30 mmHg systolic and/or 10 mmHg at 3 minutes
Permanent tachycardia and cardiac denervation can cause silent myocardial ischaemia
BP is measured after 10 minutes sitting
body.explanation: BP supine then after 3 min of orthostatism: loss of 30 mmHg SBP and/or 10 mmHg; permanent tachycardia, denervation, silent ischaemia.
option_notes: Per the lecture slides; most guidelines use >= 20 mmHg systolic or >= 10 diastolic.

title: Which laboratory findings are listed for secondary adrenal insufficiency?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which laboratory findings are listed for secondary adrenal insufficiency?
body.explanation: Secondary AI: no volume depletion and no hyperkalaemia, but hyponatraemia, normocytic anaemia and moderate lymphocytosis; ACTH low-normal with low cortisol.
option_notes: Aldosterone is preserved, so no hyperkalaemia.

title: Which stool colour suggests cholestasis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which stool colour suggests cholestasis?
body.explanation: Cholestasis: pruritus, dark urine, pale acholic stools, steatorrhoea, xanthoma, and ADEK vitamin deficiency.
option_notes: Dark green stools are not typical of cholestasis.
No bile reaches the gut, so stools are pale.

title: Factors involved in IBS-C include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Factors involved in IBS-C include:
options: Disruption of the normal gut-brain interaction
body.explanation: IBS-C factors: increased visceral hypersensitivity, gut-brain interaction disruption, psychological factors such as stress or anxiety.

title: What is the ventricular response in flutter?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the ventricular response in flutter?
body.explanation: Flutter's ventricular response is often regular; AFib's is irregularly irregular.
option_notes: A fixed AV block makes the response regular.

title: By how much does AFib raise stroke risk?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: By how much does AFib raise stroke risk?
body.explanation: Atrial fibrillation increases stroke risk about five-fold.

title: What does atrophic glossitis suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does atrophic glossitis suggest?
body.explanation: Atrophic glossitis: B12 deficiency. Angular cheilitis: iron deficiency. White tongue plaques: candidiasis. Aphthous ulcers: e.g. IBD.
option_notes: Iron overload does not cause glossitis.
Atrophic glossitis suggests vitamin B12 deficiency.
Hepatitis A does not cause glossitis.

title: Regarding fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of thyroid lumps:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of thyroid lumps:
options: U1-U2 lesions need FNAC only if high risk for malignancy
All U2 lesions must be aspirated, whatever the malignancy risk
U5 lesions do not need FNAC
body.explanation: FNAC should be carried out on all U3-U5 lesions; U1 and U2 do not need FNAC unless high risk for malignancy.
option_notes: Wrong: U2 needs FNAC only if high risk.

title: Small, hard stools totalling under 300 g/day suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Small, hard stools totalling under 300 g/day suggest:
body.explanation: A differential diagnosis of diarrhoea.
option_notes: Small hard stools under 300 g/day are not true diarrhoea.
Secretory diarrhoea gives large watery volumes.

title: Biological diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Biological diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma:
options: Urinary methoxylated derivatives are the key test
VMA is the reference test today
Plasma catecholamines are easy to interpret
body.explanation: Urine: catecholamines, especially methoxylated derivatives (urinary+++); VMA is less reliable and no longer used; plasma catecholamines have a short half-life and are hard to interpret; plasma metanephrines are very useful.
option_notes: Wrong: less reliable, no longer used.
Wrong: short half-life, hard to interpret.

title: When is tactile fremitus increased?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: When is tactile fremitus increased?
body.explanation: Increased in pneumonia (consolidation). Decreased or abolished in pleurisy, pneumothorax, atelectasis and emphysema bullae.
option_notes: Air in the pleura blocks vibrations.

title: The initial recommended lab tests in vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The initial recommended lab tests in vomiting include:
body.explanation: Initial labs: CBC, electrolytes, renal function, glucose, hCG in women of reproductive age, thyroid tests if suspected, urinalysis (ketones).

title: Above which blood glucose level does glucose appear in the urine?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Above which blood glucose level does glucose appear in the urine?
body.explanation: Once blood glucose exceeds 1.8 g/L, the tubular reabsorption threshold, sugar passes into the urine.
option_notes: 1.10 g/L is the upper normal fasting value.
1.26 g/L is the fasting diabetes threshold.
The tubular reabsorption threshold is about 1.8 g/L.

title: About the posterior pituitary:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: About the posterior pituitary:
body.explanation: Slide: posterior pituitary hormones are vasopressin (AVP) and oxytocin; the posterior lobe is the neurohypophysis.
option_notes: Stated. The slide writes 'desmopressine'; textbooks call desmopressin the synthetic AVP analogue.

title: Signs of dehydration on general examination include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Signs of dehydration on general examination include:
body.explanation: Dehydration: dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor, sunken eyes; also check heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate and temperature.
option_notes: Wrong: not a sign of dehydration.

title: On the TSH/T4 synthesis chart:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the TSH/T4 synthesis chart:
options: High TSH with normal T4 indicates subclinical hypothyroidism
Low TSH with normal T4 indicates subclinical hyperthyroidism
High TSH with normal T4 indicates clinical, full-fledged hyperthyroidism
Subclinical states always have abnormal T4
body.explanation: The chart marks 'High TSH, normal T4' as subclinical hypothyroidism and 'Low TSH, normal T4' as subclinical hyperthyroidism.
option_notes: Wrong: high TSH points to hypothyroidism.
Wrong: in subclinical states T4 is normal.

title: In acromegaly, the slides describe:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In acromegaly, the slides describe:
body.explanation: Acromegaly gives a sonorous deepening voice, macroglossia, large thickened bulky hands and feet, and thick oily sweaty skin.
option_notes: Wrong: skin is thickened, oily and sweaty.
Wrong: hands become large, thickened and bulky.

title: Adrenergic (autonomic) signs of hypoglycaemia include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Adrenergic (autonomic) signs of hypoglycaemia include:
body.explanation: Adrenergic signs: tremor, palpitations, anxiety, sweating, hunger; confusion and convulsions are neuroglycopenic.

title: What share of thyroid lumps are benign?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What share of thyroid lumps are benign?
body.explanation: The majority, 90 to 95 percent, are benign, though work-up is often needed.
option_notes: Far too low: most lumps are benign.
Too low: most lumps are benign.
90 to 95% of thyroid lumps are benign.
Only a small share is malignant, not benign.

title: How long does acute diarrhoea last?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How long does acute diarrhoea last?
body.explanation: Acute under 2 weeks; prolonged 2 to 4 weeks; chronic over 4 weeks.

title: Why can primary hypothyroidism raise prolactin?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why can primary hypothyroidism raise prolactin?
body.explanation: In primary hypothyroidism TRH rises, and TRH stimulates prolactin (the TRH stimulation test is also listed as a cause).
option_notes: TRH rises to push the thyroid and also releases prolactin.
Thyroid hormone is low, not high.
The thyroid does not make prolactin.

title: According to the hyperprolactinaemia mechanism diagram:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the hyperprolactinaemia mechanism diagram:
options: Dopamine inhibition of prolactin is increased
body.explanation: The diagram shows prolactin rising with dopamine falling, GnRH falling, FSH/LH falling and anovulation, plus milk secretion.
option_notes: Shown as FSH and LH down.
Wrong: dopamine is shown as decreased.

title: An abdominal CT scan is indicated in vomiting when you suspect:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An abdominal CT scan is indicated in vomiting when you suspect:
body.explanation: CT (if indicated): obstruction, pancreatitis or other intra-abdominal pathology.

title: A 68-year-old has had constipation for 2 months with weight loss, anaemia and blood in the stool. What is the next step?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 68-year-old has had constipation for 2 months with weight loss, anaemia and blood in the stool. What is the next step?
body.explanation: Rectal bleeding, weight loss and anaemia are red flags: an organic cause such as colorectal cancer must be ruled out by colonoscopy.
option_notes: Red flags call for colonoscopy to rule out cancer.
Red flags must not be treated symptomatically.
Functional tests come after organic causes are ruled out.
A stool chart does not rule out cancer.

title: Thyroid scintigraphy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Thyroid scintigraphy:
options: Classifies nodules as hot or cold
Is described as the optimal, first-line means of evaluating the whole thyroid gland
body.explanation: Scintigraphy uses I123 or Tc99m, shows size, shape, position/ectopic thyroid, and hot or cold nodules. Ultrasound is called the optimal means of evaluating the gland.
option_notes: Wrong: ultrasound is the optimal means of evaluation.

title: Sudden dysphagia most suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Sudden dysphagia most suggests:
body.explanation: Progressive onset suggests cancer or stricture.
option_notes: Sudden onset suggests an impacted bolus or spasm.

title: Which endoscopic treatment is used for varices?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which endoscopic treatment is used for varices?
body.explanation: Variceal band ligation; injection, thermal coagulation and clips for other lesions.
option_notes: Thermal coagulation is used for other lesions.
Clips are used for ulcers and other lesions.
Adrenaline injection alone is not the variceal treatment.

title: Symptoms of diabetes on the Cleveland Clinic panel include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms of diabetes on the Cleveland Clinic panel include:
body.explanation: Panel: increased thirst, slow-healing cuts and sores, fatigue, blurred vision, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss.
option_notes: Wrong: unexplained weight loss is listed.

title: What confirms hepatomegaly first-line?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What confirms hepatomegaly first-line?
body.explanation: Abdominal ultrasound is first-line, then CT if needed.
option_notes: Biopsy is invasive and not used to confirm the size.
ERCP studies the bile ducts and is invasive.
Ultrasound is simple, safe and first-line to confirm the liver size.
A chest X-ray does not assess the liver.

title: Which diarrhoea stops with fasting?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which diarrhoea stops with fasting?
body.explanation: Motor diarrhoea also improves with fasting.
option_notes: A VIPoma is secretory and persists.
No osmotic load when fasting, so it stops.

title: What pH-metry result confirms GERD?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What pH-metry result confirms GERD?
body.explanation: 24-hour pH-metry is the reference test.
option_notes: pH below 4 for more than 5% of the time confirms acid reflux.
A single drop is not enough.
pH over 7 is not acid reflux.

title: A patient arrives in shock with no visible bleeding. How can massive non-externalised GI bleeding be shown?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient arrives in shock with no visible bleeding. How can massive non-externalised GI bleeding be shown?
body.explanation: Massive non-externalised bleeding can present as shock without visible blood; diagnosis is made by gastric aspiration or rectal exam.
option_notes: These reveal blood not yet passed.
Occult blood tests are for chronic minimal loss.
A chest X-ray does not show GI bleeding.

title: Similar symptoms in family members or close contacts of a vomiting patient mainly suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Similar symptoms in family members or close contacts of a vomiting patient mainly suggest:
options: A shared infectious or toxic cause
body.explanation: The history asks about similar cases in close contacts, together with toxic exposure and travel: clusters point to a common source such as gastroenteritis or food poisoning.
option_notes: Correct: a common infectious or toxic source.

title: What is an air bronchogram?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is an air bronchogram?
body.explanation: Translucent bronchi visible inside an alveolar opacity, typical of consolidation.
option_notes: Air in the pleura is pneumothorax.
A cavity is a lucent zone.
Air-filled bronchi seen through filled alveoli.
A blunted angle is an effusion.

title: Sources of ectopic ACTH shown on the causes chart:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Sources of ectopic ACTH shown on the causes chart:
body.explanation: Ectopic hormone sources: small cell lung cancer, carcinoid, medullary thyroid carcinoma and pancreatic islet cell tumour. Adrenal carcinoma is ACTH-independent.
option_notes: Wrong: it is an ACTH-independent adrenal cause.

title: How may angina present in elderly patients?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How may angina present in elderly patients?
body.explanation: Classically squeezing chest pain radiating to neck, jaw, arms, shoulders, back; in the elderly, stomach-area pain after meals; in women, burning or tenderness.
option_notes: Leg pain on walking is claudication.
In the elderly, angina can present as atypical epigastric pain.
Headache is not an angina equivalent.
Visual loss is not an angina equivalent.

title: The chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) triggers vomiting when stimulated by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) triggers vomiting when stimulated by:
body.explanation: The CTZ is stimulated by drugs or toxins; head movements act through the vestibular system, emotions through higher cortical centres.
option_notes: Correct: CTZ stimulation by drugs or toxins.
Wrong: that is the vestibular route.
Wrong: that is the higher cortical route.

title: Which single result is enough to diagnose diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which single result is enough to diagnose diabetes?
options: Random plasma glucose of 2.3 g/L in a patient with polyuria and polydipsia
body.explanation: A random glucose ≥ 2 g/L with classic symptoms is diagnostic. Fasting glucose ≥ 1.26 g/L must be confirmed on 2 samples; HbA1c 6.2% and a 2-hour value of 1.7 g/L are below the thresholds.
option_notes: Random ≥ 2 g/L with symptoms is enough.
A single fasting value needs confirmation.
1.7 g/L is below the 2-hour threshold of 2 g/L.

title: According to the hypopituitarism cartoon:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the hypopituitarism cartoon:
options: It may end in sudden death
Personality changes, weakness and weight loss may occur
It is hard to treat even once suspected
body.explanation: The cartoon shows personality changes, weakness, weight loss, muscle wasting, lost libido/amenorrhoea and sudden death; 'easy to diagnose and treat if you think of it'; DI may be present.
option_notes: Slide says easy to diagnose and treat if you think of it.
DI is listed as 'may also be present'.

title: A 55-year-old has a hard thyroid nodule, a voice change for 2 months and a harsh, high-pitched noise on breathing in. Which statement is correct?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 55-year-old has a hard thyroid nodule, a voice change for 2 months and a harsh, high-pitched noise on breathing in. Which statement is correct?
options: The noise is stridor, a sign of upper airway obstruction, and with the hoarseness it is a warning sign
Hoarseness is expected with any benign goitre and needs no work-up
Most thyroid lumps are malignant, so surgery comes first
The noise is a thyroid bruit from high blood flow
body.explanation: Hoarseness, cervical lymph nodes and stridor (a harsh inspiratory sound from upper airway obstruction) are features that may be seen in thyroid cancer. Still, 90-95% of thyroid lumps are benign, so the work-up comes before surgery.
option_notes: Stridor and hoarseness are warning signs that may be seen in thyroid cancer.
New hoarseness with a hard nodule needs a work-up.
90 to 95% of thyroid lumps are benign; work-up comes first.
A bruit is heard over the gland in hyperthyroidism; this inspiratory noise is stridor.

title: In a man with hyperprolactinaemia, what is usually the first symptom?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a man with hyperprolactinaemia, what is usually the first symptom?
body.explanation: In men the signs are those of hypogonadism, and low libido comes first; then erectile dysfunction, gynaecomastia and infertility.
option_notes: Field loss needs a large tumour and is not the first sign.
Polyuria is not a sign of high prolactin.

title: An asymptomatic person has a random plasma glucose of 2.1 g/L. Is diabetes diagnosed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: An asymptomatic person has a random plasma glucose of 2.1 g/L. Is diabetes diagnosed?
options: Not on this alone: a random value counts with classic symptoms or a hyperglycaemic crisis
Yes, any value above 2 g/L is enough
No, random glucose is never used
body.explanation: The random-glucose criterion (≥ 2 g/L, 200 mg/dL) applies in a patient with classic symptoms or a hyperglycaemic crisis; otherwise confirm with another criterion.
option_notes: Without symptoms, confirm with another criterion.
The criterion needs classic symptoms or a crisis.
Random glucose is a criterion with symptoms.
A normal HbA1c would argue against diabetes.

title: Hypopituitarism is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hypopituitarism is:
options: Diminished or absent secretion of one or more pituitary hormones
A deficiency that can be partial or complete
Always the loss of all anterior pituitary hormones together
Excess secretion of a single trophic hormone
body.explanation: Slide: hypopituitarism is diminished or absent secretion of one or more pituitary hormones (partial or complete deficiency).
option_notes: One or more hormones, not necessarily all.

title: Cushing disease versus Cushing syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cushing disease versus Cushing syndrome:
options: Long-term glucocorticoid medication causes Cushing syndrome
Cushing disease has a fundamentally different clinical picture
Cushing disease is caused by an adrenal adenoma
body.explanation: The comparison chart says symptoms are the same for both; causes of Cushing syndrome include long-term glucocorticoid use, while Cushing disease is the pituitary ACTH source.
option_notes: Chart: same for syndrome and disease.
Wrong: Cushing disease is pituitary ACTH excess.

title: A patient with Addison's disease stopped his treatment, and now has collapse with a thready pulse, abdominal and lumbar pain, vomiting and confusion. Which sta…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with Addison's disease stopped his treatment, and now has collapse with a thready pulse, abdominal and lumbar pain, vomiting and confusion. Which statement is correct?
options: Give high-dose hydrocortisone at once and take hormone samples without delaying treatment
Wait for the cortisol result before treating
Do a synacthen test before any treatment
body.explanation: This is acute adrenal insufficiency, triggered by stopping treatment. Hormone assays are taken without delaying treatment, and the diagnosis is confirmed by the response to high-dose hydrocortisone.
option_notes: Acute AI is an emergency: treat at once.
Waiting for results delays life-saving treatment.
Dynamic tests come later, not in the emergency.
Salt loss worsens the crisis; a salt-free diet is a trigger.

title: Respiratory manifestations of GERD include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Respiratory manifestations of GERD include:
body.explanation: Respiratory symptoms: chronic (especially nocturnal) cough, asthma-like symptoms due to micro-aspirations, recurrent bronchitis or laryngospasm.
option_notes: Wrong: not a GERD manifestation on the slides.

title: Which psychiatric risk is stressed in hypercortisolism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which psychiatric risk is stressed in hypercortisolism?
body.explanation: Depression with suicide risk, or euphoria and delirium.
option_notes: Psychosis can occur, but schizophrenia is not the stressed risk.
Depression with suicide risk is stressed.

title: A newly diabetic patient has fruity breath, nausea and ketones in the urine, but is fully alert and breathing normally. What does this picture show?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A newly diabetic patient has fruity breath, nausea and ketones in the urine, but is fully alert and breathing normally. What does this picture show?
options: Signs of ketosis without signs of acidosis
body.explanation: In mild ketoacidosis there are signs of ketosis (fruity breath, anorexia, nausea, vomiting); Kussmaul breathing and altered consciousness mark acidosis in moderate to severe forms.
option_notes: Ketosis signs without Kussmaul breathing or drowsiness.
Severe forms bring Kussmaul breathing and drowsiness.
Hypoglycaemia does not give ketonuria and fruity breath.
The hyperosmolar state has no marked ketosis.

title: Which bilirubin rises in haemolysis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which bilirubin rises in haemolysis?
body.explanation: Non-cholestatic jaundice is unconjugated, as in haemolysis.
option_notes: Unconjugated bilirubin does not pass into urine.

title: Which nerve involvement signs occur in mediastinal syndromes? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which nerve involvement signs occur in mediastinal syndromes? (choose all)
body.explanation: Horner (sympathetic), hiccups and girdle pain (phrenic), dysphonia (recurrent), bradycardia and sialorrhoea (vagus).
option_notes: Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy gives dysphonia.
Diplopia is not a mediastinal sign.
Hearing loss is not a mediastinal sign.

title: Hardening of stools in constipation is explained by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hardening of stools in constipation is explained by:
options: Excess water absorption during slow transit
Increased water secretion into the colonic lumen
Accelerated colonic transit through the colon
Reduced water absorption by the colonic mucosa
body.explanation: Slow transit can result in excess water absorption, leading to hard stools.
option_notes: Correct: slow transit allows excess water absorption.
Wrong: transit is slowed, not accelerated.

title: The skin and face in hypopituitarism show:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The skin and face in hypopituitarism show:
options: Constant depigmentation of the areolas and external genitalia
body.explanation: Slide: pale facies, a bit 'old'; depigmentation of areolas and genitalia is constant; thin, cold, dry skin with fine wrinkles.
option_notes: Skin is thin, cold and dry; oily skin is acromegaly.
Purple striae are a Cushing sign.

title: Which test confirms achalasia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which test confirms achalasia?
body.explanation: Absent peristalsis and a non-relaxing LES.
option_notes: Manometry shows absent peristalsis and a non-relaxing sphincter.
Endoscopy can be nearly normal in achalasia.

title: What does percussion find in pneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does percussion find in pneumothorax?
body.explanation: Distended painful hemithorax, reduced expansion, decreased fremitus, hyperresonance, reduced or absent breath sounds.
option_notes: Air in the pleura changes the sound.

title: At the start and end of the rectal examination:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: At the start and end of the rectal examination:
options: The exam ends with percussion of the abdomen
The exam ends by cleaning off lubricant
The exam starts with a deep rectal sweep
body.explanation: Step 1 is examining the skin; step 7 is end-of-examination care: clean off any lubricant.
option_notes: Sweeps come after advancing the finger.

title: Which fluid collection fills the peritoneum in RHF?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which fluid collection fills the peritoneum in RHF?
body.explanation: The peritoneal space takes up a lot of fluid: ascites.
option_notes: Pleural effusion is in the chest.
Ascites is fluid in the peritoneum.
Haemarthrosis is blood in a joint.

title: A 62-year-old has recurrent urinary infections and a foot sore that will not heal. What should be checked first?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 62-year-old has recurrent urinary infections and a foot sore that will not heal. What should be checked first?
body.explanation: Slow-healing cuts and sores and infections are among the symptoms that can reveal diabetes.
option_notes: Hyperglycaemia slows healing and favours infections.
Thyroid tests are not first here.

title: Which tremor is typical of hyperthyroidism?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which tremor is typical of hyperthyroidism?
body.explanation: A fine rhythmic tremor of the hands, tongue or lightly closed eyelids.
option_notes: A coarse resting tremor suggests Parkinson's disease.
Fine, rapid tremor of the outstretched hands, tongue or closed eyelids.
Intention tremor points to a cerebellar problem.
Flapping tremor (asterixis) suggests liver or kidney failure.

title: Altered mental status, dizziness or nystagmus in a vomiting patient point to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Altered mental status, dizziness or nystagmus in a vomiting patient point to:
body.explanation: Altered mental status, dizziness or nystagmus: central nervous system causes of vomiting.
option_notes: Correct: central nervous system causes of vomiting.
Wrong: abdominal causes give abdominal signs.
Wrong: the cardiovascular exam looks for heart failure.
Wrong: no neurological signs in psychogenic vomiting.

title: During a 75 g OGTT, the 2-hour glucose is 11.5 mmol/L. What does it mean?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: During a 75 g OGTT, the 2-hour glucose is 11.5 mmol/L. What does it mean?
options: OGTT cannot be used to diagnose diabetes
body.explanation: A 2-hour plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) during an OGTT is a diagnostic criterion.
option_notes: 2-hour value ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (2 g/L) meets the criterion.
It is above the prediabetes range.
The OGTT is one of the diagnostic criteria.

title: Symptoms of Cushing's syndrome listed on the Lancet case slide include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Symptoms of Cushing's syndrome listed on the Lancet case slide include:
body.explanation: Symptoms: decreased libido, psychiatric disorders, proximal muscle weakness, hair loss, menstrual irregularities.
option_notes: Not listed; points to vasopressin disorders.

title: According to the key messages and conclusion of the GERD lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the key messages and conclusion of the GERD lecture:
options: Endoscopy is required in every patient with heartburn
GERD is a purely digestive disease
Chronic cough or dysphonia should make you consider extra-digestive GERD
body.explanation: Key messages: GERD is frequent and often benign, diagnosis is clinical in typical cases, endoscopy if red flags, and always consider extra-digestive forms in chronic cough or dysphonia; it is at the crossroads of digestive, ENT and respiratory pathology.
option_notes: Wrong: endoscopy is indicated if red flags are present.
Wrong: it is at the crossroads of digestive, ENT and respiratory pathology.

title: Where does normal depolarisation start?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where does normal depolarisation start?
body.explanation: SA node, atria, AV node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres, ventricles.
option_notes: The AV node relays the signal.
The bundle of His conducts it.
The SA node is the natural pacemaker.
Purkinje fibres are the last step.

title: Which treat angina? (choose all)
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which treat angina? (choose all)
body.explanation: Nitrates, aspirin, beta blockers and calcium channel blockers.

title: A patient with suspected adrenal insufficiency has an 8 a.m. cortisol of 12 µg/dL. What does this mean?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient with suspected adrenal insufficiency has an 8 a.m. cortisol of 12 µg/dL. What does this mean?
options: It is intermediate, so a synacthen test is needed
body.explanation: 8 a.m. cortisol below 5 µg/dL confirms AI; above 18 µg/dL excludes it. Values in between may be normal or latent insufficiency, so dynamic tests are needed.
option_notes: Between 5 and 18 µg/dL: a dynamic test is needed.
Confirmation needs a value below 5 µg/dL.
Exclusion needs a value above 18 µg/dL.
A morning cortisol is not used to detect Cushing's.

title: In high-income countries, which kills more?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In high-income countries, which kills more?
body.explanation: In high-income countries cancer causes twice as many deaths as cardiovascular disease.
option_notes: Cancer kills about twice as many in rich countries.

title: On the 'Type 2 diabetes and PAD' poster, warning signs include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the 'Type 2 diabetes and PAD' poster, warning signs include:
options: Leg pain that does not go away after exercising
Foot or toe wounds that heal slowly or not at all
Poor toenail growth or hair loss on the legs
Lower temperature in the lower leg or foot than the rest of the body
body.explanation: The poster lists all four as reasons to see a doctor; PAD is a narrowing of arteries, usually of the legs.

title: A patient's chronic dry cough at night and hoarseness have not improved with ENT treatment. Which diagnosis must be considered?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient's chronic dry cough at night and hoarseness have not improved with ENT treatment. Which diagnosis must be considered?
body.explanation: Always consider extra-digestive forms of GERD when facing chronic cough or dysphonia.
option_notes: Reflux causes chronic cough and dysphonia.

title: Which drug class causes a chronic dry cough?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drug class causes a chronic dry cough?
body.explanation: ACE inhibitors are a classic cause of chronic dry cough.
option_notes: ACE inhibitors raise bradykinin, causing a dry cough.
Beta blockers can cause bronchospasm, not this cough.

title: On the chart, the first test after finding raised unconjugated bilirubin is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the chart, the first test after finding raised unconjugated bilirubin is:
body.explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin -> CBC (reticulocytes); conjugated bilirubin -> LFT.

title: In a man, what can the digital rectal examination also assess?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a man, what can the digital rectal examination also assess?
body.explanation: The digital examination explores the anal canal, the distal rectum and, in men, the prostate.
option_notes: The prostate can be felt through the anterior rectal wall.
The bladder lining is not felt on rectal exam.
The appendix is far out of reach.
The finger only reaches the distal rectum.

title: In the post-traumatic hypopituitarism case, the clinical signs described include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the post-traumatic hypopituitarism case, the clinical signs described include:
body.explanation: Caption: lack of facial hair, dehydration, Queen Anne's sign, pale skin, muscular atrophy, loss of body hair and anorexia.
option_notes: Pallor, not dark skin, as ACTH is lacking.

title: What volume defines high-abundance hemoptysis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What volume defines high-abundance hemoptysis?
body.explanation: Low: under 50 mL. Medium: 300 to 500 mL. High: over 500 mL at once or in 24 hours. Every hemoptysis is an emergency.

title: Ophthalmological signs described as RARE in pituitary mass effect:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Ophthalmological signs described as RARE in pituitary mass effect:
body.explanation: Rarely, decreased visual acuity, pupillary abnormalities, optic atrophy, papilloedema, cranial nerve palsies and nystagmus may be seen; bitemporal superior loss is the typical sign.
option_notes: Wrong: this is the typical chiasmal sign, not a rare one.

title: Which complication carries a cancer risk?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which complication carries a cancer risk?
body.explanation: Barrett's oesophagus is mucosal metaplasia with cancer risk.
option_notes: A stricture causes dysphagia but is not pre-cancerous.
Barrett's metaplasia carries a cancer risk.

title: On average, how long after it starts is diabetes diagnosed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On average, how long after it starts is diabetes diagnosed?
body.explanation: Median clinical diagnosis delay of 2.2 to 2.4 years after the physiological onset.
option_notes: The median delay is about 2.2 to 2.4 years.
Too long for the average delay.
Diabetes is usually found late, not at onset.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Endoscopy. Upper endoscopy finds the source in over 90%; colonoscopy for lower bleeding; treats by injection, coagulation, clips, banding.
option_notes: Finds the source and can treat it.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Severe hypoglycaemia (level 3) is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Severe hypoglycaemia (level 3) is characterised by:
options: Severe cognitive impairment, seizures or coma
Need for external assistance and injectable treatment
body.explanation: Level 3: no specific glucose threshold; severe cognitive impairment, seizures, coma requiring external assistance and injectable glucose or glucagon.

title: On adrenal CT/MRI, adrenal hyperplasia appears as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On adrenal CT/MRI, adrenal hyperplasia appears as:
options: A homogeneous increase in volume with preserved morphology
A unilateral heterogeneous mass with loss of shape
body.explanation: CT/MRI: hyperplasia = homogeneous increase in volume with preserved morphology.
option_notes: Wrong: that is atrophy (e.g. autoimmune AI).
Wrong: morphology is preserved in hyperplasia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Oesophageal phase. Involuntary peristalsis toward the stomach.
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Oesophageal phase: involuntary peristalsis.
Another box. Oesophageal: food sticks behind the sternum.
Another box. Motor: liquids as much as solids (paradoxical).

title: Abdominal percussion in a vomiting patient looks for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal percussion in a vomiting patient looks for:
body.explanation: Percussion: fluid (ascites) or dullness suggesting a mass. Scars are seen on inspection; tenderness is found on palpation.

title: The Whipple triad comprises:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The Whipple triad comprises:
options: Resolution of symptoms after glucose intake
Ketonuria on a urine test strip
body.explanation: Whipple triad: symptoms of hypoglycaemia, low blood glucose (< 70 mg/dL) and resolution of symptoms after glucose intake.
option_notes: Second element; threshold as given on the slide.
Ketonuria relates to ketosis/DKA, not to the triad.

title: Hyperemesis gravidarum is:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Hyperemesis gravidarum is:
options: Severe and persistent vomiting during pregnancy
A chronic gastrointestinal cause of vomiting
body.explanation: Hyperemesis gravidarum: severe and persistent vomiting during pregnancy.
option_notes: Wrong: listed under pregnancy, acute non-GI causes.

title: A 58-year-old with years of reflux now has trouble swallowing solids and has lost 5 kg. What is needed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 58-year-old with years of reflux now has trouble swallowing solids and has lost 5 kg. What is needed?
body.explanation: Dysphagia and weight loss are alarm signs: any alarm sign requires endoscopy (stricture, cancer).
option_notes: pH-metry does not show strictures or tumours.
Manometry is not first with alarm signs.

title: Which chest pain is sudden and stabbing?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which chest pain is sudden and stabbing?
body.explanation: A sudden stabbing pain suggests pneumothorax; progressive pain suggests bronchial cancer.
option_notes: Air suddenly entering the pleura gives sudden stabbing pain.

title: Which jugular vein is always observed?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which jugular vein is always observed?
body.explanation: Always observe the right internal jugular vein; distension reflects raised central venous pressure.
option_notes: The left side is less direct.
The right internal jugular is in direct line with the right atrium.

title: Put the hyperglycaemia symptoms in their causal order:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Put the hyperglycaemia symptoms in their causal order:
options: Glycosuria, then osmotic diuresis with polyuria, then polydipsia
body.explanation: Hyperglycaemia causes glycosuria; glycosuria causes an osmotic diuresis (polyuria); polyuria causes polydipsia. In primary polydipsia the order is reversed: drinking comes first.
option_notes: Glycosuria, then osmotic diuresis, then thirst.

title: Regarding drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia:
options: It is usually mild, about 25 to 100 ng/mL
Risperidone can push levels above 200 ng/mL
Opioids typically push levels above 200 ng/mL
Verapamil typically gives levels above 200 ng/mL
body.explanation: Table footnote: drug-induced hyperprolactinaemia is usually mild (25-100 ng/mL) except for the highlighted agents (phenothiazines, risperidone, metoclopramide), which can exceed 200 ng/mL.
option_notes: Wrong: opioids are not among the highlighted agents.
Wrong: verapamil is not a highlighted agent.

title: Characterising the jaundice itself involves:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Characterising the jaundice itself involves:
options: Which side of the body is more yellow
body.explanation: Jaundice: acute or chronic onset, duration, aggravating or intermittent.

title: Which lymph node signals digestive cancer metastasis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which lymph node signals digestive cancer metastasis?
body.explanation: The left supraclavicular node is the key site of digestive cancer metastasis.
option_notes: The axillary node drains the arm and breast.
Inguinal nodes drain the leg and perineum.
The left supraclavicular node signals digestive cancer metastasis.

title: On CT, an aldosterone-producing adenoma:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On CT, an aldosterone-producing adenoma:
options: Usually exceeds 5 cm and is easily seen on ultrasound
Is seen far better on MRI than on CT
body.explanation: CT scan: hypodense mass of 1 to 3 cm; MRI is roughly equivalent to CT.
option_notes: Wrong: it is small; ultrasound detects only tumours >5 cm.
Wrong: MRI is about equal to CT.

title: What daily stool weight suggests constipation?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What daily stool weight suggests constipation?
body.explanation: A reduced amount under 100 g of faeces per day.
option_notes: Under 100 g of faeces per day.

title: Causes of outlet dysfunction include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of outlet dysfunction include:
