body.explanation: Causes of outlet dysfunction: anismus, megarectum, rectocele, internal rectal prolapse; colonic inertia and spastic colon cause slow transit.
option_notes: Wrong: cause of slow transit constipation.
Wrong: cause of slow transit constipation.

title: Macrovascular complications of diabetes correspond to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Macrovascular complications of diabetes correspond to:
options: Thickening of the capillary basement membrane
body.explanation: Macrovascular complications are an accelerated atherosclerosis: chronic heart disease (more MI), stroke, PAD (peripheral gangrene). Gangrene is pictured on p75.

title: What is the function of cough?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the function of cough?
body.explanation: Cough maintains airway permeability by eliminating secretions and foreign particles. It is non-specific.
option_notes: Cough clears secretions and particles to keep the airways open.
Cough does not regulate blood pressure.

title: Diabetic mononeuropathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Diabetic mononeuropathy:
options: Includes loss of sensation, pain and motor weakness
Is a bilateral symmetric sensory disorder
Mainly affects pelvic girdle muscles with wasting
body.explanation: Mononeuropathy: involvement of a mixed nerve trunk with loss of sensation, pain and motor weakness.

title: Why are plasma catecholamines hard to interpret in suspected phaeochromocytoma?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why are plasma catecholamines hard to interpret in suspected phaeochromocytoma?
options: They are stress hormones with a short half-life
They are not secreted by the tumour
They are only found in urine
They rise only after MIBG injection
body.explanation: Plasma catecholamines are stress hormones with a short half-life, so their level is difficult to interpret. Plasma metanephrines are more useful.
option_notes: Stress raises them and they clear fast, so levels are unreliable.
MIBG is an imaging tracer and does not raise them.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Chronic diarrhoea. Over 4 weeks; identify the mechanism.
option_notes: Another box. Osmotic: stops with fasting (lactase deficiency, laxatives).
This is the box at the arrow. Chronic: over 4 weeks.
Another box. Malabsorptive: greasy, pale, foul stools.

title: What does Kussmaul breathing in ketoacidosis correspond to?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does Kussmaul breathing in ketoacidosis correspond to?
options: A sign of acidosis: fast, deep breathing
body.explanation: Kussmaul respiration (tachypnoea with deep inspirations) is listed among the signs of acidosis in moderate to severe ketoacidosis.
option_notes: Fast, deep breathing compensates for acidosis.
Kussmaul breathing is fast and deep.

title: The 'other paraclinical tests' listed for vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The 'other paraclinical tests' listed for vomiting include:
options: Endocrine or toxicological tests if indicated
body.explanation: Other tests: ECG, cerebral CT, endocrine or toxicological tests if indicated.

title: Cushing's syndrome is confirmed and ACTH is high or 'inappropriately normal'. Which test comes next per the slides?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cushing's syndrome is confirmed and ACTH is high or 'inappropriately normal'. Which test comes next per the slides?
body.explanation: A normal or high ACTH means an ACTH-secreting neoplasm (Cushing's disease or ectopic ACTH). The next step is the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test.
option_notes: The next step for ACTH-dependent Cushing's.
Adrenal CT is for a low ACTH.
Synacthen tests adrenal reserve, not cortisol excess.
The aldosterone/renin ratio is for hyperaldosteronism.

title: Carbohydrate and lipid effects of glucocorticoid excess (diabetogenic effect) include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Carbohydrate and lipid effects of glucocorticoid excess (diabetogenic effect) include:
body.explanation: The diagram lists increased hepatic glycogen deposition, peripheral insulin resistance, gluconeogenesis and free fatty acid production, giving a diabetogenic effect.

title: Which is a cause of outlet dysfunction?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which is a cause of outlet dysfunction?
body.explanation: Outlet causes: anismus, megarectum, rectocele, internal rectal prolapse. Slow transit: colonic inertia, spastic colon.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Severity. Pallor, cold extremities, tachycardia; then hypotension, oliguria, confusion, mottling.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Pallor, tachycardia, then hypotension, oliguria, confusion.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Bilirubin is combined with glucuronic acid (conjugated) in the:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Bilirubin is combined with glucuronic acid (conjugated) in the:
body.explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin reaches the liver where it is combined with glucuronic acid to form conjugated bilirubin.

title: A woman with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term prednisolone develops a moon face and purple striae. What is her own ACTH expected to be?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A woman with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term prednisolone develops a moon face and purple striae. What is her own ACTH expected to be?
options: Low, because the steroid feeds back on the hypothalamus and pituitary
body.explanation: Exogenous glucocorticoids cause Cushing's syndrome. Like cortisol, they exert negative feedback on CRH and ACTH, so ACTH is low.
option_notes: The steroid suppresses CRH and ACTH by negative feedback.
Cushing's disease has high ACTH from a pituitary tumour.
Ectopic ACTH comes from a tumour, not from prednisolone.

title: Why is the digital rectal exam key?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Why is the digital rectal exam key?
body.explanation: DRE assesses impaction, anal tone, masses and pelvic floor dysfunction.
option_notes: The DRE only reaches the rectum.
It finds impaction, anal tone, masses and pelvic floor problems.
Thyroid function is a blood test.

title: Which hormone deficiency slows motility?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which hormone deficiency slows motility?
body.explanation: Hypothyroidism is an endocrine cause of constipation (slide 26).
option_notes: Prolactin deficiency is not a cause of constipation.

title: In mild ketoacidosis, signs of ketosis (as opposed to signs of hyperglycaemia) include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In mild ketoacidosis, signs of ketosis (as opposed to signs of hyperglycaemia) include:
body.explanation: Ketosis: abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, ketonic breath. Hyperglycaemia: polyuria, polydipsia, thirst, blurry vision, nocturia, weight loss.
option_notes: Wrong: nocturia is a hyperglycaemia sign.

title: How long should a patient rest before vital signs?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: How long should a patient rest before vital signs?
body.explanation: Resting comfortably, supine or sitting, for 3 to 5 minutes, with no blood draw just before.
option_notes: 3 to 5 minutes of rest gives stable baseline readings.

title: Which drug can cause secretory diarrhoea?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which drug can cause secretory diarrhoea?
body.explanation: Drugs causing secretory diarrhoea: colchicine and digitalis (slide 19).
option_notes: Insulin does not cause secretory diarrhoea.
Loperamide slows transit and treats diarrhoea.

title: Expiratory dyspnoea suggests what?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Expiratory dyspnoea suggests what?
body.explanation: Inspiratory dyspnoea: high (laryngotracheal) obstruction. Expiratory: low obstruction, as in asthma.
option_notes: Narrow small airways trap air on expiration.
Effusion is not linked to a phase.
Pneumothorax is not linked to a phase.

title: Which disorder causes paradoxical dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which disorder causes paradoxical dysphagia?
body.explanation: Achalasia: solids and liquids from onset, intermittent, worse with hot or cold, general state preserved.
option_notes: A foreign body causes sudden blockage.
A motor disorder affects liquids as much as solids.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Malabsorptive diarrhoea. Abundant, greasy, pale, foul stools with deficiencies (coeliac, pancreatic insufficiency).
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Malabsorptive: greasy, pale, foul stools.
Another box. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.

title: Medications causing constipation, according to the lecture, include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Medications causing constipation, according to the lecture, include:
body.explanation: Medications: opioids, antidepressants (tricyclics, SSRIs), antihistamines, iron; the diagram adds calcium channel blockers and antipsychotics.
option_notes: Wrong: prokinetics stimulate motility and are not listed as causes.

title: In the phaeochromocytoma section, adrenal computed tomography:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the phaeochromocytoma section, adrenal computed tomography:
options: Assesses the size and the lipid structure of the adrenal mass
Is the test that proves catecholamine excess
body.explanation: The slide lists what adrenal CT assesses: adenoma size, structure (lipid) and tumour extension; its example is a left phaeochromocytoma. Secretion is shown by biology, not by imaging.
option_notes: Correct: size and structure (lipid) are listed.
Wrong: catecholamine excess is proven biologically; CT localises the tumour.

title: Etiological antibody tests for hypothyroidism per the slides are:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Etiological antibody tests for hypothyroidism per the slides are:
body.explanation: Etiological investigations: autoantibody assays anti-TPO and anti-Tg, plus CBC, guided by history and clinical picture.
option_notes: Wrong: calcitonin is a thyroid cancer marker.
Wrong: stimulating TRAb point to Graves'.

title: What does manometry show in achalasia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does manometry show in achalasia?
body.explanation: Absent peristalsis and a lower oesophageal sphincter that does not relax.
option_notes: Absent peristalsis and a sphincter that does not relax.
Manometry measures pressures; it does not see masses.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Motor diarrhoea. Accelerated transit; post-prandial, urgent, improves with fasting (hyperthyroidism, IBS).
option_notes: This is the box at the arrow. Motor: fast transit, post-prandial and urgent.
Another box. Osmotic: stops with fasting (lactase deficiency, laxatives).
Another box. Secretory: persists during fasting.

title: Exploration of lower GI and small-bowel bleeding:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Exploration of lower GI and small-bowel bleeding:
options: Anoscopy and rectoscopy explore anal or rectal causes
Colonoscopy is the key exam for lower GI bleeding
Capsule endoscopy or enteroscopy explore the small intestine if no source is found
Capsule endoscopy is first-line for upper GI bleeding
body.explanation: Anoscopy/rectoscopy for anal or rectal causes; colonoscopy is the key exam for lower GI bleeding; enteroscopy or capsule endoscopy explore the small intestine if no source is found.
option_notes: Wrong: EGD is first-line for upper bleeding.

title: Lateral extension of a pituitary tumour causes diplopia by compressing the cranial nerves:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Lateral extension of a pituitary tumour causes diplopia by compressing the cranial nerves:
body.explanation: Slide 22: compression of cranial nerves III, IV and VI gives diplopia and palpebral ptosis.
option_notes: Wrong: not part of the cavernous sinus compression described.

title: Bone catabolism in Cushing syndrome causes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Bone catabolism in Cushing syndrome causes:
body.explanation: Bone catabolism: pain, especially spinal; osteoporosis with vertebral compression; pathologic fractures.

title: Additional tests (beyond clinical diagnosis) in GERD are reserved for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Additional tests (beyond clinical diagnosis) in GERD are reserved for:
options: A young patient with typical heartburn and regurgitation
body.explanation: Typical forms are diagnosed clinically; tests are reserved for atypical/extra-digestive forms, alarm signs, poor response to treatment, age over 50 or long-standing reflux.
option_notes: Wrong: typical forms are diagnosed clinically.

title: Causes of lower GI bleeding include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of lower GI bleeding include:
body.explanation: Lower GI causes: anal lesions; colorectal cancer or polyps, diverticular disease, angiodysplasia, IBD; small-bowel vascular malformations, tumours, Meckel's diverticulum.
option_notes: Wrong: upper GI cause after vomiting.

title: According to the clinical examination slide, the hyperpigmentation of primary adrenal insufficiency:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: According to the clinical examination slide, the hyperpigmentation of primary adrenal insufficiency:
options: Is a fundamental element of the diagnosis
Involves palmar creases, nipples and areolae
Is the key sign of secondary adrenal insufficiency
body.explanation: Hyperpigmentation is a fundamental element of diagnosis, seen in non-naturally pigmented patients, mainly in sun-exposed areas, with palmar creases, nail beds, nipples, areolae and mucosa involved.
option_notes: Wrong: secondary AI has no hyperpigmentation (pale skin).

title: Yellow discolouration of jaundice is looked for on:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Yellow discolouration of jaundice is looked for on:
body.explanation: Jaundice is yellow discolouration of the sclera and/or skin; slides 3 and 13 show scleral icterus.
option_notes: Scleral, not iridal, discolouration is shown (slide 3).

title: A 40-year-old has attacks of pounding headache, profuse sweating, palpitations and pallor, with BP up to 220/120 during attacks. Which first test is most usefu…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 40-year-old has attacks of pounding headache, profuse sweating, palpitations and pallor, with BP up to 220/120 during attacks. Which first test is most useful?
options: MIBG scintigraphy before any lab test
body.explanation: The triad headache + sweating + palpitations with paroxysmal hypertension suggests phaeochromocytoma. Urinary methoxylated derivatives are the key test; plasma catecholamines are hard to interpret and VMA is no longer used.
option_notes: Plasma catecholamines are hard to interpret.

title: In arginine vasopressin resistance:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In arginine vasopressin resistance:
options: AVP acts ineffectively on the kidneys
AVP release is increased in compensation
Excess drinking is the first event
body.explanation: Diagram: (1) ineffective AVP action in the kidneys, (2) polyuria, (3) polydipsia with compensated increased AVP release.

title: The monofilament test in diabetic neuropathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The monofilament test in diabetic neuropathy:
options: Is applied to plantar sites such as the big toe and metatarsal heads
Is applied to the dorsum of the foot
body.explanation: The 10 g monofilament is applied to the sole (hallux, metatarsal heads) and tests superficial sensation.
option_notes: Sites shown on the plantar diagram.

title: A 45-year-old woman has thyrotoxicosis with a single painless nodule and no eye signs. What is scintigraphy most likely to show?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 45-year-old woman has thyrotoxicosis with a single painless nodule and no eye signs. What is scintigraphy most likely to show?
options: Diffuse homogeneous hyperfixation of an enlarged gland
A hot nodule with reduced or absent uptake in the rest of the gland
Multiple functioning nodules with patchy uptake
body.explanation: This is a toxic adenoma: an isolated, painless nodule, thyrotoxicosis and no ocular signs. It shows as a hot (hyperfixing) nodule while the contralateral lobe is reduced or silent. Diffuse uptake fits Graves'; patchy uptake fits toxic multinodular goitre.
option_notes: Toxic adenoma: one hot nodule, the rest of the gland reduced or silent.
Patchy uptake from several nodules is toxic multinodular goitre.
A cold nodule is non-functioning and cannot cause thyrotoxicosis.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Complications. Peptic oesophagitis, bleeding, peptic stricture, Barrett's oesophagus, respiratory complications.
option_notes: Oesophagitis, bleeding, stricture, Barrett's, respiratory complications.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: The pituitary gland measures about:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The pituitary gland measures about:
body.explanation: Slide 4 gives pituitary dimensions of 5x10x15 mm, lying in the sella turcica below the optic chiasm.
option_notes: Wrong: too large; that would be a macroadenoma-sized mass.

title: Lying BP is 110/70 mmHg. After 2 minutes standing it is 86/66 mmHg and the patient feels dizzy. How is this interpreted?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Lying BP is 110/70 mmHg. After 2 minutes standing it is 86/66 mmHg and the patient feels dizzy. How is this interpreted?
options: Negative test, since diastolic fell less than 10 mmHg
The test is only valid after 10 minutes
body.explanation: Schellong test is positive with a fall in systolic BP of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic of at least 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing. Here systolic fell by 24 mmHg.
option_notes: Systolic fell by 24 mmHg within 3 minutes: positive.
A systolic fall of 20 mmHg or more is enough.
A 24 mmHg fall with dizziness is abnormal.
The test is read within 3 minutes of standing.

title: Where does oedema collect when a patient lies down?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Where does oedema collect when a patient lies down?
body.explanation: Gravity: ankles and legs when standing, the sacrum when lying down.
option_notes: Lying down, fluid moves to the sacrum.
Ankles are where oedema collects when standing.
The face is not the main site.
The hands are not the main site.

title: Bilateral sensory diabetic polyneuropathy features:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Bilateral sensory diabetic polyneuropathy features:
options: Impaired vibration sense and two-point discrimination
Brisk reflexes with an extensor plantar response
body.explanation: Polyneuropathy: paresthesias, impaired pain, temperature, light touch, two-point and vibration sense, decreased ankle and knee reflexes.

title: Which findings suggest pneumothorax?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which findings suggest pneumothorax?
body.explanation: Pneumothorax: hyperresonant, breath sounds abolished, vocal resonance decreased.
option_notes: Air: hyperresonance and no breath sounds.

title: Aetiologies of jaundice include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Aetiologies of jaundice include:
body.explanation: Causes span biliary obstruction, haemolysis, liver disease including viral hepatitis, and haematological or genetic diseases (e.g. Gilbert).
option_notes: Take-home: genetic disease; Gilbert on slide 23.

title: Jaundice with fever and abdominal pain suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Jaundice with fever and abdominal pain suggests:
body.explanation: Acute cholangitis: PAIN, FEVER, JAUNDICE.
option_notes: Non-haemolytic conjugation defect (slide 23); not the pain-fever-jaundice triad.

title: What does hypotension suggest in dysentery?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What does hypotension suggest in dysentery?
body.explanation: Hypotension may occur with severe dehydration or septic shock.
option_notes: Hypotension is a sign of severity.
Severe fluid loss or septic shock lowers blood pressure.

title: Possible paraganglioma locations given in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Possible paraganglioma locations given in the lecture:
body.explanation: The figure shows 1 head and neck paragangliomas, 2 phaeochromocytomas (adrenals), 3 organ of Zuckerkandl, 4 bladder paragangliomas.
option_notes: Wrong: not listed (the figure shows head and neck, adrenals = phaeochromocytoma, organ of Zuckerkandl, bladder).

title: Painful swallowing is called:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Painful swallowing is called:
body.explanation: Often infectious or inflammatory.
option_notes: Aphagia is total inability to swallow.

title: Endocrine and metabolic abnormalities seen in acromegaly include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Endocrine and metabolic abnormalities seen in acromegaly include:
options: Diabetes mellitus or impaired glucose tolerance
body.explanation: Slide 17 lists DM/IGT, type IV hypertriglyceridaemia, hyperlipoproteinaemia, hypercalciuria and diffuse or nodular goitre.

title: Pathological causes of hyperprolactinaemia include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Pathological causes of hyperprolactinaemia include:
options: Acromegaly with GH and prolactin co-secretion
body.explanation: The pathologic column lists pituitary tumours (prolactinoma, acromegaly co-secreting GH and PRL, nonsecretory adenoma), hypothyroidism, CKD, liver failure, stalk lesion, irradiation, spinal cord lesions, hypophysitis and PCOS.
option_notes: Wrong: dopamine inhibits prolactin; less dopamine raises it.

title: The work-up of hyperprolactinaemia on the slides includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The work-up of hyperprolactinaemia on the slides includes:
options: Classifying a prolactinoma as micro or macro/invasive
body.explanation: Investigations: prolactin assay with PEG and pituitary MRI, which classifies prolactinomas as micro or macro/invasive.
option_notes: Wrong: that is a Cushing test.
Wrong: adrenal CT is not part of this work-up.

title: Which result is NOT enough on its own to diagnose diabetes?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which result is NOT enough on its own to diagnose diabetes?
options: Random glucose of 2.5 g/L with polyuria and polydipsia
body.explanation: Fasting glucose must be ≥ 1.26 g/L on 2 samples.
option_notes: A single fasting value must be confirmed on a second sample.
Random ≥ 2 g/L with symptoms is enough.

title: Neonatal hypothyroidism can result from:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Neonatal hypothyroidism can result from:
options: Placental transmission of TSH-receptor blocking antibodies
Maternal TSH crossing the placenta and suppressing the fetal thyroid
body.explanation: The aetiology slide lists neonatal hypothyroidism due to placental transmission of TSH-R blocking antibodies.
option_notes: Correct: TSH-R blocking antibodies cross the placenta.

title: A constipated patient also has tiredness, weight gain and cold intolerance. Which test should be done?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A constipated patient also has tiredness, weight gain and cold intolerance. Which test should be done?
body.explanation: Thyroid function tests look for hypothyroidism, an endocrine cause of secondary constipation.
option_notes: Celiac tests are done if indicated by other clues.
Defecography looks for structural pelvic defects.

title: A 30-year-old woman has amenorrhoea, hirsutism and acne, as well as wide purple striae and proximal weakness. What should be ruled out?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 30-year-old woman has amenorrhoea, hirsutism and acne, as well as wide purple striae and proximal weakness. What should be ruled out?
body.explanation: Reproductive dysfunction (hirsutism, acne, menstrual disorders) is part of Cushing's; with purple striae and proximal weakness, cortisol excess must be tested.
option_notes: Purple striae and proximal weakness point to Cushing's.
PCOS does not cause purple striae or proximal myopathy.
Hypothyroidism does not cause hirsutism and striae.
Addison's causes weight loss and pigmentation.

title: Which laboratory pattern fits jaundice from haemolysis?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which laboratory pattern fits jaundice from haemolysis?
options: Raised unconjugated bilirubin, high LDH and low haptoglobin
Raised conjugated bilirubin with high GGT and ALP
Raised conjugated bilirubin with dilated bile ducts
body.explanation: Haemolysis gives non-cholestatic jaundice with unconjugated bilirubin; LDH and haptoglobin are among the haemolysis tests.
option_notes: Red cell breakdown raises unconjugated bilirubin and LDH and uses up haptoglobin.
No raised bilirubin means no jaundice.

title: Parts of the digestive system accessible to physical examination include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Parts of the digestive system accessible to physical examination include:
options: The anal region and lower rectum
body.explanation: The slide lists the mouth, stomach/small intestine/colon, anal region and lower rectum, and the liver and spleen partially. The oesophagus is not accessible to examination.
option_notes: Slide 8: oesophagus not accessible to examination.

title: A 24-year-old with Crohn's disease has small, painful, round ulcers inside the cheeks. What is this lesion?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 24-year-old with Crohn's disease has small, painful, round ulcers inside the cheeks. What is this lesion?
body.explanation: Aphthous ulcers of the oral mucosa are an oral sign seen in inflammatory bowel diseases.
option_notes: Painful round mucosal ulcers, seen for example in IBD.
Candidiasis gives a white plaque on the tongue.
Cheilitis affects the corners of the mouth.
Glossitis is an inflamed, smooth tongue.

title: Cholestatic jaundice without bile duct dilatation:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cholestatic jaundice without bile duct dilatation:
options: May be due to chronic liver disease
Is typically due to biliary lithiasis
body.explanation: No dilated ducts = intrahepatic cholestasis, e.g. chronic liver diseases.

title: What is lid lag?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is lid lag?
body.explanation: The upper lid lags behind the globe when the patient looks slowly down.
option_notes: Blinking frequency is not lid lag.
Double vision comes from extraocular muscle dysfunction.
The upper lid lags behind the globe when the patient looks slowly down.

title: In the physical examination of a vomiting patient, the cardiovascular examination looks for:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In the physical examination of a vomiting patient, the cardiovascular examination looks for:
options: Signs of heart failure if a cardiac cause is suspected
Papilledema and signs of raised intracranial pressure
body.explanation: Cardiovascular examination: any signs of heart failure if cardiac causes are suspected.

title: Liver palpation is performed:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Liver palpation is performed:
options: With a flat hand using the fingertips, or a hook
body.explanation: Liver palpation: under right ribs, flat hand with tip of fingers or hook, during deep breath.
option_notes: Left ribs are for the spleen.

title: Cardiovascular manifestations of hyperthyroidism include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cardiovascular manifestations of hyperthyroidism include:
options: A systolic murmur, mostly at the apex
body.explanation: Slide: persistent resting tachycardia with palpitations and sometimes exertional dyspnoea, loud ringing heart sounds, systolic murmur mostly at the apex, increased systolic BP.
option_notes: Correct: heart sounds are loud and ringing.
Correct: systolic murmur mostly at the apex.
Correct: palpitations and sometimes exertional dyspnoea.

title: What is the first-line investigation for dysphagia?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is the first-line investigation for dysphagia?
body.explanation: Allows biopsies to exclude malignancy.
option_notes: Endoscopy sees the mucosa and takes biopsies.

title: What is melena?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is melena?
body.explanation: Melena: black, tarry, foul stools of digested blood. Haematochezia: bright red rectal blood.
option_notes: Bright red rectal blood is haematochezia.
Black, tarry, foul-smelling stools of digested blood.

title: In acute diarrhoea, tests are indicated when it lasts over:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In acute diarrhoea, tests are indicated when it lasts over:
body.explanation: Or with dehydration, blood, fever, epidemic context, immunosuppression.

title: The semiological characteristics of vomiting to describe include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The semiological characteristics of vomiting to describe include:
options: Triggers and relieving factors such as diet or head position
body.explanation: Onset and duration, circumstances, frequency, content, volume, triggers and relieving factors.
option_notes: Wrong: not a characteristic of vomiting.

title: Solids first then liquids suggests?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Solids first then liquids suggests?
body.explanation: Solids then liquids: mechanical. Liquids more than solids (paradoxical): motor, as in achalasia.
option_notes: Achalasia affects liquids from the start.
A narrowing blocks solids first, then liquids as it worsens.

title: Which pairing of tendon reflexes with thyroid state is correct?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which pairing of tendon reflexes with thyroid state is correct?
options: Hyperthyroidism: brisk reflexes; hypothyroidism: delayed relaxation
Hyperthyroidism: delayed relaxation; hypothyroidism: brisk reflexes
Reflexes do not change in thyroid disease
body.explanation: Hyperthyroidism causes hyperkinesia and hyperreflexia. Hypothyroidism causes delayed relaxation of tendon reflexes (for example of the ankle jerk).
option_notes: Reflexes are not absent in either.

title: Cardiovascular complications of hypothyroidism include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cardiovascular complications of hypothyroidism include:
options: Myxoedema cardiomyopathy with congestive heart failure
Pericardial effusion that usually becomes large enough to cause tamponade
Coronary disease related to raised total and LDL cholesterol
body.explanation: Myxoedema cardiomyopathy causing CHF, myxoedema pericarditis (effusion rarely enough to cause tamponade), and coronary disease from high total/LDL cholesterol.
option_notes: Correct: CAD linked to high cholesterol and LDL.

title: The face of the child photographed in the Cushing section shows:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The face of the child photographed in the Cushing section shows:
options: A thin face with temporal wasting
body.explanation: The photo shows a round, full face with red cheeks, matching 'moon face' and 'red cheeks' on the labelled drawing.
option_notes: Wrong: mucosal pigmentation is a sign of primary adrenal insufficiency.
Wrong: the face is full, not wasted.

title: Choleriform diarrhoea is caused by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Choleriform diarrhoea is caused by:
options: Lactase deficiency with osmotic water retention
body.explanation: Cholera, enterotoxigenic E. coli.

title: The hypometabolism syndrome of hypothyroidism is described as:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hypometabolism syndrome of hypothyroidism is described as:
options: Asthenia that is physical, psychological, intellectual and sexual
Isolated proximal muscle weakness without any psychological or intellectual change
body.explanation: Hypometabolism affects the main vital functions: physical, psychological, intellectual and sexual asthenia.

title: The digital rectal examination assesses:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The digital rectal examination assesses:
body.explanation: Digital examination: anal canal, distal rectum, prostate.
option_notes: Caecum is in the right iliac region, not reachable.

title: Toxic adenoma is characterised by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Toxic adenoma is characterised by:
options: An isolated, painless nodule on palpation
Reduced or absent contralateral lobe function on scintigraphy
Diffuse homogeneous hyperfixation of the whole gland on scintigraphy
body.explanation: Toxic adenoma: thyrotoxicosis, no ocular signs, isolated painless nodule; scintigraphy shows a hot nodule with decreased/absent contralateral function.
option_notes: Wrong: toxic adenoma has no ocular signs.
Correct: contralateral lobe function reduced or absent.

title: The hydro-electrolytic complications of vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The hydro-electrolytic complications of vomiting include:
body.explanation: Complications: hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, metabolic alkalosis and dehydration.

title: A patient has a low FT4 with a TSH that is low or normal rather than high. What does this pattern suggest?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A patient has a low FT4 with a TSH that is low or normal rather than high. What does this pattern suggest?
body.explanation: In primary hypothyroidism the pituitary responds to low FT4 with a high TSH. If TSH fails to rise, the problem is the pituitary: secondary (central) hypothyroidism.
option_notes: The pituitary fails to raise TSH despite low FT4: a pituitary cause.
Hashimoto's is primary hypothyroidism with a high TSH.
Subclinical hypothyroidism has a high TSH with a normal FT4.
Iodine deficiency is a primary cause with a high TSH.

title: Metabolic and endocrine causes of chronic vomiting include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Metabolic and endocrine causes of chronic vomiting include:
body.explanation: Chronic metabolic/endocrine: chronic renal failure (uraemia), hyperthyroidism, Addison's disease. DKA is an acute cause.

title: The ophthalmological examination of a diabetic includes:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The ophthalmological examination of a diabetic includes:
options: Visual acuity with and without optical correction
Examination of the iris and lens for rubeosis iridis and cataract
Examination of the vitreous and fundus after pupillary dilation
body.explanation: All four components are listed on the retinopathy examination slide.

title: In a patient with GI bleeding, the rectal examination is used to:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: In a patient with GI bleeding, the rectal examination is used to:
options: Look for haemorrhoids, fissure or a rectal mass
body.explanation: The rectal exam confirms melena or haematochezia and checks for haemorrhoids, fissure or a rectal mass.
option_notes: It shows the colour of the stool on the glove.

title: Which shunt direction occurs in septal defects initially?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which shunt direction occurs in septal defects initially?
body.explanation: Blood flows from the high-pressure left side to the low-pressure right side through atrial or ventricular septal defects, overloading the right heart.
option_notes: High left pressure pushes blood to the right side.

title: Mallory-Weiss syndrome:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Mallory-Weiss syndrome:
options: Is a mucosal tear at the junction of the stomach and oesophagus
Is a life-threatening rupture with leakage into the mediastinum
body.explanation: Mallory-Weiss: forceful vomiting tears the mucosa at the gastro-oesophageal junction, leading to bleeding. Leakage into the mediastinum is Boerhaave syndrome.

title: Regarding the left supraclavicular lymph node:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Regarding the left supraclavicular lymph node:
options: It is a key node in the cervical examination
It may reveal metastasis of digestive cancers
It is examined during the proctological exam
It is a sign of portal hypertension
body.explanation: Left supraclavicular ++ (metastasis of digestive cancers).
option_notes: It belongs to the cervical exam.

title: Gastroparesis is often associated with:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Gastroparesis is often associated with:
body.explanation: Gastroparesis: often associated with diabetes.
option_notes: Wrong: not linked to gastroparesis on the slide.
Wrong: migraine is a neurological cause.

title: What is hepatomegaly?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is hepatomegaly?
body.explanation: Enlargement of the whole liver or part of it; diagnosis is clinical.
option_notes: Hepatomegaly simply means an enlarged liver, whole or in part.
Hepatitis is one possible cause, not the definition.
A tumour is one possible cause, not the definition.

title: What is heart failure?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What is heart failure?
body.explanation: The heart muscle does not pump blood as well as it should; blood backs up and fluid builds in the lungs.
option_notes: The heart pumps less well than it should.
A stopped heart is cardiac arrest.
Valve calcification is a possible cause, not the definition.
Fluid in the pericardium is an effusion.

title: Vomiting with headache, photophobia and fever should make you think of:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Vomiting with headache, photophobia and fever should make you think of:
body.explanation: Headache and photophobia form a meningeal syndrome; meningitis is a neurological cause of acute vomiting.
option_notes: Correct: headache and photophobia form a meningeal syndrome.
Wrong: does not explain headache, photophobia and fever.
Wrong: does not explain the neurological signs.
Wrong: gives late postprandial vomiting, not meningeal signs.

title: Per the synthesis slide:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Per the synthesis slide:
options: Adrenal cortex hypersecretion includes Cushing and hyperaldosteronism
Primary adrenal insufficiency comes with hyperpigmentation
Hyperaldosteronism is linked to an aldosterone-secreting adenoma
Phaeochromocytoma is a form of cortex insufficiency
body.explanation: Synthesis: cortex hypersecretion (Cushing, hyperaldosteronism); cortex insufficiency, primary (with hyperpigmentation) or secondary; hyperaldosteronism - aldosterone-secreting adenoma; phaeochromocytoma.
option_notes: Wrong: phaeochromocytoma is a medullary catecholamine tumour.

title: A 60-year-old has painless, progressive jaundice with itching, dark urine and pale stools. Conjugated bilirubin, GGT and ALP are raised. Which test comes first…
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A 60-year-old has painless, progressive jaundice with itching, dark urine and pale stools. Conjugated bilirubin, GGT and ALP are raised. Which test comes first to find the cause?
options: Abdominal ultrasound looking for dilated bile ducts
body.explanation: This is cholestatic jaundice. The strategy then asks whether there is a biliary obstruction: abdominal ultrasound looks for dilated bile ducts.
option_notes: Dilated ducts mean an extrahepatic (obstructive) cause.
Haemolysis is the question for non-cholestatic (unconjugated) jaundice.
Biopsy is not a first step.
Gilbert gives unconjugated bilirubin without cholestasis.

title: Graves' ophthalmopathy:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Graves' ophthalmopathy:
options: Involves inflammation of orbital muscles, periocular tissue and retro-orbital fat
Can cause diplopia and scleral injection
Can reduce visual acuity through optic neuropathy
Is a typical feature of toxic adenoma, accompanying its isolated and painless nodule
body.explanation: Ophthalmopathy is inflammatory involvement of orbital muscles (myositis), periocular tissues and retro-orbital fat: lid retraction, exophthalmos, chemosis, scleral injection, diplopia, optic neuropathy. Toxic adenoma has no ocular signs.
option_notes: Correct: myositis, periocular tissue and retro-orbital fat.
Correct: diplopia and scleral injection are listed.
Correct: decreased visual acuity = optic neuropathy.
Wrong: toxic adenoma has no ocular signs.

title: Causes of hypopituitarism illustrated on the cartoon slide include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of hypopituitarism illustrated on the cartoon slide include:
body.explanation: The cartoon shows three causes: adenoma, infarct and 'empty sella'.
option_notes: Not shown; pregnancy is a physiological cause of high prolactin.

title: Causes of Cushing's syndrome given in the lecture:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Causes of Cushing's syndrome given in the lecture:
options: A paraganglioma of the bladder wall
body.explanation: Slide 33 (Etiologies): ACTH-independent Cushing is of adrenal origin with low, undetectable ACTH (adenomas, carcinomas, adrenal hyperplasia). ACTH-dependent Cushing has normal or high ACTH, from a pituitary adenoma (corticotropic cells secreting ACTH) or ectopic ACTH/CRH secretion (small-cell lung carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumours). Slides 34-35 show a pituitary adenoma on MRI and a resected adrenal adenoma.
option_notes: Wrong: adrenal tuberculosis causes adrenal insufficiency.

title: At what angle is the patient placed to assess the JVP?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: At what angle is the patient placed to assess the JVP?
body.explanation: Supine with the head raised 15 to 45 degrees, head turned left.
option_notes: Flat fills the veins too much.
15 to 45 degrees shows the top of the venous column.

title: Features of the acromegalic face include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Features of the acromegalic face include:
body.explanation: Acromegalic facies: prominent supraorbital ridges, frontal bossing, nose enlargement, prognathism, dental problems, coarse features, deep nasolabial furrows, macroglossia and large lips.
option_notes: Wrong: the mandible grows downward and forward (prognathism).

title: On auscultation of a constipated patient, hyperactive bowel sounds could suggest:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On auscultation of a constipated patient, hyperactive bowel sounds could suggest:
body.explanation: Absent bowel sounds could suggest an ileus; hyperactive sounds could suggest an obstruction.
option_notes: Wrong: fecal loading is suggested by dullness on percussion.
Wrong: it is a pathological finding here.

title: Painful HMG with hepatojugular reflux suggests?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Painful HMG with hepatojugular reflux suggests?
body.explanation: A painful liver with hepatojugular reflux points to cardiac congestion.
option_notes: Hepatojugular reflux shows right heart congestion of the liver.
Metastases do not cause hepatojugular reflux.
An abscess causes fever and pain but no reflux.

title: Aspiration pneumonia after vomiting:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Aspiration pneumonia after vomiting:
options: Results from inhaling stomach contents into the lungs
Causes fever, cough and difficulty breathing
Is classed as a mechanical complication
Is classed as an infectious complication
body.explanation: Aspiration pneumonia, an infectious complication: inhalation of stomach contents into the lungs, causing fever, cough and difficulty breathing.
option_notes: Wrong: mechanical complications are the oesophageal tears.

title: Feculent vomiting (faecal odour) strongly suggests:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Feculent vomiting (faecal odour) strongly suggests:
body.explanation: Faecal odour or feculent vomit strongly suggests severe bowel obstruction; it is also an alarm sign.
option_notes: Wrong: not linked to the content.

title: Abdominal auscultation assesses:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Abdominal auscultation assesses:
options: Abnormal sounds such as in aortic aneurysm
body.explanation: Auscultation: bowel movement sounds, arteries (normal beats, abnormal sounds e.g. aortic aneurysm).

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Extra-digestive forms. ENT, respiratory and non-cardiac chest pain.
option_notes: Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.
ENT, respiratory and non-cardiac chest pain forms.
Another box of the diagram, not the one at the arrow.

title: Signs of hypermetabolism in phaeochromocytoma include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Signs of hypermetabolism in phaeochromocytoma include:
body.explanation: Signs of hypermetabolism: weight loss, fever, thermophobia, glucose intolerance or even diabetes.

title: What skin sign is typical of Cushing's syndrome?
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: What skin sign is typical of Cushing's syndrome?
body.explanation: Wide purple striae, with acne.
option_notes: White, thin striae are common in simple weight gain.
Wide purple striae (over 1 cm) are typical.
Vitiligo is a depigmentation, not a Cushing sign.

title: Signs of autonomic neuropathy sought on the feet during neuropathy assessment include:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Signs of autonomic neuropathy sought on the feet during neuropathy assessment include:
body.explanation: Autonomic neuropathy signs++: skin dryness, hyperkeratosis, loss of sweating.
option_notes: Loss of pulses is a sign of PAD.

title: A diabetes found on a routine blood test in a patient without symptoms corresponds to the diagnostic circumstance:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: A diabetes found on a routine blood test in a patient without symptoms corresponds to the diagnostic circumstance:
body.explanation: Diagnosis circumstances: accidental diagnosis, hyperglycaemia symptoms, or acute/chronic complications.

title: Cholestatic jaundice corresponds to raised:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Cholestatic jaundice corresponds to raised:
body.explanation: Strategy: cholestatic jaundice (conjugated bilirubin) vs non-cholestatic (unconjugated).

title: On the aldosterone regulation diagram, renin secretion is inhibited by:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: On the aldosterone regulation diagram, renin secretion is inhibited by:
body.explanation: Renin is stimulated by low renal arterial pressure, beta-adrenergic action and prostaglandins, and inhibited by ANP and dopamine.
option_notes: Wrong: low renal arterial pressure stimulates renin.

title: Before examining a patient, the doctor should:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: Before examining a patient, the doctor should:
options: Explain the examination and take consent
Check the temperature of the room
Ask the patient to sit upright on a chair
body.explanation: Before examination: check identity, explain and take consent, intimate calm environment, check room temperature, patient lying flat, doctor on the right side.
option_notes: The patient lies flat on a bed.

title: The association of haematemesis with melena or rectal bleeding indicates:
subject: subj:semio

body.stem: The association of haematemesis with melena or rectal bleeding indicates:
body.explanation: Per the severity slide: haematemesis + melena or rectal bleeding = abundant bleeding.
option_notes: Wrong: haematemesis implies an upper source.
